title: feat(external): VTA external accounts — management, credential issuance and Sui signing
body:
Adds the `external/*` family: a VTA holds identities at clouds and third-party services, and lets bound integrations use them only through short-lived, downscoped credentials or protocol-defined signatures. Design: [`vta-external-accounts.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/docs/05-design-notes/vta-external-accounts.md) in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

- **Management:** `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,secret/set,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,setup,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore,delete}/0.1`. Changing an account is recommended to need consent, with approvers signing with their own DIDs. Suspend and revoke never need it.
- **Use:** `external/credentials/issue/0.1`. The custodian does the exchange and downscopes the result itself, and the response is a `sealed_transfer` bundle.
- **Signing:** `external/sign/0.1`, for `sui-signer` only. It signs only allow-listed Move calls, under gas and amount caps, and the custodian builds the digest.
- **Models:**
  - `aws-roles-anywhere`
  - `gcp-wif-pinned`
  - `azure-cert`
  - `oauth2-private-key-jwt`
  - `s3-static-presign`
  - `sui-signer`
  - `static-secret`, which is never released

  None of them needs the custodian to be reachable inbound. Plain OIDC discovery federation is excluded, and `_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md` says why.

Unverified, and written as options:
- whether GCP accepts ES256 (`signingAlgorithm`);
- whether a Roles Anywhere session accepts a per-request session policy (the `chainedRoleArn` fallback);
- the exact Sui secp256r1 digest; conformance requires Sui's reference verifier to accept the signature.

Bindings are regenerated for all four languages. `validate`, `check-bindings` and the Rust conformance tests pass.

title: Specify trigger links: the QR code or link that starts an exchange with a wallet (VTI-LNK-001 – 116)
body:
## Summary

Adds a chapter, **Trigger Links** (`spec/07a-links.md`, area `LNK`, profile `Links`), for the text an inviter shows as a QR code or a link so that whichever wallet a person uses can start an exchange with it. Two flows are registered: `sign-in`, a member signing in to a community portal by scanning the code it shows, and `vta-claim`, a wallet claiming a VTA from a VTA Farm.

```
https://link.trustoverip.org/t#_from=<VID>&_id=<handle>&_exp=<epoch>&_type=/vti/flow/sign-in/0.1
```

## What the chapter specifies

- **The link.** An `https` URL. Every field a reader uses is in the fragment, which no server receives. Readers ignore unknown names, so appended tracking parameters don't break a link. A repeated reserved name is refused.
- **Reading.** One reading order with named reasons, and five outcomes a person sees (`update`, `expired`, `unreachable`, `pass-on`, `invalid`). The reader never says which field failed.
- **Fields.**
  - `_from` is any VID.
  - `_id` is 16–32 random bytes as unpadded base64url, with one spelling per handle.
  - `_exp` is epoch seconds, with a 60 s clock allowance.
  - `_type` is a versioned flow URI. It may be written as a path that resolves against `https` and the link's lowercased host.
- **Flows.** A registry under `https://link.trustoverip.org/vti/flow/`, governed by this specification, with MAJOR/MINOR version rules.
- **After the link.**
  - Show the contact as unverified before any network activity. There's an exception for contacts already in the reader's records.
  - Verify the DID document, and take the transport only from it.
  - Sign the first request with a fresh identifier, and carry the handle as `parentThreadId`.
- **Security of the handle.** It confers nothing, no GET spends it, and readers never log it.
- **Producers.**
  - Emit ASCII only.
  - Keep the `https` form within 251 bytes at QR level M, or 177 at level Q (version 11).
  - Serve pages showing a link with `no-referrer` and `no-store`, with no third-party scripts.
  - Give redirects an explicit fragment.
  - Never put the link host on the page's own domain.
- **Link host.** Association files claim only the trigger path. A no-wallet page never reads the fragment.
- **`sign-in`.**
  - `_exp` is required, at most 300 s.
  - A reader acts only for a community already in its records, and offers to join otherwise.
  - The contact's document must list the portal's service.
  - The VTC uses a 16-byte handle.
  - Includes a size-budget note.
- **`vta-claim`** (VTI-LNK-110 – 116, added after review by the VTA Farm).
  - The contact is the Farm, not the VTA. `_exp` is required, at most 300 s.
  - The Farm is a first contact, so nothing is resolved before the person continues.
  - The fresh identifier that issues the first request becomes the VTA's administrator.
  - The Farm accepts one claim per handle.
  - A claim check (SHOULD) catches a bystander who scans first: the page and the wallet both show 6 characters derived from the claimed identifier, and the person confirms they match.
- **Clicking the code** (VTI-LNK-056, 086, 105): a page SHOULD make its QR code a link to the same text, so a wallet on the same device can be used without scanning. A reader that sees the click, such as a browser extension, records the page's origin. For `sign-in` that origin MUST match the portal origin in the verified document (`wrong-origin`), which stops a page relaying a genuine portal code. This replaces the browser plugin's SIOPv2 login.
- **Path DIDs** (VTI-LNK-050): before the person continues, the reader shows the path as well as the domain.

Wiring: `specs.json`, the intro's structure and reading tables, `STRUCTURE.md`, the conformance area, profile and target tables, references, and one glossary term (`trigger link`). `Links` is MAY for every target. VTI-LNK-001 binds any target that reads, produces or hosts trigger links.

## Not in this revision

- **Agent names** in `_from` are reserved (VTI-LNK-032). Readers refuse them with `update` until three things are settled with the agent-names authors: their canonical form, what a community name resolves to, and the redirect contract.
- **The sign-in exchange after the first request** (its Trust Tasks, and whether the first claim locks the request) is being specified separately. VTI-LNK-050 – 054 already fix its order: show the community from the reader's records, the member continues, then the first signed request.
- **Adding a device with `vta-claim`:** who sees the code, which role the new identifier gets, and whether the claim check is then required are open with the Farm.
- **Farm login** will reuse `sign-in` over `auth/oob`, replacing SIOPv2, which becomes legacy for a deprecation window. That needs VTI-LNK-101 and 104 widened from "community" to "a party the wallet already has a relationship with", pending the sign-in authors.

## Open dependencies outside this PR

- Trust Over IP hosting `link.trustoverip.org`.
- Device tests of fragment survival across camera, browser and OS hand-offs (Keyring). If a platform drops the fragment, the link form needs another answer there.
- How the VTA signs the sign-in approval documents. `vault/sign-trust-task` picks the proof purpose from the document type (VTI-KEY-106), so these documents are signed for `authentication`. The sign-in design expects `assertionMethod`. To be settled with the sign-in protocol.

## Origin

Agreed between Affinidi and the Keyring authors from [keyring-wallet PR #354](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/pull/354). That PR's spec and annex will refer to this chapter, and its trigger and transport-selection vectors will be updated to this wording as the conformance vectors. The informative examples at the end of the chapter cover the cases settled in that exchange.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no errors.

title: perf(audit): cache the active audit key per keyspace, failing closed
body:
**Stacked on #2003** (`perf/vsock-atomic-opcodes` @ 1623c372, itself on #1999). Retarget to `main` once those merge.

## What and why

Every audited operation read the active audit key from storage twice — the `audit_key:active` marker, then the key it names. #1951 (Carlos Rincon) measured removing both at roughly +13–25% `keys/sign` throughput in a Nitro Enclave. This caches it without missing a rotation through another instance, without weakening VTI-APV-022, and without the cancelled-write gap.

## Design

**Per-keyspace write tracking in the store** (`vti-common/src/store/generation.rs`), shared by every handle for a keyspace name:
- **Begin** (before the request leaves): bump the generation, count the write in flight.
- **End** (completed, failed or dropped): bump again, uncount.
- **Unknown only when the frame may have reached the parent.** The pool reports it: `round_trip_within` (under the pool's 10 s per-round-trip deadline) sets the caller's `ever_sent` flag at the same moment as its own per-attempt `sent`, once the whole frame has been written (`request_tracked`, `request_once_tracked`) — so it also survives the caller's future being dropped, where no error can say so. A write that ends with no reply **after** that — transport failure, a deadline that expired after sending, or its future dropped — marks the keyspace *unknown*. A write that ends **before** it (connect error, pool closed, write error, a deadline that expired before the frame was fully written, cancelled before sending) cannot have been applied — the proxy acts only on a whole frame — so it is a known outcome and marks nothing.
- **The unknown mark clears** when a write that *began after it* completes, **or after `UNKNOWN_SETTLE` = 30 s**: longer than any plausible late apply of an abandoned frame (the parent applies a frame as soon as it reads it; the frame is already in its buffer when the enclave gives up, and the pool drops that connection; a parent stalled past 30 s would be failing every storage call). Without it, one timed-out write on `audit_key` — written once in weeks — would switch the cache off until the next rotation.
- **Readers** take a ticket before reading: none while a write is in flight or unknown; a fresh read is cached only if its ticket is still current afterwards.

**Vsock — both pool paths tracked:** `send` → `request_tracked` (plain insert/delete, every single-op fallback, the restore's plain insert) and `send_atomic` → `request_once_tracked` (`OP_TAKE`, `OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT`, `OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT`, `OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL`, the restore's insert-if-absent). In `send`, anything that is not a known read-only opcode is a write.

**Local:** each write's guard runs inside the blocking closure that performs it, so its outcome is always known (a panic excepted → unknown).

**`AuditKeyStore::active` / `try_active`** serve the cached key only under a current ticket and while younger than **`MAX_CACHE_AGE` = 30 s** (belt and braces: bounds anything unforeseen to 30 s of hashing under the previous key, which stays retained and verifiable). The value is per instance; only the tracking is per keyspace.

## Gaps closed
- **Late-applied abandoned write:** a rotation's marker write held by the parent, its writer times out, the parent then applies it → the next read sees the new key. Verified the test fails without the unknown mark.
- **One failed write disabling the cache for weeks:** a pre-send failure (including a pre-send deadline) marks nothing; an after-send unknown settles after 30 s. Verified the pre-send tests fail if every unreplied write is treated as unknown.

## VTI-APV-022
`vti_apv_022_a_waiver_that_cannot_be_audited_is_refused` deletes the marker through `state.audit_key_ks` and passes **unchanged**.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib`: **735 passed**.
- Vsock, both proxy generations, through a different handle than the cache's: one test per write path (insert, insert_raw, remove, insert_if_absent, insert_raw_if_absent, take_raw, swap, move_if_unchanged); an absent take retires the cache iff it sent `OP_TAKE`; the restore after an undecryptable take is two tracked writes (generation +4); late-applied rotation never served stale; in-flight write suppresses caching; a write that never left (plain and atomic path) does not disable caching; an after-send unknown disables it until it settles; **a deadline expiring after the frame was sent disables caching, and one expiring before it does not (both pool paths)**.
- Local: rotation via another instance seen; deleted marker fails closed; a hit reads nothing and any write ends it; failed read not remembered; max age forces a re-read; local in-flight write suppresses caching. `store::generation::tests`: the state machine, including pre-send failure and settle.
- `nextest -p vti-common -p vta-audit`: 700 passed. APV-022 test: passed. (Earlier on this branch: `vta-service` audit 31 passed; `vtc-service` audit / APV-022 / single-admin / syncer / tail 150 passed.)
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common --all-targets -D warnings`: default, `--all-features`, `vsock-store,encryption`. `cargo fmt --check`.

## Backport
none

title: perf(vta-service): multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed
body:
Part C of the plan for #1951 (TEE `keys/sign` throughput). **Stacked on #1999**, which makes the enclave store's multi-step operations atomic — the precondition for running REST handlers in parallel in the enclave.

## Kept from #1951 (Carlos Rincon, cherry-picked with `-x`)
- **REST on one worker per CPU** (current-thread on one CPU). #1951 measured this plus direct vsock taking a 2-vCPU enclave from ~287 to ~345 keys/sign/s and a 4-vCPU enclave to ~380–400.
- **REST served on vsock directly**, removing the in-enclave inbound `socat` (a fork per connection; connect timeouts under load).

## Changed
- **Fail closed.** `VTA_REST_VSOCK_PORT` is read once at boot, before anything binds. A value that is not a vsock port, or any value in a build without `vsock-store`, **refuses the boot**, naming the value. #1951 silently fell back to a TCP port nothing forwards to in an enclave.
- **No TCP port** in vsock mode at all.
- **Bound once, like TCP.** The vsock listener is bound once at boot and each REST generation gets a `try_clone()` of the same socket. `/vta/restart` does not join the old REST thread, so rebinding per generation could race it for the port (EADDRINUSE → process exit).
- **Adoption never panics.** Each generation wraps its clone in `AsyncFd` itself (`set_nonblocking` + `AsyncFd::new`, both fallible) rather than tokio-vsock's `FromRawFd`, which unwraps; the REST runtime build is fallible too. A real OS error (EMFILE, a runtime shutting down) reaches the boot. No `unsafe`.
- **A failed restart shuts down cleanly.** If a soft restart's REST generation cannot adopt its listener, the iteration signals shutdown, cancels messaging, joins the REST thread and persists the store before returning the error.
- **No accept-error flood.** Accept failures back off 10 ms → 1 s (reset on success), warn on the first failure and then at most one summary per 10 s.
- **Only the parent.** The listener accepts `vti_common::store::vsock::PARENT_CID` only (one public constant; others dropped, logged `security_alert`) and reports it as `vti_common::rate_limit::VSOCK_PARENT_PEER` = `0.0.0.3` — never a valid TCP source, so no TCP peer and nothing inside the enclave can present it.
- **No HEALTHCHECK in `Dockerfile.nitro`.** It polled `localhost:8100`, which no longer exists. The image runs only as an enclave, where Docker never executes a HEALTHCHECK, and a process-alive probe would never go false; health is checked from the parent through `enclave-proxy` (the load balancer's target check).

## `trust_xff_cidrs`

| Entry | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `0.0.0.3/32` | the enclave VTA | believe `X-Forwarded-For` from the parent's `enclave-proxy`, nothing else |
| `127.0.0.1/32` | the parent's `enclave-proxy` (`trusted_upstream_cidrs`) | a TLS terminator on the parent's loopback, as before |

The shipped Nitro configs list both. In vsock mode the VTA trusts exactly what it is told, with one rule:

- **A trusted `127.0.0.1` also trusts the parent.** On vsock the VTA binds no TCP, so a trusted `127.0.0.1` can only ever have meant the socat hop from the parent. Logged once at info, with how to make it explicit.
- A non-empty list naming neither address reads no header and is **warned** at boot.
- An empty list trusts nothing and is not warned — how a byte-bridging parent must be configured.
- TCP mode is unchanged.

This is safe because a non-empty list implies the Rust `enclave-proxy`, which sets `X-Forwarded-For` itself: `parent-proxy.sh` (a byte bridge) refuses to start whenever `trust_xff_cidrs` is set. Trusting the parent unconditionally was rejected for that reason.

### Operator migration
**No action needed.** A config that still says `trust_xff_cidrs = ["127.0.0.1/32"]` keeps per-client rate limiting after the upgrade: the VTA reads it as the parent and logs once how to make that explicit (add `"0.0.0.3/32"`). Configs with an empty list are unaffected.

## Security, against `main`
- **Before:** the trusted-proxy address was `127.0.0.1` — the parent's traffic via socat, *or any process inside the enclave*.
- **After:** only the parent instance can be the VTA's trusted proxy (CID check, an address TCP cannot carry). The parent proxy's own trust is unchanged.
- Misconfiguration refuses the boot instead of producing an unreachable API. A soft restart cannot take the process down. A listener failure is reported, not panicked.

## ⚠️ New PCR0
The entrypoint and Dockerfile are part of the enclave image. Operators pinning `--expect-pcr0` must re-measure.

## Tests
- `server::rest_ingress_tests` (11 with `vsock-store`, 3 without):
  - port parsing fails closed, naming the value;
  - legacy `127.0.0.1` list → parent trusted (end to end through the key extractor);
  - explicit `0.0.0.3` → trusted, no note or warning;
  - empty list → nothing trusted, no warning;
  - a list naming neither → warned, not widened;
  - TCP mode unchanged;
  - backoff 10 → 20 → … → 1000 ms cap, reset on success;
  - failures reported first, then at most every 10 s, and a new outage reported at once;
  - restart generations share one bound listener.
- `vti_common::rate_limit` (23), `auth::session::tests::concurrent_claims_of_one_refresh_token_admit_exactly_one` (16 × 20 rounds, multi-thread runtime → exactly one each).
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -E 'test(rate_limit)|test(refresh)|test(rest_ingress)|test(auth)'` → 167 passed. `cargo nextest run -p vti-common --features rate-limit,vsock-store,encryption -E 'test(rate_limit)|test(auth::)|test(store::)'` → 278 passed.
- Clippy `-D warnings` clean: `vta-service` default and `--no-default-features --features rest,didcomm,vsock-store`; `vti-common --features rate-limit,vsock-store,encryption`. `cargo fmt --check` clean. `cargo check -p vta-enclave --no-default-features --features rest,didcomm,vsock-store` clean. `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy` `cargo test --release --locked` → 39 passed (comment-only change there).
- `hadolint` is not installed locally, so the Dockerfile change (a removed `HEALTHCHECK`, replaced by a comment) is unlinted.

## Follow-ups
- `vta-enclave/src/vsock_log.rs` still has a private `PARENT_CID`; switch it to `vti_common::store::vsock::PARENT_CID` once the logging PR (which edits that file) lands.
- Pre-existing, not from this PR: the wrapping-key reaper (`wrapping_cache.spawn_reaper()`) is spawned per restart iteration and never stopped.

## Only an appliance can confirm
- Throughput and connect-timeout figures (rerun #1951's load test).
- The parent's CID is 3 as seen from inside the enclave (Nitro docs; same constant as the storage client).
- Boot with the real entrypoint: REST reachable on vsock:5100, nothing on TCP 8100; `/vta/restart` keeps serving.

## Backport
none

title: perf(storage): atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move in the parent proxy
body:
Part E1 of the plan for #1951 (TEE `keys/sign` throughput). **Stacked on #1999** (enclave-side per-key locks; rebased onto its round-trip deadline, `4847c198`); merge that first.

## Design
The parent's storage proxy now serves the enclave store's claims and moves as single operations, advertised by a capability probe:

| Opcode | Replaces | Round trips (old → new) |
|---|---|---|
| `OP_TAKE` (get + delete) — `take_raw`, the refresh-token claim | GET, DELETE | 2 → 1 |
| `OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT` — `insert_if_absent`, `insert_raw_if_absent` | GET, INSERT | 2 → 1 |
| `OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT` — `swap` | GET, INSERT, DELETE | 3 → 1 |
| `OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL` — `move_if_unchanged` | GET, GET, INSERT, DELETE | 4 → 2 |
| `OP_HELLO` | — | once per connect |

- **Parent:** each op runs under a per-keyspace `std::sync::Mutex` held across its fjall steps. It's a mutex, not fjall's transactional database: the critical sections are a few fjall calls with no `await`, and switching the database type would touch every operation. Plain get/insert/delete don't take it, matching the local store.
- **Off the workers:** each op's critical section (the lock plus the fjall calls under it) runs in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. Contended ops on one keyspace (every refresh-token claim) therefore wait on the blocking pool instead of tying up runtime workers and starving plain reads on other connections. The std mutex stays: nothing under it awaits. A dropped connection never cancels a section midway.
- **Crash-atomic moves:** swap-if-absent and move-if-equal commit their insert and delete as **one fjall write batch** (one journal record, one seqno), so a parent crash never leaves the moved-from row live beside its replacement.
- **Reply frames** up to 64 KiB go out in one write (#1951 follow-up); larger ones are written as header then payload, not copied (the enclave client's rule).
- **Never resent once possibly applied:** the enclave pool has `request` (idempotent: get/insert/delete/scans/HELLO, resent once as before) and `request_once` (the atomic ops).
  - A `request_once` is resent only if its frame was not completely written; the proxy reads a whole frame before acting.
  - The 10 s round-trip deadline from #1999 follows the same rule: expiry after the frame was fully written is outcome-unknown, and expiry before is a not-sent retry.
  - After that, any failure is `OutcomeUnknown`: returned as an error, never resent, and **no single-op fallback**, since either could apply it twice (a resent take would refuse a legitimate refresh; a resent move would report `TargetExists` for a move that happened).
  - Idle connections are checked before use with one non-blocking read poll (no-op waker). An idle connection owes nothing, so `Pending` means live; EOF, an error or stray bytes discard it before any write. A parent that closed an idle connection therefore doesn't produce an outcome-unknown error; a close that lands after the check is reported as unknown, the safe direction.
  - `OnceError` is the typed form inside the crate. Callers see `AppError::Internal("…outcome unknown…")`, because adding an `AppError` variant would be a breaking change.
- **Enclave:** the per-key locks from #1999 are still held around every operation. That gives defence in depth, and the same exactly-one guarantee on the single-op fallback.

## The parent never needs plaintext
Values are AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to (keyspace, key). Take, insert-if-absent and swap move opaque bytes. For compare-and-move, the **enclave** reads the row, decrypts it and compares plaintext; it then asks the proxy to move only while the row still holds *the exact ciphertext it just read*. The test `the_parent_never_sees_plaintext` asserts no plaintext reaches the parent in either mode.

## Compatibility: either side may be upgraded first
- **New enclave, old proxy:** `HELLO` gets "unknown opcode", so capabilities are 0 and the enclave uses today's single operations.
- **Any other error to `HELLO` fails the probe, and the connect.** HELLO reads no storage and takes no input, so a proxy that refuses it is broken or not the proxy expected; guessing "none" would hide that on the slow path.
- **Old enclave, new proxy:** the enclave never sends the new opcodes.
- **Proxy downgraded mid-run:** the next atomic op gets "unknown opcode"; nothing was applied, so it falls back and succeeds.
- **Re-probe:** with no capabilities known, the next operation after 60 s asks again (one caller does), so a proxy upgraded again, or one that was old at boot, is used atomically without an enclave restart.
- `deploy/nitro/README.md` documents this.

## Tests
- **Proxy** (`cargo test --release --locked`, 53 passed): each op and its outcomes; 64-wide concurrency on a 4-worker runtime with exactly one winner for take / insert-if-absent / swap / move; truncated and over-long fields return errors rather than panicking. Every move commits exactly one write batch and a refused move commits none. A small frame is one write; a large one is two, with the payload not copied; a 192 KiB frame round-trips. Contention: with two workers and two contended ops holding / waiting for a 300 ms critical section, a GET on another keyspace answers within 100 ms. With the lock taken on the worker (the old placement), the same test fails at about 310 ms; five reruns of the new code pass. `cargo clippy --release --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean; fmt clean.
- **Enclave** (`cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::`, 144 passed):
  - every exactly-one test runs 32-wide against **both** proxy generations;
  - `atomic_opcodes_cut_round_trips` counts requests: old `[2,2,3,4]` vs new `[1,1,1,2]`;
  - an older proxy probes as no capabilities;
  - a mid-run downgrade falls back without failing;
  - every `move_if_unchanged` outcome matches in both modes;
  - no plaintext reaches the parent;
  - an `OP_TAKE` or `OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT` that was applied and then hung up on returns an error: one frame, no resend, no fallback, state applied once;
  - pool: an atomic request is not resent after its frame was received, while an idempotent one is; a write failure before sending is retried and applied once; a stale idle connection is discarded without error;
  - pool deadline: an atomic request whose reply never comes times out as outcome-unknown (one frame, no resend, connection dropped); one whose write never completes times out and goes out once on a new connection;
  - `HELLO` refused otherwise fails the probe; a downgraded-then-upgraded proxy is re-probed and used again; there's no re-probe before it's due.
- Also passes with `vsock-store` alone (55 vsock tests). Clippy is clean with `vsock-store,encryption`, `vsock-store` alone and default features; fmt clean.

## Risks
- **Resolved: an undecryptable `OP_TAKE` no longer destroys the row** (`bae14a1d`).
  - **The problem:** `OP_TAKE` deletes in the parent before the enclave decrypts. Before this fix, a value that failed to decrypt or authenticate was gone once the error came back, so a storage-key misconfiguration would have wiped every row a claim touched.
  - **The fix:** the enclave re-inserts the exact bytes it received at the same key, while still holding the key's lock, and then returns the original decrypt error. The restore uses `OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT` where the proxy serves it, so a legitimate value written meanwhile is never overwritten; otherwise `OP_INSERT`. If the restore itself fails, it's logged at `error` with `security_alert = true`, and the decrypt error is still returned.
  - **Tests:** with the wrong key, the row is still present and byte-identical in both proxy generations, and the right key then claims it once. With encryption on, a successful take is still one round trip; the restore path is two.
- The proxy is a separate binary, so the parent and the enclave image can roll out in either order (see Compatibility above).

Credit: #1951 (Carlos Rincon) measured the round trips this removes and proposed the one-write reply.

title: feat(rooms): files in data rooms, and VTC room storage administration
body:
Adds Trust Tasks for files in data rooms, and for the hosting community's administration of room storage. Design: [`data-rooms-files.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md) in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

## Room tasks (authorized by the room's own chain, never host ACLs)
- `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.1`: chunked, resumable upload of a file's ciphertext. The manifest is committed before any byte moves, and every limit is checked and reserved at `begin`.
- `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}/0.1`: download of a file's ciphertext.
- `rooms/records/put/0.2`: a record can name a committed blob (`blobs`). This is a new version rather than an edit, because a 0.1 host would accept a record pointing at a blob it never checked.
- `rooms/info/0.1`: the room's limits and usage, plus the caller's own.
- `rooms/usage/0.1`: per-member usage, for the room's owner. Not offered on `private` rooms.
- `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`: the member's VTA releases the key for one file. The spec explains why this releases a key when `rooms/keys/open` deliberately does not.

## VTC-only tasks, under a new `vtc.rooms.admin` capability
- `vtc/rooms/{get,limits/set,usage}/0.1`
- `vtc/rooms/storage/{assign,migrate}/0.1`
- `vtc/storage/configs/{list,get,create,update,retire,probe}/0.1`
- `vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.1`: the discouraged fallback for a sealed credential. It is write-only; only a fingerprint comes back.

Storage changes park in the administrator action list.

## Shared types
- `rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json`:
  - `BlobRef`, `BlobManifest`, `TransferId`;
  - the limits and usage types: `ScopeLimits`, `RoomLimits`, `Usage`, `LimitExceeded`;
  - `FileManifest`, the sealed body's `file` member, which carries the KDF and STREAM construction.
- `vtc/_shared/0.1/room-storage.schema.json`

Bindings for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart are regenerated. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` passes.

title: fix(vti-common): pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations
body:
Part A of the plan for #1951 (TEE `keys/sign` throughput), reworked so the VTA's security improves rather than regresses.

## Kept from #1951 (Carlos Rincon, cherry-picked with `-x`)
- **Connection pool** for the enclave's vsock storage (up to 8), including the fix for a cancelled request leaving its response for the next caller.
- **One write per request frame.**

## Added
- **Atomic multi-step operations in the enclave store.** `take_raw` (the refresh-token claim), `insert_if_absent`, `insert_raw_if_absent`, `swap` and `move_if_unchanged` now hold per-key striped locks across their round trips, shared by every handle from one `VsockStore`. On `main` these were non-atomic and only safe because I/O was serial; #1951's pool and multi-thread REST would have made double-claims easy (review finding 1). Now they're atomic regardless — **stronger than `main`**.
- The "single-replica TEE deployments are unaffected in practice" warnings and caveats are gone, because the gap is.

## Tests
- `store::vsock::atomicity_tests`: each operation 32-wide on a 4-worker multi-thread runtime against a fake parent speaking the real wire protocol (3 ms per request) — exactly one winner each. A control test proves the harness catches the old unlocked read-then-delete (>1 winner).
- `store::key_locks::tests`: exclusion, no self-deadlock on a shared stripe, no deadlock for crossed two-key operations.
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::` → 123 passed. Clippy clean with and without `vsock-store`.
- CI: new step in the Enclave job runs these (nothing else compiles `vsock-store`).

## Follow-ups (same plan)
C (multi-thread REST + direct vsock inbound) builds on this. E1 adds native `TAKE` / `INSERT_IF_ABSENT` / `CAS` opcodes to the parent proxy to cut these to one round trip each.

title: feat(vta-sdk)!: wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal
body:
## Summary

The VTA side of wallet sign-in with a trigger link. The VTC is the sign-in service over the `auth/oob/*` Trust Tasks, and the member's VTA signs the two documents the wallet carries:

- **`auth/oob/grant` is an attestation (VTI-KEY-106).** It is added to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so the VTA signs it for `assertionMethod`. `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`, as the service verifies it.
- **Default policy for sign-in documents on `vault/sign-trust-task`.** `identify` and `grant` must match an exact schema. They are signed only for an enrolled, active device, as the entry's own principal, for one of the entry's targets, and within a clock-skew window. A `grant` also needs a never-reused id and the device's user-verification consent in `ext["org.openvtc.uv-consent"]`. That consent is a signed `task-consent/decision/0.2` over the digest of the unsigned grant. It can come from a hardware key or a WebAuthn ES256 passkey, verified with `vti-webauthn`. Each signature is audited, and a signature the audit trail cannot record is withheld.
- **User-verification key enrolment.** `device/register/0.2` and `device/heartbeat/0.2` accept an optional `ext["org.openvtc.uv-key"]`. It is stored on `DeviceBinding.uv_key` and summarised on the binding under `ext["org.openvtc"].uvKey`. A malformed key is refused. A disabled or wiped device cannot enrol one, and a replacement is accepted only on heartbeat.
- **`vtc-host` template.** It now advertises `TrustTaskHTTPS` (`#trust-tasks`, `{URL}{TRUST_TASKS_BASE}`, default `/v1`) and `SignInPortal` (`#sign-in-portal`, `{URL}{SIGN_IN_PORTAL_PATH}`, default `/members/`).
- **Many devices per member.** Each device (every browser install, every phone) has its own DID, its own ACL entry, and so its own binding, `consumerKind`, form factor and UV key. The gate checks the caller's own row. It checks a grant's UV decision against that row's UV key and the caller's own transport key, never another device's. Disabling or wiping one device changes one row, and the member's other devices keep signing in. A disabled or wiped device is refused with the new `oobDeviceDisabled`, distinct from `oobNotEnrolledDevice` (no binding, which the device fixes with `device/register`). No data-model change was needed; the design is in `design-docs/vta-multi-device.md` in the workspace docs.
- **Tests.** New tests pin that every built-in template and every VTA-minted document lists an `assertionMethod` key, so a persona can sign a grant.

The `vtc-service` side is in the companion PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1998.

## Backwards compatibility

What I checked, against `main`:

- **`ATTESTATION_SLUGS`.** `auth/oob/grant` is appended. The three existing slugs and their purposes are unchanged, and the proof-purpose classifier test still pins them. The constant's type grows from `[&str; 3]` to `[&str; 4]`, so the commit is marked `!`. No code in this workspace or in its sibling repos names that type.
- **`vtc-host.json` services.**
  - The template renders only when a DID is minted, so existing VTC DIDs are unaffected until someone runs `dids edit`.
  - The new variables are in `optionalVars` with defaults.
  - `VTCRest` and `VTCStatusList` are byte-for-byte unchanged and keep indices 0 and 1 when there is no transport.
  - The `TrustRegistry` referral moves from index 2 to 4. I searched production code for service selection by index or position and found none. All such uses are in `#[cfg(test)]` modules, and production code matches on `type` or `id`.
- **The VTC's `TrustTaskHTTPS` follows the base convention in HTTPS binding 0.2 §6.** Its `serviceEndpoint` is the Trust-Task base (`{URL}/v1`), and clients POST to `<base>/trust-tasks`, which is `/v1/trust-tasks`. Every existing consumer composes the URL this way: `vti-common`'s push engine, `vta-service`'s outbound REST and DID-hosting transport, `vta-sdk`'s `ServiceCapabilities`, the browser plugin and DID hosting. The `did-host-http*` templates already publish `{URL}/api` as a base. An earlier draft of this branch published the full URL, which would have sent those peers to `/v1/trust-tasks/trust-tasks`. A test now pins that the rendered entry resolves, through `ServiceCapabilities`, to the base.
- **`device/register/0.2` and `device/heartbeat/0.2`.** The `org.openvtc.uv-key` extension is optional. A client that does not send it gets exactly the old behaviour: no `uv_key`, no extra audit event, and no `ext` added to the wire binding unless local capabilities already put one there.
- **`vault/sign-trust-task/0.2` and the UV-consent gate.** The gate classifies the envelope first and returns early for anything outside the `auth/oob/` family, so every other type signs exactly as before. Within the family, only `auth/oob/grant/0.1` requires `org.openvtc.uv-consent`. `identify/0.1` is policed without one. Other `auth/oob/*` types, which no VTA signed before because the family is new, are refused rather than signed unattended. The new optional `ext` member on the request body is ignored for every non-grant type.
- **Multi-device.**
  - No storage or wire-shape change.
  - `register`, `heartbeat`, `list`, `disable` and `wipe` keep their requests and responses.
  - A registration still writes only the caller's own entry, so it cannot change the kind or binding of the member's administrative entries or of another device.
  - The one behaviour change is on this PR's own unreleased gate: a disabled or wiped device now gets `oobDeviceDisabled` instead of `oobNotEnrolledDevice`.
  - `OobError` (new in this PR) is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
  - A test writes an ACL row in the pre-`uvKey`, pre-`version` shape raw. It still loads, signs `identify` and enrols a passkey on heartbeat.
- **Storage.**
  - `DeviceBinding.uv_key` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. Old ACL rows load unchanged, and a row with no UV key serialises exactly as before.
  - `AclEntry`/`DeviceBinding` are not `deny_unknown_fields`, so an older VTA reading a row that has a UV key ignores the field.
  - The new audit actions are plain strings in the existing record shape.
- **Public API.** I ran `cargo semver-checks` against `main`.
  - **`vta-sdk`:** 196 checks pass. Everything is additive.
  - **`vti-common`:** one finding, `constructible_struct_adds_field` for `DeviceBinding.uv_key`, so a struct literal outside the crate would need `uv_key: None`. Nothing outside this repo constructs `DeviceBinding`; I checked the sibling OpenVTC and Affinidi repos. The commit is marked `feat(vti-common)!` so the release tooling sizes the bump.
  - **`vta-service`:** `register_device` and `heartbeat_device` gained parameters. `OobError` and the rest of `oob_sign_in` are new in this PR. Against this branch's previous head, the only finding is the added `OobError::DeviceDisabled` variant, and the enum is now `#[non_exhaustive]` so later variants are not breaking.
- **`notAfter` on a grant.** The VTA's check accepts integer epoch seconds (contract C9) and also RFC 3339 timestamps. That is deliberately lenient as a reader, and it is left accepting both.

## Dependence with the VTC PR

There is no build-time dependency in either direction. Each PR compiles and passes on its own base, and the VTC PR does not use the `ATTESTATION_SLUGS` change, because it names the purpose it requires and verifies against it. The dependency is at runtime: wallet sign-in against a VTC with #1998 completes only when the member's VTA has this PR, which signs `grant` for `assertionMethod` after the device's user-verification consent. A VTA without it signs a grant for `authentication`, and the VTC correctly refuses it.

## Testing

Run locally after rebasing onto current `main`, with the same commands CI uses.

Re-run for the multi-device commit:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy` for `--workspace --all-targets`, `--workspace --all-features --all-targets` and the three reduced `vta-service` feature sets: all clean.
- Every `cargo check` feature combo, including `rest,didcomm` without `webvh`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -p vti-common -p vta-sdk`, the `--doc` tests, `setup::interactive`, `routes::bootstrap` and `transport_harness_tests`: all pass.
- `vta-enclave` with `vsock-store` is Linux-only and was not built locally; this commit does not touch it.

Earlier results:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --no-default-features` with `rest`, with `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis` and with `setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis`, all `--all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Every other command in the "Feature combos (vta-service builds)" job is clean, including `rest,didcomm` without `webvh`, which the first push missed (fixed in e85538c1), and the `setup::interactive` and `routes::bootstrap` test runs. The commands are `cargo check -p vta-service --no-default-features` with `tee,rest,didcomm`, `rest,didcomm`, `aws-secrets,keyring,rest` and `azure-secrets,keyring,rest`.
- `cargo check -p vta-sdk --features client,sealed-transfer,provision-integration`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5446 passed, 23 skipped.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed.
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features`: passed.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2871 passed, 1 skipped. This shows the `vti-common` change does not affect the VTC.
- `cargo semver-checks --baseline-rev origin/main -p vta-sdk -p vti-common`: `vta-sdk` clean. `vti-common` has the one finding described above.

New tests:
- `vta-service/tests/it/vault_sign_in_oob.rs`: the sign-in policy end to end, covering an enrolled device, UV consent from a hardware key and from a passkey, replay, and the refusals. It also covers one member with two browsers and a phone:
  - each device signs with its own UV key, and another device's key is refused;
  - disabling or wiping one device leaves the others' rows unchanged and still signing in;
  - registration touches only the registering row;
  - an old-shape row still loads.
- Unit tests for UV key enrolment, replacement and refusal.
- The proof-purpose classifier.
- The template and minted-document `assertionMethod` pins.

## Known follow-ups

- The browser session key (design §12.9) is not built.
- GeoIP is stubbed to "unknown".
- Existing VTCs need `dids edit` plus `cnm did-log install` to publish the new `TrustTaskHTTPS` and `SignInPortal` services.

## Related

- Companion VTC PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1998.
- Browser plugin, which registers each install as a device before its first sign-in: https://github.com/OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin/pull/305. It needs this PR deployed for sign-in to complete.
- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

title: feat: register each install as a device before wallet sign-in
body:
## Why

Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (#303, #304) failed against a real VTA for any plugin that had never registered as a device. The VTA signs `auth/oob/identify` only for a caller whose own ACL entry has an active device binding. The plugin registered only inside `enrolUvPasskey`, at the first grant, which comes after `identify`. So `identify` was refused with `oobNotEnrolledDevice`, after the claim had already gone to the community.

**Requires OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1997 to be deployed for plugin sign-in to complete.** That PR has the `auth/oob` signing gate, UV-key enrolment and the `oobDeviceDisabled` code this PR reads.

## Multi-device model

The model needs no change. Every install is already a device of its own:

- onboarding mints a holder DID per install;
- the VTA keys the ACL entry, and the device binding on it, by that DID.

So two browser profiles, or a browser and a phone, are separate devices. Each has its own transport key, UV key, `consumerKind` and display name, and each can be listed, disabled or wiped without the others noticing. This PR makes the plugin act like one.

## What changed

- **Enrol early, once per holder per agent.**
  - New `ensureDeviceRegistered` (core) sends `device/heartbeat/0.2` first and falls back to `device/register/0.2` on `not_found`. A `conflict` from a racing register counts as success.
  - The offscreen document registers as `companion`/`browser`, under a name like "Chrome on macOS" (`device-name.ts`, from Client Hints or else the UA string):
    - after onboarding;
    - when an agent's inbox comes up, which is how existing installs enrol on upgrade, with no new onboarding;
    - at sign-in prepare, before anything is sent to the community.
  - A per-agent IndexedDB record (`pnm/device-enrolment/<vtaDid>` → the holder DID) keeps this to one heartbeat per holder.
- **Recover once, then explain.**
  - `identify` and `grant` register once and retry once on `oobNotEnrolledDevice`.
  - `oobDeviceDisabled`, `oobNoUvKey`, `oobUvInvalid` and a repeated `oobNotEnrolledDevice` show a clear message, and the claim is cancelled so the portal stops waiting.
  - Codes are read from `details.details.code` (R3.7).
- **The UV passkey stays lazy, and is tracked per agent and per holder.**
  - The window keeps the whole public enrolment.
  - The `uv-challenge` result names the credential the VTA holds for this holder.
  - When it is absent or different, the window enrols this browser's passkey (creating one only if it has none) and asks for a fresh grant. So a second agent or a re-onboarded holder works without a second passkey.
  - An `oobNoUvKey` refusal clears the record.
- `taskRefusalReason` moves into `vta/errors.ts`, so `device` and `vault` share it without a sideways import.

## Backwards compatibility

- **No new manifest permissions, no new dependencies.** The page-facing API (`window.vtaWallet.*`) is unchanged.
- **Stored state is additive.**
  - New keys: `pnm/device-enrolment/*`, `pnm/uv-passkey/enrolment` and `pnm/uv-passkey/enrolled/*`.
  - A missing key means "enrol now", never an error.
  - The legacy `pnm/uv-passkey/credentialId` is still written. A wallet that holds only that key reads as having no passkey, and creates one at its next approval: one extra passkey prompt, once.
- **Existing installs are not re-onboarded.** They register at the next unlock or sign-in.
- **Against a VTA without #1997** there is no `auth/oob` gate, so registering is harmless. `device/register/0.2` and `heartbeat/0.2` are sent exactly as the VTA already accepts them.
- `SignInVta.ensureDevice` and `enrolledUvCredential` are optional. The `uv-challenge` result gains an optional `uvCredentialId`.

## Tests

- `core/tests/device.ensure-registered.mjs`:
  - heartbeat-only when registered;
  - register on `not_found`;
  - `conflict` counts as success;
  - other refusals are rethrown;
  - `vaultOobRefusal` reads the code, never the message.
- `extension/tests/sign-in-flows.test.mts`:
  - the device enrols before identities are read and before anything reaches the community;
  - `uvCredentialId` is passed through;
  - VTA refusals map to messages and the claim is cancelled.
- `extension/tests/sign-in-view.render.test.mts`:
  - a first approval creates, enrols, then asserts over a fresh grant;
  - a passkey the VTA holds is asserted directly;
  - a stored passkey is enrolled at an agent that lacks it, without a second passkey.
- `extension/tests/device-name.test.mts`.
- Every `run` step of `ci.yml` passes locally on Node 26.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). There are no new network clients; everything goes through the existing `VtaSession`.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1). The enrolment and passkey records are written only after the VTA accepted. If the process dies first, the next heartbeat finds the binding.
- [x] Every retry is bounded; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). There is one retry, only after a definitive `oobNotEnrolledDevice`, which the VTA returns before it signs or records anything.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). Enrolment from `startInbound` is fire-and-forget and cannot fail the inbox.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): no wire change. The `uv-challenge` bridge result gains an optional member.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): an absent record means "register again", never "assume registered".
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): "registered" is logged only on a successful `device/register`.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged: none.

title: perf(vta-service): fewer storage reads per keys/sign without widening key custody
body:
## What and why

Part B of the rework of #1951 (Carlos Rincon's TEE `keys/sign` throughput PR). It keeps that PR's sign-path saving — **10 storage operations per `keys/sign` down to 8** — and fixes what review found in how it got there.

**Kept from #1951** (cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship and sign-off preserved):
- `fcc9f0d7` perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign (from 72371e53)
- `bd000667` perf(vta-service): reuse the context record for the keys/sign custody check (from 7e284648)

**Changed on top:**
- **Finding 8 — nested Option in a security gate.** `require_key_in_caller_scope` took `Option<Option<AclEntry>>` (outer `None` = not read, inner `None` = no row); a future `Some(None)` for a skipped lookup would silently pass gate 4 (#818). The row is now read once into `CallerAcl`, which has no "not read" state, and both gates take `&CallerAcl`. Same gates, same order, same audited refusals. `ensure_may_sign` keeps `Result<()>` for its other callers.
- **Finding 9 — key custody trusted a caller-supplied record.** `derive_record_key_in_context(…, Option<&ContextRecord>, …)` is gone. `key_custody::load_sign_context` does the one context read itself and returns a `CustodyContext` (private fields — only key custody constructs one), and `derive_record_key_in` takes it. The base path rule 6 checks comes only from key custody's own read in this request; a `CustodyContext` read for another context falls back to the record's own context. Key custody is again the only code that decides the base path, as CLAUDE.md requires.
- **Finding 10 — per-ancestor clone on the hot path.** `effective_context_policy_and_record` cloned every ancestor's `ContextPolicy`. It now resolves over borrowed policies; nothing is cloned and the leaf record comes back whole.

## Tests
- New: `gate_4_binds_a_protocol_defined_signature_too` — gate 0 does not run for `ProtocolDefined`, gate 4 still refuses a key outside `allowed_keys`.
- New: `the_sign_contexts_base_comes_from_custodys_own_read` — a `CustodyContext` read for another context cannot vouch for a foreign path; both refusals audited.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service -p vta-support --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -p vta-support` — 1851 passed, 1 skipped
- `cargo test -p vta-service -p vta-support --doc` — ok
- `key_custody_census` passes unchanged (no new raw seed access).

Not re-run: the enclave load test; storage-op count is unchanged from #1951's measured build (8 per sign).

none

title: fix(vta-enclave): bounded, visible log loss; warnings and errors never dropped
body:
## What and why

Part D of the #1951 rework. Carries Carlos Rincon's commit from #1951 (`fix(vta-enclave): log to stderr only while vsock logging is down`, cherry-picked with `-x`), which removes the per-line console write that capped throughput, and fixes the two log-loss findings from its review.

| Review finding | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 4: lines queued while connected were drained and dropped during reconnect backoff, and with stderr skipped they vanished entirely | `while rx.try_recv().is_ok() {}` on every retry | The queue is left alone (bounded, so memory cannot grow) and sent after reconnect, in order, after the line whose write failed |
| 5: a full channel dropped lines silently, with no console fallback | `let _ = tx.try_send(..)` | Drops are counted; one `vsock-log: dropped N lines (queue full)` line precedes the next line that fits. WARN/ERROR lines that cannot be queued go to stderr. The level comes from event metadata (`make_writer_for`), not text |

The module docs now say exactly what can still be lost: a line handed to a write that fails on both the old and the new connection.

CI: the enclave job now compiles `vsock-log` (both its feature sets). It is in the Nitro image and was otherwise only checked by hand.

## Tested
- 9 unit tests in `vsock_log` (the drain task is generic over the stream and connector, so they run without vsock): drop counting and marker, a marker that does not fit, WARN/ERROR fallback, no double console write, level from metadata, and replay of queued lines after an outage (fails against the old drain-and-drop).
- `cargo check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` for `vta-enclave` with `rest,didcomm,vsock-store,vsock-log` and `...,tenant-overlay` (macOS); `cargo fmt --check`; actionlint.

**Only CI / an enclave can verify:** Linux compilation of the CI feature sets, and behaviour against the real parent log receiver.

title: feat: wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob/*)
body:
## Summary

Adds wallet sign-in with a trigger link (`auth/oob/*`) to `@openvtc/rp-sdk`.

- **New entry point `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser`.** `createSignIn` is the starter. It generates a non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519 key `K_b`, sends `auth/oob/request`, builds the trigger link, renders it as a clickable SVG QR code at level M, hides it on `visibilitychange`, and long-polls `auth/oob/redeem`.
- **Server helpers on the main entry.**
  - `verifyOobClaim`, `verifyOobIdentify` and `verifyOobGrant`.
  - `verifyDidKeyDocument` and `computeContextDigest`.
  - `OobSignInService`, a reference state machine over a pluggable `OobRequestStore`.
  - `OOB_ERRORS`.
  - `trustTaskEndpoint(doc)` and `signInPortalOrigin(doc)`.
- **Wire format** follows the agreed contract (C1, C2, C7, C9) and is checked against the `auth/oob/*` schemas.
- **`trustTaskEndpoint(doc)`** treats a `TrustTaskHTTPS` `serviceEndpoint` as a base URL, following HTTPS binding 0.2 §6. It removes one trailing slash and appends `/trust-tasks`. For example, `https://members.example.org/v1` becomes `https://members.example.org/v1/trust-tasks`, and `…/api` becomes `…/api/trust-tasks`. The constant is exported as `TRUST_TASK_HTTPS_PATH`.
- **SIOPv2 deprecation.** The SIOPv2 helpers are marked `@deprecated` in JSDoc only (contract C7). They still work.

## Backwards compatibility

Nothing is removed or renamed, and no existing behaviour changes.

- **Existing exports.** I built `origin/main` and this branch, then diffed the generated `.d.ts` files. For `confirm`, `did-resolver`, `jcs`, `session` and `verify-id-token`, the only differences are doc comments, meaning the new `@deprecated` tags. `index.d.ts` only gains new exports, and no new name collides with an existing one. `verifyIdToken`, `IdTokenVerificationError`, `constantTimeEqual`, `KeyResolver`, `buildSessionCookie`, `establishSession` and the confirm helpers keep their names, signatures and types. The internal `eddsa-jcs-2022` refactor of `confirm.ts` is covered by the existing confirm tests.
- **The `package.json` `exports` map.** `main` already had an `exports` map with only `"."`, so deep imports were already blocked before this change. `"."` is unchanged (`types` + `import`), and `./browser` is added next to it. Neither version has `typesVersions`. The package is ESM-only before and after, so there is no CJS output to check. `npm pack --dry-run` includes `dist/browser*`.
- **The main entry's dependencies (fixed in this PR).** Originally, the main entry re-exported `defaultQrEncoder` from a module that imported `qrcode-generator`, so `import "@openvtc/rp-sdk"` on a server loaded the QR library.
  - The QR core (`oob/qr.ts`) now has no third-party import and no DOM use.
  - `defaultQrEncoder` and `createTriggerLinkElement` live in `browser/qr.ts`, which only `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser` imports.
  - From the main entry, `renderQrSvg` and `renderTriggerLinkHtml` take a required `encoder`. From the browser entry, the encoder defaults to `qrcode-generator`.
  - Three checks guard this:
    - `npm run lint` now also compiles `src/index.ts` without the DOM lib (`tsconfig.server-check.json`). I confirmed this check fails on the browser entry.
    - A test walks the main entry's import graph.
    - A Node module-resolution trace shows `dist/index.js` loads no `qrcode-generator`, and only `dist/browser.js` does.
- **Minimum Node version and TypeScript target.** `engines.node` is still `>=18.0.0`, and the `tsconfig.json` target is still ES2022. Both are unchanged.
- **Version and changelog.** I followed the repo convention: entries go under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`, and the version is bumped in a separate release commit (PR #6 did not bump either). The additions are minor-level, so the next release should be **0.3.0**.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` passes. It covers `tsc --noEmit`, the new no-DOM check of the main entry, and `prettier --check`.
- `npm test` (vitest) passes: 12 files, 133 tests. These include schema validation of emitted documents against the `auth/oob/*` schemas, the starter state machine, the service, QR rendering and entry-point isolation.
- `npm run build` passes. I also checked runtime imports of `@openvtc/rp-sdk` and `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser` under Node.
- The repo has no `.github/workflows`, so these local checks are the CI-equivalent run.

## Third-party dependency: approval needed

This PR adds **`qrcode-generator` 2.0.4**, pinned. It is MIT-licensed and has no dependencies of its own. Its approval under the organization's third-party dependency policy is **still pending**, so please do not publish a release until it is approved.

The library sits behind the `QrEncoder` interface (`(text) => { size, isDark(row, col) }`) and is loaded only by `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser`. If it is not approved, you can swap it by passing `encoder` or by replacing `defaultQrEncoder` in one file (`src/browser/qr.ts`). The rest of the API stays the same.

## Related

- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58

title: feat(vtc): wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob/*); SIOPv2 kept as legacy
body:
## Summary

The VTC side of wallet sign-in with a trigger link. The VTC acts as the sign-in service over the `auth/oob/*` Trust Tasks on `POST /v1/trust-tasks`.

- **`auth/oob/*` handlers** for `request`, `claim`, `prove`, `respond`, `redeem` and `cancel`, with `identify` and `grant` carried inside `prove` and `respond`. They follow contract C5 and C9:
  - The claim is by `K_a` and carries `parentThreadId` equal to `payload.requestId`.
  - `identify` is verified against the member's `authentication` key, and `grant` against `assertionMethod`.
  - The step 1 and step 2 responses are signed by the VTC's `assertionMethod` key (new `LocalSigner::sign_attested_response`).
  - `redeem` returns `{ subject, displayName, notAfter, amr }` and sets the member session as HttpOnly cookies. It goes through the same backend, keyspace and cookie shapes as every other portal sign-in.
  - `auth/oob/*` responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **Request state.** Requests live in the member-sessions keyspace under their own `oob_req:` prefix and are swept by the storage thread. The `K_b` key is held on the request record, not on the session.
- **Member portal.** "Sign in with your wallet" (a clickable trigger-link QR) is the default and first option. `GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` gives the page the community DID, the link host and the flow. The portal HTML is served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `no-store` and the default CSP.
- **SIOPv2 is deprecated (contract C7) but kept.** It is behind "Using an older wallet?", marked deprecated in code and docs, and not removed.
- **`vtc status`** reports whether the VTC's DID document lists the `SignInPortal` and `TrustTaskHTTPS` services, and names the fix if not.
- **Audit:** new `AuditEvent::MemberWalletSignIn` (city and country only, never the address).
- **Config:** new optional `admin_ui.sign_in_link_host`, defaulting to `link.trustoverip.org`.

The VTA side is in the companion PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997.

## Backwards compatibility

What I checked, against `feat/vtc-member-portal`:

- **SIOPv2 member-portal sign-in.**
  - Its routes are unchanged: `/v1/member/wallet/auth/challenge`, `/v1/member/wallet/auth/` and `/v1/member/wallet/auth/refresh`. So are `/v1/member/session` and the cookie names, paths and session format.
  - The backend change is doc comments only.
  - The existing integration tests in `tests/it/member_portal.rs` still pass. They cover the full challenge → `id_token` → session flow, refresh, the cookie session and cookie scoping.
  - In the UI, the SIOPv2 button and install guide moved inside a closed `<details>` "Using an older wallet?". `Portal.test.tsx` pins that the SIOPv2 button is still there and that the trigger-link option comes first.
- **`POST /v1/trust-tasks` dispatch.**
  - The `auth/oob/*` arm matches only `oob_tasks::URIS`, and `oob_tasks::precheck` returns `None` for every other type.
  - Every existing type routes exactly as before, and the `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri` census still covers them.
  - The new `HttpContext` task-local is read only by the `auth/oob` handlers. Cookies are appended only when a handler set some, and `no-store` only for `auth/oob/*` bodies.
- **`AuditEvent::MemberWalletSignIn`.**
  - `AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and adjacently tagged (`type`/`data`), so adding a variant leaves existing records byte-for-byte readable.
  - The payload's optional fields are `#[serde(default)]`.
  - An older binary skips an envelope it cannot parse rather than failing (`audit/writer.rs`). `vti-common`'s change is additive (a new variant on a non-exhaustive enum and a new struct).
- **Sessions and cookies.**
  - `vti_common::auth::Session` is unchanged. `K_b` lives on the `oob_req:` record, not on the session.
  - `cleanup_expired_sessions` iterates only `session:` and the new sweep only `oob_req:`, so neither reads the other's rows.
  - Sessions minted by `redeem` are ordinary member sessions, so existing sessions load as before.
- **Config.** `admin_ui.sign_in_link_host` is `Option` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, so existing configs start unchanged and a default config does not write it.
- **`TrustTaskHTTPS` follows the base convention (HTTPS binding 0.2 §6).**
  - `vtc status` checks for a `TrustTaskHTTPS` entry at the Trust-Task base `<public_url>/v1`, which is what the `vtc-host` template publishes. Clients POST to `<base>/trust-tasks`.
  - The check refuses an entry at the full `/v1/trust-tasks` URL, because base-plus-append consumers would reach `/v1/trust-tasks/trust-tasks`.
  - The handler stays at `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, and the portal posts there directly.

## Dependence on the VTA PR

There is no build-time dependency. This branch compiles and its tests pass on its own base, and it does not use the `ATTESTATION_SLUGS` change: the VTC states the purpose it requires (`assertionMethod` for `grant`, `authentication` for `identify`) and verifies against it directly. The dependency is at runtime: a member's wallet can complete sign-in only against a VTA that has the VTA PR. That VTA signs `grant` for `assertionMethod` after the device's user-verification consent, and enrols the UV key. Until then the VTC refuses a grant signed for `authentication`, as it should.

## Testing

Run locally on `feat/vtc-member-portal`, with the same commands CI uses:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2924 passed, 1 skipped.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: passed.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p vti-common --all-features`: 740 passed.
- Admin UI (`vtc-service/admin-ui`): `npm run wire:check` clean, `npx tsc -b --noEmit` clean, and `npx vitest run` 863 of 863 passed across 73 files.

New tests:
- `vtc-service/tests/it/member_portal_oob.rs`: the whole `auth/oob` flow over `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, and its refusals.
- `oob.rs` unit tests, including the `TrustTaskHTTPS` base check.
- `WalletSignIn.test.tsx`.
- `Portal.test.tsx`: the option order, and SIOPv2 behind "Using an older wallet?".
- The `trust_task_manifest` census.

The existing SIOPv2 integration tests in `tests/it/member_portal.rs` are unchanged and pass.

## Known follow-ups

- The plugin's VTA-minted holder is not an enrolled device. The VTA signs `identify` only for an enrolled device, and `register_device` overwrites the ACL entry's kind. A decision on how the plugin enrols is pending.
- The browser session key (design §12.9) is not built.
- GeoIP is stubbed to "unknown".
- Existing VTCs need `dids edit` plus `cnm did-log install` to publish the `TrustTaskHTTPS` and `SignInPortal` services. `vtc status` names the exact entries.

## Related

- Companion VTA PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997.
- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58

## Backport

title: feat(auth/oob): add the auth/oob out-of-band sign-in Trust Task family
body:
## What it adds

The `auth/oob/*` family: out-of-band sign-in, where a starter (the browser) asks a service to open a request and an approver (the wallet) decides it on another device. There are eight Trust Tasks, each at `https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/oob/<task>/0.1`:

`request`, `claim`, `prove`, `identify`, `respond`, `grant`, `redeem`, `cancel`

- **Shared schema** `specs/auth/oob/_shared/0.1/oob.schema.json`. It defines `RequestId`, `OobKey`, `MatchNumber`, `Mode`, `Purpose`, `Origin`, `Service`, `Requester` and `SameNetwork` once for the whole family. Beside it:
  - `CONVENTIONS.md` holds the family rules: purposes, disclosure at each step, windows and errors.
  - `TRIGGER-LINK.md` describes the QR code / trigger link the starter shows.
- **Wire details** follow the cross-repo sign-in contract (C9):
  - `claimDeadline`, `decisionDeadline` and `notAfter` are integer epoch seconds.
  - `contextDigest` is a `DigestMultibase`.
  - `decision` is `approve` or `decline`.
  - `sameNetwork` is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`.
  - `matchNumber` and `enteredNumber` match `^[0-9]{2}$`.
  - The claim's `parentThreadId` must equal `payload.requestId`.
  - `cancel` returns `{status: "cancelled"}`, and `respond` returns `{status: "approved" | "declined"}`.
  - `redeem` returns `{subject, displayName, notAfter, amr}`, never tokens.
- **Endpoint discovery:** `TRIGGER-LINK.md` and `auth/oob/claim` say the `TrustTaskHTTPS` `serviceEndpoint` is the Trust-Task base, and they point to HTTPS binding 0.2 §6 for how to build the request URL (`<base>/trust-tasks`).
- **Generated bindings:**
  - Rust: `trust_tasks_rs::specs::auth::oob::<task>::v0_1`, under the existing `auth` feature. Includes conformance tests.
  - TypeScript: `AuthOob<Task>_v0_1` and `OobShared_v0_1`.
  - Go and Dart: packages and libraries under `specs/auth/oob/...`.

## Backwards compatibility

Everything in this PR is additive. What I checked:

- **Diff against `main`:** every file is new except five generated index files. Those five only gain lines; no line is removed.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/src/schema_index.rs`: new match arms.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/auth/mod.rs`: `pub mod oob;`.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/tests/conformance/main.rs`: new test modules.
  - `trust-tasks-ts/src/index.ts`: new namespace exports.
  - `trust-tasks-ts/src/_shared/components.ts`: new hoisted types.
- **Existing specs:** no existing spec, schema, `$id`, Type URI or generated binding changes in content, name or path.
- **Tooling:** no generator or tooling changes. The diff does not touch `scripts/`, `trust-tasks-codegen`, any `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pubspec.yaml` or `go.mod`. I re-ran all four generators (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` with `cargo fmt`, and `build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`) and there was no drift.
- **Rust features:** default features are unchanged (`default = ["all-specs"]`). The new modules sit behind the existing `auth` feature, so no new feature is introduced.
- **Packages:** the npm, Go and Dart package exports only gain entries. The new TS shared type names do not collide with existing exports, and `tsc` passes.
- **Registries:** the registry and indexes only gain entries.
- **Versions:** no version is bumped, as RELEASING.md asks. The Release PR sizes the bump from the conventional commits (`feat` gives a minor bump).

## Testing

I ran the same steps the CI workflows run:

- **Registry:** `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run build` passes: 698 specs validated and 1343 examples checked against the envelope schema. `npm run test:infra`, `npm run test-ceremonies` and `npm run check-dart-packages` pass.
- **Bindings conformance:** `npm run check-bindings` reports that all 698 specs agree across TS, Rust, Go and Dart, and that the 1549 declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`.
- **Generation drift:** Rust codegen with fmt, and the TS, Go and Dart generators, leave the tree clean.
- **Rust:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` passes with default features and with `--all-features`.
  - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` pass, with 0 failures.
  - `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` passes.
- **TypeScript:**
  - `trust-tasks-ts`: `tsc --noEmit` passes, `npm test` passes 79/79, and `npm run smoke` passes.
  - `trust-tasks-ts-proof`, `-tsp` and `-capability-client`: build, test typecheck and tests all pass.
- **Go:** `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./...` pass for the core module, `tsp` and `proof`.
- **Dart:**
  - `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` is clean, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` at the pubspec floor is clean, and `dart test` passes 74/74.
  - The proof, https, didcomm, capability-client and tsp packages: analyze is clean and the tests pass.

## Related

- VTI spec: https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58
- Implementations in other repos will link back to this PR.
