title: fix(vetting): tickets follow the live PCS mode; get tokens in one key; enrolment answers survive restarts
body:
## What was wrong

1. **PCS mode was cached forever.** `hides_vetters()` returned true whenever this client held a hidden-vetting engine for the community, whatever the community published now. So a VTC that turned PCS ZKP off kept gating that vetter's tickets on an enrolment it no longer needed, and attesting still went down the hidden path. The ticket gate decided from that remembered state and never re-read it.
2. **A lost enrolment answer was a month-long dead end.** The blinding that opens a `pcs-root` answer was held only in memory. A restart between the ask and the answer, or a second enrolment asked while the first was in flight (the VTC answers the first and refuses the second with `alreadyEnrolled`), lost it. The VTC issues one credential per member per label and keeps no copy to send again.
3. **Getting tokens was hard to find**, `t` only refused, and a new vetter waited up to an hour ("on the next pass") to enrol.
4. **The manifest was fetched several times in seconds** (repeated `d`, or passes chained on answers).
5. The copy had problems: a doubled `..`, and the full refusal appeared in both the banner and the "You vet for" row.

## What changed

**Live mode (`openvtc-core/src/vetting/mode.rs`, new)**
- The mode is now a *reading* of the join manifest (`vetting.ext` / `org.openvtc.hidden-vetting`, served live from the VTC's stored criteria). It is persisted as last-known on `KnownCommunity::vetter_mode` together with `read_at`. Read failures are kept in memory and say which kind they are: unsent / unanswered / refused / unreadable (R6.4).
- Both the DIDComm and REST manifest paths record the reading. Every consumer now uses the same reading: the badges (Communities, desk, join, journey), the ticket gate, attesting and the drip.
- TTL is 10 min. A stale reading is re-read when the desk is opened, and on the 5 s sweep while the desk stays open, at most once per 2 min per community (R1.4). The desk shows the reading's age or the failure next to the last-known value.

**Tickets**
- `t` asks the community afresh and decides only on an answer that arrived *after* it asked:
  - named → a named ticket with no gate;
  - PCS ZKP → the enrolment/token gate;
  - failure → no ticket, and the message says why.
- The wait is bounded (R1.2). Mode switches are announced ("first-vtc switched from PCS ZKP to named vetting.").
- Tickets record the mode they were issued under, and are marked when that differs from the community's current mode.
- If `t` finds no tokens, it runs the get-tokens pass itself where that can help. Otherwise it says exactly when tokens can come (next window / next label date) and what the operator can do.

**Tokens / enrolment**
- `k` on the desk gets tokens: it enrols if needed, then draws every window that has begun. It reports per community what it is doing or what blocks it. It never draws ahead of the schedule.
- The enrolment blinding is saved to the protected config **before** the request is sent, using a bounded synchronous save. A late answer after a restart still opens.
- No second enrolment is sent while one is unanswered.
- A newly minted engine is saved.
- A received vetter grant runs the vetter side within seconds, and the first draw follows the enrolment answer.
- Manifest re-reads wait ≥30 s after the last ask or answer, and never overlap an open question.

## VTI changes needed (not made here)
- **Unblocking an already-lost enrolment:** `vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root` should *re-issue* rather than refuse with `alreadyEnrolled` when the member already holds `label` **and** the request presents the same PCS identifier `id` the member is bound to (`EnrolmentRecord.id`).
  - This cannot give one vetter two votes. The credential is bound to `id = Tag(usk, c0)`, every attestation tag derives from `usk`, and applicant proofs require pairwise-distinct tags.
  - Tokens are rate-limited per member/label/tick, independently of the credential.
  - A request under a different `id` stays `identifierRebound`.
- **What an operator can do today:** publish hidden vetting again with a new live period first in `livePeriods`, e.g. `["2026-10b","2026-10"]`. The vetter presses `k` and enrols under `vetter/2026-10b`.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). The ticket's mode read is bounded by the 30 s query window plus a hard 35 s bound. The save-before-send is bounded at 15 s.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The enrolment blinding is now durable *before* the send. The ticket is created only after the mode answer.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Mode re-reads are limited to once per 2 min, manifest re-reads to once per 30 s, and save-failure retries are capped by `VETTER_REFRESH_RETRIES`. Concurrent enrolments are no longer sent.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: none on the wire. New persisted types are camelCase; `AskedEnrolment` is `deny_unknown_fields`.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*). An unknown or failed mode issues no ticket.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [ ] Deviations: `HiddenVetterState` (`deny_unknown_fields`) gains `enrolmentsAsked`, so a config written by this build will not load in an older build while an enrolment is in flight. This follows the earlier precedent for that struct.

## Tests
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` and `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc` all pass.

New tests cover:
- a stale reading being replaced;
- a PCS→named switch issuing a named ticket with no gate;
- a named→PCS switch gating the ticket;
- failures being surfaced by kind, plus the bounded wait;
- the lost enrolment message (said once, no `..`, with dates and the operator hint);
- ticket mode marking;
- get tokens (not enrolled → enrol + draw; window drawn → exact next window; lost → hint);
- a stored blinding opening an answer after a restart;
- a refused enrolment dropping its blinding;
- a grant triggering immediate enrolment;
- manifest re-ask throttling.

body:
fix(vetting): tickets follow the live PCS mode; get tokens in one key; enrolment answers survive restarts (#462)

* fix(vetting): a ticket follows how the community vets now, read fresh, not a forever-cached mode

How a community vets (named or PCS ZKP) is now a reading of its join
manifest kept with when it was read (KnownCommunity::vetter_mode), plus a
memory-only record of how the last read failed. Holding a hidden-vetting
engine is no longer taken as PCS ZKP mode.

- t asks the community afresh and decides the ticket only on that answer:
  named => named ticket, no enrolment gate; PCS ZKP => enrolment/token gate;
  failed read => no ticket, saying unsent / unanswered / refused / unreadable
  beside the last-known mode (R6.4), bounded wait (R1.2).
- Mode switches are said and every badge follows the reading.
- Opening the desk, and keeping it open, re-reads a stale (>10 min) mode at
  most once per 2 minutes per community (R1.4); the desk shows staleness.
- Attesting and the token drip follow the reading.
- Tickets record the mode they were issued under and are marked when it
  differs from the current one.
- The lost-enrolment refusal says the label, the date the next monthly label
  can start, and what to do meanwhile, once; the desk keeps a short status.
  The doubled full stop is gone.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): get tokens in one key, enrol a new vetter at once, never lose an enrolment answer to a restart

- The enrolment blinding is saved to the protected config before the
  pcs-root request is sent (HiddenVetterState::enrolments_asked), so an
  answer that lands after a restart still opens. No second enrolment is
  asked while one is unanswered (its alreadyEnrolled was what read as a
  lost answer). A freshly minted engine is saved.
- k on the desk gets tokens: enrol if needed, then draw every window that
  has begun, saying per community what it does or what blocks it and until
  when. t with no tokens runs the same pass instead of only refusing, and
  says when the next window opens / next label can start, with the
  operator hint (publish a new live period) for a lost enrolment.
- A received vetter grant runs the vetter side at once: enrol within
  seconds and draw the current window as soon as it is answered.
- A manifest is not re-fetched within 30 s of the last ask or answer, nor
  while a question for it is open (R1.4).

title: fix(vetting): the face step asks for what the community needs, and takes it right there
body:
## Problem

On the applicant journey's **Face** step, someone with no attributes hit a dead end. The make-a-face form said "add it under My Identity" three different ways. It then failed with "Tick at least one attribute with space", even though there was nothing to tick. To get past it, they had to leave the flow, find My Identity, work out that the type key is `name.legal`, add the attribute, come back, and press `f`.

## What changes

The form is now built from what the community's card requires (plus any optional claims a vetter's session named):

```
 Name                  Vetting

 What this community asks for
▸ ✗ Legal name        needed  name.legal
      Your legal name (name.legal), exactly as on your documents:
      Alice Example▎

 0 of 1 required attribute ready — Enter: save your legal name
Tab/↑/↓: move  ←/→ or Space: choose  Enter: continue  Esc: cancel
```

- **Missing attributes are filled in on the form.** A required claim type with no matching attribute gets an input on its row. Enter saves the value as a real self-asserted attribute with the correct type key and ticks it in the face. It is saved the same way My Identity saves one: the new `pool::draft_from_text` does the validation (My Identity's attribute form now uses it too), then `pool::put` does the write. My Identity's listing is queued to re-read.
- **Sensible defaults.** Required claims start ticked. Optional claims and the holder's other attributes are offered but stay unticked, so only what was asked for is shown. The face name starts as the community's **verified** agent name (from the cached round-trip), otherwise "Vetting". It never uses an unverified name.
- **Several matches.** When more than one attribute matches a required type, ←/→ or Space picks which one (`←/→ 1 of 2`). Rows show values so two legal names can be told apart. Only non-sensitive values are read (`include_sensitive: false`), and they are masked according to the agent's claim-type registry, as on the Identity page.
- **One voice.** A single status line says what Enter does next ("1 of 1 required attribute ready — Enter: make the face and wear it"). Enter makes the face only once every required claim is ticked. Until then it moves the focus to the row the status line names. The duplicate "My Identity" lines and the tick error are gone. The form shows an error line only for a value that does not parse or a save the agent refused, and the error includes the agent's reason (R6.4).
- **Same text wherever the form is reached.** The `f` picker's "Make a face" row, its no-faces message, the card preview's fix hint, and the card refusal text now point to the form instead of to My Identity.

## Tests

- State: no attributes → typed value → `Save(draft)` with `name.legal` → `AttributeSaved` ticks it and queues the Identity refresh → `Make`. Also: a held requirement makes the face on the first Enter; several candidates cycle with ←/→ and Space; a refused save keeps the value and shows the reason; the face name uses only a verified agent name.
- Render (`vetting_panel`): a single inline prompt with no contradictory lines; a typed value and its "save" status; a held requirement shown ✓ with its value; the `←/→ 1 of 2` marker; extras offered unticked.
- Keys + TestBackend (`main/mod.rs`): a needed-value row takes typing, spaces included, and Enter submits; a held row routes Space → `Toggle` and ←/→ → `Cycle`; the drawn screen shows the prompt and status line and not the old errors.
- Core: `draft_from_text` checks.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)

- [x] R1.2: no new client. The save uses the existing `VtaClient` (finite timeouts) through `pool::put`, the same call My Identity uses.
- [x] R1.4: no polling added.
- [x] R6.4: a holder-grant refusal on the save goes to the same HolderGrant view as the pool read. Any other failure shows the agent's text on the form.
- [x] R3.6: no new endpoints. Uses the existing `persona/attribute/put` and `persona/attribute/list` calls.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (with and without default features), and `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc` all pass.

title: fix: no built-in storm.ws org or mediator DID — the mediator comes from your VTA
body:
## Problem
Settings showed `Org DID: did:webvh:QmXk…dZHK:fpp.storm.ws`. It was hardcoded: setup wrote it into every account. A persona minted against a VTA that advertised no DIDComm mediator was also given a built-in "public" mediator on `fpp.storm.ws`. That host is one operator's own deployment, and a reference CLI shouldn't hardcode it.

## Changes
- **Org DID removed.** Nothing used `Account.org_did`; Settings only displayed it and let you edit it. This PR removes the row, `SettingsMode::EditOrgDid`, `update_org_did`, the setup writes, and the field. **Old configs still load.** `Account` has the D19 `#[serde(flatten)] extra` catch-all, so an existing `org_did` key lands in `extra` and is written back unchanged. An older build reading the file still finds it. New tests cover loading a legacy `org_did`, carrying it through a round trip, and new accounts not writing one.
- **Settings rows have names.** Rows are now addressed through constants in `settings_panel.rs` (`FRIENDLY_NAME_ROW` … `WIPE_ROW`) instead of the scattered literals `2`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `8`, `9`. The renderer, the key handler and the edit dispatch all use them.
- **No mediator fallback.** A new persona's mediator comes only from `KeyBackend::Vta { mediator_did }`, the mediator the VTA advertised at connect time (`setup_config::vta_mediator`). If there is none:
  - **Create persona:** `mint_standalone_persona` refuses before creating any context, key or DID.
  - **Join with a new persona:** the `IdentityPick::Mint` arm fails the join before creating keys. Reusing an existing persona is unaffected.
  - **`mint_persona_into`:** acts as a backstop and refuses rather than persisting a persona with a mediator nobody chose.

  The error (`NO_VTA_MEDIATOR`) says the VTA advertised no DIDComm mediator, so the persona can't be given one, and that the VTA's operator needs to configure one (R6.4).

title: fix(setup): running the PNM command is its own step, and a rejected setup DID leads back to it
body:
## Problem

The first-time setup page "Authorise the setup DID via PNM" read as information: a DID, commands, and "[ENTER] once authorised" at the end. People pressed Enter without running the `pnm` command. Step 2 then failed with `forbidden: DID not in ACL: …` under the diagnostics, and Enter took them back with nothing linking the refusal to the step they had skipped.

## Change

**Step 1 of 2: Run the PNM command** (`vta_acl_instructions.rs`)
- Leads with numbered actions: 1. copy (F2 new context / F3 existing context / **F4 `acl delete`**, new), 2. run it in your PNM session, 3. press Enter once PNM prints **"ACL entry created"**. That phrase is in both `pnm contexts create` ("Admin ACL entry created:") and `pnm acl create` ("ACL entry created:"), checked against `vta-cli-common`.
- Warns that `pnm contexts create`'s "already exists … --admin-did was NOT added" (it exits 0) means the grant did not land, so use F3.
- Says the grant lasts 1 hour and the setup DID can use it once. Enter is labelled "I've run it".
- When step 2 sends the user back, a banner at the top says what went wrong and which command fixes it. Under a re-grant, F3/F4 are marked ▶.

**Step 2 of 2: Connect to the VTA** (`vta_provisioning.rs`)
- A failure is classified by `state_handler/setup_sequence/provision_failure.rs::classify` and routed (R6.4: one hint per failure class, not one for all):

| class | detected by | the user sees | Enter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NotAuthorised` | `DID not in ACL`, the SDK authz probe's `is not authorized on`, `VtaError::{Forbidden,Auth}` Display (`forbidden: `, `authentication failed: `), REST `failed (401`/`(403`, `permissionDenied` | "The VTA didn't accept the setup DID. This almost always means the PNM command hasn't been run yet, or it ran against another VTA or context, or it expired." | back to step 1, same DID and context |
| `GrantSpent(Expired / AlreadyUsed / NoHandoff)` | `ACL entry expired`, `hand-off entry for … has expired`, `there is no hand-off to exercise`, `no one-time hand-off` / `carries no hand-off marker` (vta-service VTI-ACL-053..058) | the specific reason + "re-grant: delete, then re-create" | back to step 1, banner asks for F4 then F3 |
| `GrantSpent(UsedByThisAttempt)` | rollover happened (`credential_did` set), then a later step failed | "accepted and rolled over, then failed; the grant is used up" | back to step 1 for a re-grant |
| `Unreachable` | a failed `ResolveDid` row (typed `DiagCheck`), `network error: `, `tsp/didcomm transport error: `, `could not connect to VTA`, DNS/TLS/refused/timeout phrasing | "The VTA could not be reached … not about the PNM command" | **retry from step 2**, `[B]` back |
| `Other` | anything else | the error verbatim + a short hint | back to step 1 (error repeated there), `[R]` retries |

  A refusal outranks a transport fault, because the runner can log a failed TSP row and then reach the VTA on its fallback leg. The old `needs_handoff_regrant` check is folded into this.
- The setup DID is never re-minted on the way back. It is minted once per wizard run at VtaEnterDid, so the commands shown stay valid. A grant the run already spent is re-granted for the same DID.
- `handle_vta_start_provision` now clears the previous attempt's `diagnostics` and `credential_did` before it starts, so the classifier reads only the current attempt. Retry is debounced locally.
- `context_occupied.rs` is untouched.

### Why string matching
`vta-sdk` 0.63.2's provision runner flattens every failure to the `String` in `VtaEvent::Failed` / `DiagStatus::Failed`, and `provision_admin_rotated_via_rest` returns `ProvisionError::WorkflowFailed(String)`. There is no typed `VtaError` to match by the time OpenVTC sees the failure. What survives is the failed `DiagCheck` row (typed, used for resolve), the `thiserror` Display prefixes of `VtaError` variants, and the VTA's refusal phrases. Each pattern is listed once in `provision_failure.rs` with its upstream source. Follow-up worth raising in VTI: carry a typed failure kind on `VtaEvent::Failed`.

## Checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)
- R6.4: refused vs unreachable vs other each get their own text and their own next step. Unreachable never names PNM.
- R1.2: no new outbound clients. Retry is user-driven and goes through the existing provisioning path (SDK timeouts, interrupt race in `setup_wizard`).
- R1.4: no polling added.
- R3.6: refusal phrases checked against current `vti-common::acl::check_acl*`, `vta-service` `operations::acl::exercise_handoff` and `provision_integration::refuse_unmarked_expiring_rollover`, the SDK's `provision_client::{authz,auth_rest,runner_*}`. PNM output checked against `vta-cli-common::commands::{contexts,acl}`.

## Tests
- `provision_failure`: 8 classification tests (refused on each transport's error shape, each grant problem, unreachable even when the SDK sentence mentions `pnm acl create`, failed resolve row, refusal outranking an earlier transport fault, refusal found on a diagnostics row, other stays other, after rollover).
- Step 1: TestBackend render tests (numbered steps and success phrase, banner per class, verbatim Other, fits at 80 columns with the banner) and key tests (Enter starts step 2 with the typed context and clears the banner, typing keeps it).
- Step 2: render and key tests for refused (Enter goes back with the reason, no retry sent), unreachable (Enter retries, second press is debounced, B goes back), other (verbatim, R retries, Enter carries the detail), spent grant, and no-ops mid-flight.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` all pass locally.

fix(setup): running the PNM command is its own step, and a rejected setup DID leads back to it (#458)

The "Authorise the setup DID via PNM" page read as information, so people
pressed Enter without running the command; step 2 then failed with
`forbidden: DID not in ACL` and nothing tied it back to the skipped step.

Step 1 is now "Run the PNM command": numbered actions (copy with

created"), the "already exists ... NOT added" trap named, and the
1-hour, use-once grant stated. F4 copies the `acl delete` a re-grant
needs.

Step 2 classifies a failure (`provision_failure::classify`) from the
failed diagnostics rows and the VTA's/SDK's refusal phrases (the SDK
flattens errors to strings before they reach us) and routes it (R6.4):

title: Bump undici and wrangler
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) to 7.29.1 and updates ancestor dependency [wrangler](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/tree/HEAD/packages/wrangler). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `undici` from 7.29.0 to 7.29.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.29.1

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3: BalancedPool could drop function-valued connection options while cloning its configuration, including custom TLS certificate validation callbacks. Undici now preserves connect and legacy tls options when creating upstreams. Fixed by f690157d.
  • GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5: a WebSocket server could select a subprotocol when none was requested, causing an uncaught TypeError that could terminate the process. Undici now rejects the handshake with protocol error 1002. Fixed by 6615e017.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v: a malformed permessage-deflate payload exceeding the configured decompression limit could emit an unhandled zlib error and terminate the process. Undici now destroys the inflater after reaching the limit. Fixed by 63cf698b.
  • GHSA-rx4f-c7p8-82vq: an unclean WebSocketStream close could create an unobserved rejected promise when its writable stream was locked, potentially terminating the process. Undici now propagates the failure through the retained writable stream controller. Fixed by 1858656e.
  • GHSA-2jfj-6hjv-fm6j: shared caches could store and replay responses containing Set-Cookie, disclosing one user's cookies to another caller. Undici now excludes these responses from shared caches, including existing entries and revalidation paths. Fixed by b6c5a002.
  • GHSA-3xpg-4rpp-hhhm: the decompression interceptor did not bound decoded output, allowing compressed responses to consume excessive memory. Undici now limits every decompression stage to 64 MiB by default and supports a configurable maxSize. Fixed by 2c7d7e12.
  • GHSA-pmjh-fq2x-6v4x: a terminal retry failure after response headers were exposed could orphan the original response body, causing consumers to hang indefinitely. Undici now propagates the terminal error to the exposed body. Fixed by 3c672659.

Low severity

  • GHSA-8436-99hf-9mmv: cache interceptors could store and replay responses to unsafe HTTP methods such as POST or DELETE. Undici now restricts cache reads and writes to safe methods while preserving invalidation by successful unsafe requests. Fixed by b61d9432.
  • GHSA-2gqq-gqf2-x968: the dump interceptor could treat an oversized chunked response as successfully truncated when no Content-Length was present. Undici now enforces maxSize against received bytes and aborts oversized responses. Fixed by 21693f40.
  • GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r: the retry interceptor could concatenate a resumed response with inconsistent framing into downstream output, enabling response splitting or corruption. Undici now validates Content-Range against the original response framing before resuming. Fixed by cd8af90b.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] drop: remove Node.js 26 from shared-builtin CI build by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5592
  • fix(h2): honour headersTimeout by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5604
  • fix(h2): keep the connection ref'd while requests are outstanding by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5605
  • ci: increase Windows workflow timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5621
  • fix(h2): retire the request that completed, not the head of the queue by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5618
  • fix(h2): settle a request whose stream is cancelled by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5607
  • perf: reduce EventSourceStream parser allocations (#5032) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5646
  • fix(h2): handle GOAWAY for CONNECT streams by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5640
  • [v7.x] perf(h1): drop idle-socket timer floor with a ref'd setImmediate (#5707) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5769

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.29.0...v7.29.1

Commits
  • d39a83e Bumped v7.29.1 (#5772)
  • 0d88464 fix(test): remove unused EventEmitter import
  • f57411b perf(h1): drop idle-socket timer floor with a ref'd setImmediate (#5707) (#5769)
  • 3c67265 fix(retry): settle exposed body on terminal failure
  • cd8af90 fix(retry): validate resumed response framing
  • 6615e01 fix(websocket): reject unrequested subprotocols
  • 2c7d7e1 fix(decompress): limit decompressed response size
  • b6c5a00 fix(cache): do not cache Set-Cookie in shared caches
  • 21693f4 fix(interceptor/dump): abort oversized chunked responses
  • f690157 fix: preserve BalancedPool connection options

Updates `wrangler` from 4.140.0 to 4.147.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.147.0

Minor Changes

  • #15928 7f57b1c Thanks @​ichernetsky-cf! - Allow "us" as a jurisdiction for Container applications

    Container placement constraints now accept constraints.jurisdiction: "us" in Wrangler and typed Cloudflare configuration. This makes the US jurisdiction available alongside "eu" and "fedramp".

Patch Changes

  • #15974 7f700ef Thanks @​martinezjandrew! - Fix wrangler containers list to report live instances

    The LIVE INSTANCES column now reports each application's active runtime instances instead of its configured instance count, matching the Cloudflare dashboard. JSON output continues to expose the configured count through the existing instances field.

  • #15980 90e6a1b Thanks @​martinezjandrew! - Accept Durable Object application IDs in Containers commands

    wrangler containers instances and wrangler containers delete now accept the 32-character hexadecimal application IDs returned for Durable Object-backed applications, in addition to legacy dashed UUIDs.

  • #15871 6a4b0fe Thanks @​tw4! - Retry transient API failures in wrangler workflows instances list and wrangler workflows instances describe

    Previously, a single temporary 5xx response or dropped connection made these read-only commands exit with an error, even though the next request would have succeeded. They now use Wrangler's existing bounded API retry handling. The read that resolves --id latest is retried too, which also benefits the other wrangler workflows instances commands that accept latest; the mutating requests they make afterwards are not retried. Persistent failures are still reported after the retries are exhausted, and under --json any retry notices are written to stderr so stdout stays valid JSON.

  • #15777 464a582 Thanks @​Naapperas! - Support the new Workflows createBatch() API in local development

    Local Workflows bindings now accept object-form batches that create instances from a count or a list of instance options. The result includes handles for created instances and indexed per-instance errors, matching the runtime API while preserving the deprecated array form.

  • #15639 aee2842 Thanks @​hugo-vicente11! - Add --allowed-mail to the experimental wrangler tunnel quick-start command

    The option forwards exact email addresses, comma-separated lists, and wildcard domains to cloudflared. It can be specified more than once to combine multiple recipient rules.

    Email-protected tunnels require cloudflared 2026.9.2 or later. Wrangler checks the selected binary before starting the tunnel and reports an upgrade error when it is incompatible.

title: fix: readable in Terminal.app and terminals without 24-bit colour; add --monochrome
body:
## Problem
In macOS's built-in Terminal.app, the TUI is close to unreadable: everything is washed out to pale grey on white. There are two causes:
1. **24-bit colour.** The TUI draws every role in 24-bit RGB. Terminal.app doesn't support 24-bit colour; it guesses at the escape, and the guess washes colours out. The CLI's own output already handled this (`Themed`: truecolour when `COLORTERM` says so, otherwise `nearest_256`), but the TUI never did.
2. **A dark default theme.** The default theme is OpenVTC's dark one, which draws ordinary text near-white. Terminal.app's default profile has a white background.

## Fix
- **`theme::paint`** now calls a new `to_256_colours` after theming when `terminal::truecolor()` is false. Every `Color::Rgb` becomes `Color::Indexed(nearest_256(..))`; named and indexed colours are untouched. `nearest_256` is now `pub(crate)`.
- **The default theme choice is `auto`** (`Choice::default`). OpenVTC asks the terminal for its background (OSC 11), so a light terminal gets the light theme. A terminal that doesn't answer is taken as dark, which is the same as before.
- **`--monochrome`** (global flag) calls `theme::force_monochrome()` before anything is drawn. `no_color()` honours it, so it's the existing `NO_COLOR` rendering (roles kept apart with bold, underline and reverse), TUI and CLI output alike.
- **`docs/themes.md`:** `auto` as the default, a section on terminals without 24-bit colour, and `--monochrome`.
- **CHANGELOG:** entries under `[0.5.0]`.

## Tests

title: vtc/members/update/0.1: publishConsent may be withdrawn by an administrator, never granted — add consentGrantForbidden
body:
## Problem
A member's consent to be published in the community's trust registry is the member's own privacy decision. The member gives it with `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.2, 0.3), and the community copies it onto the member record.

`vtc/members/update/0.1` lists `publishConsent` among the fields an administrator may change, with no direction. So an administrator can set it from `false` to `true`, which publishes someone who said no. Approving a join already doesn't consent on the applicant's behalf, and an update shouldn't either.

## Proposal
- **The direction rule:** `publishConsent` on `vtc/members/update` MAY lower consent (`true` → `false`, e.g. a takedown) and MAY restate the current value. It MUST NOT raise it (`false` → `true`).
- **Where consent comes from:** the only way consent becomes `true` is the member's own `registryConsent` on a join submit. That includes a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record.
- **A new error code** for the refused raise:

```yaml
  - code: vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden
    meaning: "The update would set `publishConsent` to true for a member who has not consented. Registry consent is the member's own decision, given on their join request; an update may withdraw it, never grant it. Nothing in the request was applied."
    retryable: false
```

- **A refused raise rejects the whole update.** No other field in the same request is applied, so a partial update can't be mistaken for a full one.
- **What a withdrawal does:** the community's registry sync should then remove the member's published record, and the spec text could say so.

## Related gap (not in this change)
A member admitted before consent existed, or who answered "no" at join, can only become listed by leaving and rejoining. That costs their credentials, role and vetter grants. A **member-signed** task for a member to grant or withdraw their own registry consent would close this. Is it worth tracking as a separate proposal?

## Reference implementation
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1962 implements this in `vtc-service`:
- `vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden`, HTTP 400;
- withdraw and restate still work;
- an end-to-end test of publish → withdraw → sync → record removed;
- the code registered as service-defined (SPEC §8.5) in its error-code census, which will fail once the spec defines it, prompting a switch to the generated constant.

OpenVTC's join flow asks for consent explicitly and off by default (OpenVTC/openvtc#439).

title: vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root/0.1: let a member recover a lost enrolment answer within the same label
body:
## Problem
`pcs-root/0.1` requires a community to refuse a second enrolment under a label it has already issued under (`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root:alreadyEnrolled`, plus the authorization check "this member has not already enrolled under this label"). That's right for counting: one credential per member per label is what makes distinct tags distinct people.

But it makes a **lost answer unrecoverable for the rest of the label**. If the community issues the root credential and the response never reaches the vetter in a form it can open, the vetter holds no credential and every retry is refused as `alreadyEnrolled`. They can't attest under hidden vetting until the next `vetter/<YYYY-MM>` label, which can be weeks away. Causes include:
- the answer arriving after the client stopped waiting,
- a client restart between request and answer, losing the blinding state,
- a transport drop, or a client defect.

This happened in a live run: the community enrolled the vetter, the client dropped the answer, and the vetter was locked out for the month. The client defect is fixed in OpenVTC/openvtc#456 and the error wording in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1961, but the protocol still has no way back. The only workaround is for the operator to republish the criterion with the next period live early, which changes the requirements digest for everyone.

## Proposal
Allow the community to **re-issue to the same bound identifier** within a label, as an idempotent recovery, instead of refusing:

- A second `pcs-root` request under a label the member is already enrolled in, **with the same `id`** (the PCS identifier recorded at first enrolment, which the spec already requires to be stable across labels), MAY be answered with a fresh issuance over the new blinded request, instead of `alreadyEnrolled`.
- Every check that applies today still applies: live vetter grant, signed request, `issuedAt` freshness.
- A request under an already-enrolled label with a **different** `id` is still refused (`alreadyEnrolled`, or the existing identifier-mismatch refusal).

**Why this looks safe for counting:**
- The member's `id` is unchanged, so any credential they end up holding derives the same per-label tags as the first.
- A member can't use two credentials to appear as two vetters: distinctness is by tag, and the tags are the same.
- What this gives up is the guarantee that the community issued exactly one credential object, not that it counts each member once.

Suite authors should confirm that re-issuing over a new blinded request with the same `id` produces identical tags and leaks nothing linkable. A rate limit per member per label (e.g. at most N re-issues) would bound abuse.

**Alternative**, if re-issuance is judged unsafe: define an administrator task to clear a member's enrolment for a label (audited), so an operator can unblock a vetter without republishing.

## Requested change
- Amend the "Two further checks" paragraph and the `alreadyEnrolled` entry in `errorCodes` to allow same-`id` re-issuance (or define the admin clear task).
- Add a short "Recovering a lost answer" note so client implementers know retrying with the same `id` is the recovery path.

title: fix(vtc): an administrator may withdraw a member's registry consent, never grant it
body:
A member's consent to be published in the community's trust registry is their own privacy decision, given with `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit` and copied onto the member record as `publish_consent`. Until now `vtc/members/update` let an administrator set it either way, so an administrator could publish someone who had said no.

Product decision: **an administrator may only lower it.**

## Changes

- **`vtc/members/update`** (`vtc-service/src/routes/members/update.rs`; the only writer of `publish_consent` outside admission, and it serves both the signed Trust Task and the legacy `PATCH /v1/members/{did}` shim):
  - `publishConsent: true` for a member whose consent is `false` is refused with **`vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden`** (400). The refusal happens before anything is written, so the request's other fields are not applied either. The message says that consent comes from the member's own `registryConsent`.
  - `true → false` (a takedown) still works. Re-stating the current value, either `true` or `false`, is a no-op and is not refused.
- **Error code.** `vtc/members/update/0.1` declares no code for this (I checked `dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf` and trust-tasks-rs 0.27.7), so it is minted under the task's own namespace per SPEC §8.5:
  - The code is `vta_sdk::protocols::members::MEMBER_UPDATE_ERR_CONSENT_GRANT_FORBIDDEN`, following the precedent of `JOIN_REQUEST_SUBMIT_ERR_REQUEST_ALREADY_OPEN`. This is an additive `pub const`.
  - It is registered in `CONSUMER_MINTED` in `error_code_census.rs`, which fails the day the spec declares it.
- **Registry sync.** No code change was needed. A `MemberUpdated` naming `publishConsent` enqueues `UpdateMember`, and `resolve` returns `Withdraw` for a published member without consent. That **deletes** the record; it is not `Departed`, because the member has not left. This PR adds an end-to-end integration test through the route for it.
- **Admin console.** It only *displays* publish consent (`plugins/members.tsx`), and nothing in it offers to set consent, so nothing changed there.
- **Docs.**
  - `docs/03-vtc/trust-registry.md`: describes consent as lower-only. The upgrade section no longer tells operators to `PATCH {"publishConsent": true}` for members admitted before #1682, since that is refused now. Such a member gives consent by rejoining.
  - `trust-tasks/members/update/1.0/spec.md`: lists the new error.
  - Comments in `registry/{mod,syncer,tail}.rs`.

## Tests

- **Unit tests (signed door, `trust_tasks::tests`):**
  - `update_refuses_to_grant_registry_consent`
  - `update_withdraws_registry_consent_and_accepts_a_no_op`
  - Two existing tests that set `publishConsent: true` on a non-consenting member now use another field.
- **Integration tests (`tests/it/members_crud.rs`):**
  - `the_update_task_refuses_to_grant_registry_consent`
  - `the_update_task_withdraws_registry_consent`
  - `restating_registry_consent_is_a_no_op`
  - `withdrawn_registry_consent_unpublishes_the_member`: publish, admin withdraw, tick. The mock registry and the local mirror both lose the record, and a re-grant is refused.
- **Run locally:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2861 passed
  - `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`
  - vta-sdk tests under the CI workspace invocation: 1236 passed
  - `cargo test -p vta-sdk --doc`

## Open questions

- Should `vtc/members/update/0.1` declare `consentGrantForbidden` upstream? If it does, the census entry flips to the generated constant.
- Members admitted before #1682 who want to be listed must now rejoin. A member-driven way to set consent without rejoining (for example a member-signed self-update) may be wanted. This PR refuses a grant even when the caller is the member themselves, following the decision that a join submit is the only source of consent.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the refusal precedes every write
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): new error code only. The admin UI and openvtc do not send `publishConsent` (checked)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): a distinct code and message for this refusal (R6.4)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(vtc): a hidden-vetting refusal says "validation error" once
body:
## What

The `pcs-root`, `pcs-tokens` and `event-mode` refusals (`vtc-service/src/vetting/pcs_tasks.rs`: `root_error`, `tokens_error`, `event_error`) work in three steps:

1. Render the `AppError` to text, for example "validation error: did:… already holds a credential under `vetter/2026-10`".
2. Match that text to pick the declared code.
3. Wrap the same text in a new `AppError::Validation`.

Step 3 adds the prefix a second time, so a vetter saw:

> validation error: validation error: did:webvh:…:devote-hotel already holds a credential under `vetter/2026-10`

The declared refusal now carries the store's own reason under one `validation error:` prefix (`declared_reason`). Declared codes and HTTP statuses are unchanged, since every declared refusal is still a `Validation`. Unit test: `vetting::pcs_tasks::tests::a_declared_refusal_names_its_reason_once`.

## Context: the live failure this came from (fixed in openvtc)

The enrolment lock-out that surfaced this message was a client bug, fixed in OpenVTC/openvtc#456. The client dropped every `spec/vtc/vetting/…#response` before routing it, so the community's `pcs-root` answer was never opened. The vetter then asked again and was refused `alreadyEnrolled`. The service behaved as pcs-root/0.1 specifies.

## Flagged, not changed: no way back for a vetter that lost its enrolment answer

pcs-root/0.1 §Authorization makes "this member has not already enrolled under this label" a MUST. A member whose client lost the answer therefore cannot be re-issued under the same label, and no admin path clears an enrolment row (`pcs-enrol:<did>` in `vetting_pcs_issue_ks`).

Re-issuing to the **same bound identifier** looks safe cryptographically:

- `issue_root` verifies the request against `id`, which is derived from the vetter's `usk`.
- So a second credential is over the same key and yields the same tags.
- It therefore cannot count the member twice, which is the rule's stated purpose.

Doing this is still a spec change (an amendment to pcs-root/0.1 or a 0.2), not something to do here. I'm raising it for the spec owners rather than inventing a task. Until then, recovery means publishing the next class period (below).

## Operator workaround for first-vtc today

The vetter `devote-hotel` is recorded as enrolled under `vetter/2026-10` and holds no credential. To let it enrol now:

- Re-publish hidden vetting for `vetted-member` (console, `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1`, or `POST /v1/vetting/hidden`) with `livePeriods: ["2026-11", "2026-10"]`.
- Keep `liveTokenLabels: ["token/2026-10"]`.
- Re-send `dripPerTick: 10`, plus `tickLength` and `events` if they were set. Publish replaces them, and `dripPerTick` defaults to 3.

The vetter (running OpenVTC with #456) then enrols under `vetter/2026-11` on its next pass. Vetters already enrolled under `vetter/2026-10` are unaffected, because that label stays live. The criterion's requirements digest changes with the republish, so any proof built against the old digest must be rebuilt (none existed in this test).

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets --features vetting-pcs -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --lib pcs_tasks`: pass.
- `--test it hidden_vetting` (13 tests): pass.
- The module is gated on `vetting-pcs`, so the default build is untouched.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): not touched
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off (R1.4): not touched
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): not touched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): not touched
- [x] New/changed wire types: none (message text only)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): not touched
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): the refusal text is now readable (R6.4)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" (R2.1): not applicable
- [x] Deviations: none

title: fix(vetting): a vetter hears hidden-vetting answers, keeps a late one, and sees its token balance
body:
## What was wrong

Live test against `first-vtc` (PCS ZKP, hidden vetting on `vetted-member`): a vetter pressing Enter on the attest form got

> Cannot attest: this community's `org.openvtc.hidden-vetting` parameters could not be read: vetter is at capacity; next free token from tick 0

after the activity log said "No answer from … about your hidden-vetting credential within 30 seconds". A later enrolment was refused `pcs-root:alreadyEnrolled`.

**Root cause.** `openvtc_core::vetting::inbound::may_claim` gates which inbound types reach the vetting router. It claimed `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vetting/…`, but hidden vetting's community tasks live under `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/vetting/…`. So every `#response` to `pcs-root`, `pcs-tokens`, `event-mode` and `pcs-challenge` was dropped before `inbound::handle` saw it. The transport gate passes them and `handle` has arms for them, so nothing logged. (The "Inbound DIDComm" log line only appears when a message changes config, so the drop left no trace.) Refusals arrive as `trust-task-error` and were claimed, which is why refusals worked and successes didn't. The Party-fixture tests call `handle` directly, so they never exercised the gate.

Chain of events: the vetter asks to enrol. The community issues the credential and records "enrolled under `vetter/2026-10`". The answer is dropped. After 30 s the question expires ("no answer"). The next pass asks again, the community refuses `alreadyEnrolled` (one credential per member per label, pcs-root/0.1), and the vetter has no credential and no tokens for the rest of the month. "tick 0" was never a tick mismatch. `hidden::attest` called `engine.accept(None, 0)`, and the `0` was a placeholder that the capacity error echoed back.

## What changed

- **Claim the four hidden-vetting answer types** (`inbound::is_hidden_vetting_answer_type`). Regression tests: `claim_tests`, plus a dispatch-level test `a_hidden_vetting_answer_reaches_the_question_it_answers` that sends an enveloped answer through `process_inbound_message`.
- **Late answers are kept.** Each enrolment's blinding state is now held per request (`VettingBook::pending_enrolments`, in memory, bounded to 8) past the 30 s reply window, and a late `pcs-root` answer is matched on it. A late `pcs-tokens` answer is taken while the wallet still holds its serials. After a successful enrolment the drip runs at once (`vetter_refresh_due`) instead of at the next pass, which can be an hour away.
- **Bounded, backed-off retry (R1.4).** An unanswered enrolment or draw sets `retry_at` at 1, 2, 4 … min, capped at 1 h (`HiddenVetterState::unanswered_at`). The pacer is pulled forward to it. The status line says "Asking again at 15:31 UTC; an answer that arrives before then is still taken" instead of "Try again later". Any answer resets the backoff. The retry of a non-idempotent enrolment is safe because the earlier request's blinding is kept, so whichever answer arrives is opened.
- **A lost enrolment stops the asking.** Two cases mean the community has enrolled us and we cannot open the answer: an answer arrives whose blinding is gone (a restart in between), or the community refuses `alreadyEnrolled` while we hold no credential. Both set `lost_enrolment`. The schedule then stops asking under that label, the vetter is told it can attest from the next label, and the `h` view says so.
- **Errors (R6.4).** `HiddenError::NotEnrolled` and `HiddenError::NoToken` replace `Unreadable` ("parameters could not be read") for these two states. "Cannot attest" now says which state applies, that nothing was sent, and when it changes, for example "0 tokens — next drip due Wed 07 Oct 00:00 UTC".
- **Token balance.** For each PCS ZKP community the desk header now shows tokens held and when that changes: next drip, request in flight, no answer with the retry time, refused, or lost enrolment. It warns when live tickets admit more requests than the tokens held. The attest form shows the same line beside PCS ZKP, plus `e` (event mode) where the community publishes event tiers. All of it is read from the engine and book (`VettingBook::hidden_outlook`), the same data the `h` view uses.
- **Ticket gate.** `issue_ticket` refuses a ticket for a PCS ZKP community while the vetter holds no token or no credential there, and says when that changes.

## Operator note (deployed first-vtc)

The vetter `devote-hotel` is enrolled under `vetter/2026-10` at the community, and its credential was lost client-side. Per pcs-root/0.1 ("this member has not already enrolled under this label" is a MUST), the community will not re-issue it. Even with this fix, that vetter cannot attest at first-vtc until it enrols under a new label. See the VTI PR for the recovery options.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The enrolment blinding is kept until the answer arrives; the served tick is recorded only on its answer.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Enrolment retries back off, and earlier requests' answers stay openable, so a retry cannot strand an issued credential. A known `alreadyEnrolled` stops retries.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Capacity is no longer reported as unreadable parameters.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). A restart drops the blinding (by design). A late answer is then recorded as a lost enrolment, not silently ignored.
- [x] Deviations: none

## Tests

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`: all pass.

New: `claim_tests::the_community_answers_to_hidden_vetting_are_claimed`, `a_hidden_vetting_answer_reaches_the_question_it_answers`, `an_enrolment_answered_after_its_question_timed_out_is_still_taken` (real blind issuance through `Issuer::issue_root`), `a_draw_answered_after_its_question_timed_out_is_still_taken` (real drip), `an_enrolment_answer_that_cannot_be_opened_stops_the_asking_until_the_next_label`, `already_enrolled_without_a_credential_stops_the_asking`, `attesting_without_a_credential_or_a_token_says_which`, `an_unanswered_question_is_asked_again_backed_off_and_bounded`, `an_unanswered_question_brings_the_next_pass_forward`, `the_token_line_says_what_is_held_and_when_it_changes`, `no_ticket_is_issued_for_requests_that_cannot_be_attested`, `the_desk_header_warns_of_tickets_beyond_the_tokens_held`, `the_token_balance_is_shown_on_the_desk_and_the_attest_form`.

title: fix(vetting): a vetter hears hidden-vetting answers, keeps a late one, and sees its token balance (#456)
body:
fix(vetting): a vetter hears hidden-vetting answers, keeps a late one, and sees its token balance (#456)

The community's answers to pcs-root, pcs-tokens, event-mode and
pcs-challenge (`trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/vetting/...#response`) never
reached the vetting router: `inbound::may_claim` only claimed
`spec/vetting/...`. A vetter's enrolment was issued by the community,
dropped here, reported as "no answer within 30 seconds", and every later
request was refused `alreadyEnrolled` - leaving no credential and no
token for the rest of the month.

- Claim the four hidden-vetting answer types.
- Keep each enrolment's blinding state past the reply window, and take a
  late enrolment or draw answer; draw at once after enrolling.
- Back off an unanswered enrolment or draw (1, 2, 4 ... min, capped at

title: fix: an ended join can be applied for again from Communities; the status says when a persona is online
body:
Two decisions from review, both following up #450.

## 1. Ended joins reappear under Joining
#450 hid an application whenever any membership record existed for its community and persona, including ended ones. Now:
- **Live membership (Pending/Active):** still hidden; the membership row covers the join.
- **Ended (Rejected/Withdrawn/Left/Removed/Expired):** listed under *Joining*, with the outcome in front of where it stands, e.g. `rejected last time — apply again · 1 of 1 statement — ready to join`. Enter opens the application's journey, as for any Joining row.

## 2. "No community yet · persona online"
- **The problem:** the indicator spoke only for community sessions. An applicant being vetted, with no membership but a connected persona listener, saw "No active community" and couldn't tell whether their vetters' messages could reach them.
- **New status:** `MediatorStatus::PersonaOnline` is shown as "No community yet · persona online", in green, in the top bar, Help/Status and the Inbox.
- **The rule:** `aggregate_status(sessions, persona_online)`:
  - a session up → Connected
  - sessions but none up → Connecting
  - no sessions and a persona listener up → PersonaOnline
  - otherwise → NoActiveCommunity
- **How it's tracked:** the loop records every listener's connected state (`ConnectionState::online_listeners`) from the listener status stream, not only community sessions.

## Tests
- New `an_application_whose_join_ended_is_listed_to_apply_again`.
- `no_community_session_reads_no_active_community_not_connecting` is extended with the persona-online case.
- CHANGELOG entries under `[0.5.0]`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`: all pass.

title: feat(review): add reproducible specification pressure-test records
body:
## Summary

Adds a bounded, machine-verifiable workflow for pressure-testing a specification using RAHP.

This introduces a reproducible review-record contract that:

- pins the target to an immutable source revision;
- records a stable assessment identity and finding identities;
- references risks from the existing RAHP risk corpus;
- separates the control plane in which remediation belongs from the current status of the finding;
- requires explicit resolution information for resolved, accepted-risk, out-of-scope, and superseded findings; and
- validates review records and associated RAHP risk references.

Addresses part of #9.

## What is included

- `review/spec-review.schema.json`
  - JSON Schema for specification review records.
- `review/validate_spec_review.py`
  - validates the schema, immutable target revision, finding identities, and references to `risks.yaml`.
- `review/examples/minimal-review.yaml`
  - small valid example.
- negative fixtures covering:
  - mutable source revision;
  - unknown RAHP risk reference; and
  - resolved finding without resolution evidence.
- `tests/test_spec_review.py`
  - positive and falsification-oriented validation coverage.
- `docs/pressure-testing-a-spec.md`
  - task-oriented workflow for conducting and recording a specification pressure-test.
- README discovery link.

## Design decisions

### Source revisions are immutable

A review record identifies the exact source revision evaluated. Branch names such as `main` are rejected because they can move after the review has been performed.

### Control plane and finding status are separate

The record distinguishes:

- **where** a control or remediation belongs, such as specification, governance, implementation guidance, runtime control, or operational policy; and
- **what happened** to the finding, such as open, resolved, accepted risk, out of scope, or superseded.

This avoids combining two different governance propositions into a single disposition vocabulary.

### Validation is not an assurance conclusion

A valid review record establishes that the review metadata is well formed, reproducibly source-pinned, and internally consistent.

It does **not** mean that:

- the reviewed specification has passed assurance;
- CI success constitutes an assurance conclusion;
- missing evidence is equivalent to resolution; or
- a risk reference proves that the referenced risk has been realised.

## Validation

The implementation includes positive and negative test coverage for:

- a valid minimal review;
- missing immutable revision;
- mutable branch name used as revision;
- duplicate finding identifiers;
- unknown RAHP risk references;
- invalid control-plane values;
- resolved findings without resolution evidence;
- accepted-risk findings without the required reference; and
- the supplied negative fixtures.

Local validation:

```text
Ran 11 tests

OK
```

The valid example also passes the review-record validator.

## Scope

This PR intentionally does **not** import the downstream RAHP assurance system wholesale.

Excluded from this tranche are:

- the downstream assurance controller;
- specialist routing;
- DPIP integration;
- Interop Lab machinery;
- terminal PASS/FAIL state machinery;
- automated reassessment;
- the full downstream lineage model; and
- repository-wide structural reorganisation.

Those capabilities require separate review and should only move upstream when their contracts and evidence are independently mature.

## Provenance

This capability is adapted from implementation and assurance work developed in the downstream `sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit` repository.

Relevant originating work includes:

- `sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#36`: portable assessment and finding lineage foundation;
- `sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#49`: source-pinned evidence findings;
- `sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#227`: typed and source-pinned assurance handoff;
- `sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#757`: independent-review working pack and falsification-oriented readiness gate; and
- `sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#761`: adopter-oriented end-to-end workflow.

The implementation in this PR has been adapted to the upstream repository's current architecture and scope rather than copied wholesale. Acceptance of this PR would make the resulting upstream capability authoritative for this repository; the downstream implementation remains an independent incubation and evidence surface.

title: fix(join): a join refused over its PCS challenge ends with the reason, not Pending
body:
## Problem
With hidden vetting (PCS ZKP), a community refuses a join **submission** when the challenge its proof is bound to:
- has expired,
- was already used,
- was never issued, or
- doesn't match.

These are VTI #1954's `vtc/join-requests/submit:challenge{Expired,AlreadyUsed,NotIssued,Mismatch}`. No request stays open at the community. In `handle_join_trust_task_error` those codes fell into the "malformed / transient" branch, so the join was left **Pending** indefinitely, waiting for a decision nobody was taking. The only trace was a `warn!` line.

## Fix
- **`vta-sdk` 0.63.1 → 0.63.2**, which has the four constants (`JOIN_REQUEST_SUBMIT_ERR_CHALLENGE_*`).
- **`join_refusal_reason` knows the four codes,** so `is_join_denial_code` treats them like `notAccepting` / `criterionUnknown`: the join ends (`Rejected`, session inactivated) with a reason.
  - The reason is the community's own message when it sends one, as #1954's server does. Otherwise it's OpenVTC's sentence for each code. `challengeMismatch` is worded as a likely OpenVTC fault.
  - Joining again asks for a fresh challenge automatically (#442), so the remedy works.
- **CHANGELOG:** entry under `[0.5.0]`.

## Tests
- `a_v0_3_submit_refusal_ends_the_join_with_a_reason` now also covers the four challenge codes: each ends the join, and the reason says what happened.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo doc -D warnings`: all pass.

title: fix(join): a join refused over its PCS challenge ends with the reason, not Pending (#454)
body:
fix(join): a join refused over its PCS challenge ends with the reason, not Pending (#454)

A community that hides its vetters refuses the whole join submission when the
challenge its zero-knowledge proof is bound to has expired, was already used,
was never issued, or does not match - and keeps no request open. Those codes
fell into the 'transient failure' branch, so the join stayed Pending forever,
waiting for a decision nobody was taking, with only a warn line in the log.

They now end the join (Rejected, session inactivated) with the community's own
message or, when it gives none, OpenVTC's sentence for each; joining again asks
for a fresh challenge on its own (#442). Bumps vta-sdk to 0.63.2, which names
the four codes (VTI #1954).

title: fix: responsive while a new persona connects; the vetter side keeps itself current
body:
Small fixes left after #447–#451, plus the start-up miss you hit as a vetter.

## 1. Making a persona during a join no longer holds the page
- **The problem:** `mint_persona_inline` awaited `start_persona_listener` inside the join loop, which reads no keys. After #447 that wait was bounded to 30 seconds, but only Ctrl-C reached it.
- **The fix:** a new `spawn_persona_listener` reads the listener spec from the config, then connects on its own task. The page answers Esc and F10 at once. The submit still waits, bounded, for the socket (`await_persona_online`), which is where being online matters.
- **Core change:** `add_listener` now takes a **per-listener-id lock** (`MessagingInner::connect_locks`) for the whole connect, and returns early if the listener is already up once it holds it.
  - A listener is registered only after it connects, so without this the background connect and the submit's own `add_listener` could each open a socket for one DID. The mediator allows one per DID.
  - The existing contract is unchanged: callers that mean to replace a listener remove it first.

## 2. The vetter side keeps itself current
You hit this as a vetter: the log showed `Could not send — try again: no listener installed for …devote-hotel` at start-up. The start-up refresh from #449 ran before the vetter's listener had connected, and nothing retried for an hour.
- **When a request arrives:** `inbound::take_request` sets `VettingBook::vetter_refresh_due`, a field that's never saved. The loop's 5-second sweep takes it and runs `RefreshVetterSide`.
- **When asking fails:** a refresh that can't send schedules a retry on the sweep, bounded by `VETTER_REFRESH_RETRIES` (12, about a minute). A refresh that sends resets the count.
- **When the answer arrives:** a manifest that newly publishes PCS ZKP parameters (`hidden_published` changes) sets the flag too, so enrolment follows immediately rather than at the next refresh.
- **The log line:** a failed background requirements request now reads "Could not yet ask … what it requires (…) — asking again shortly." instead of "try again".

## 3. No "Connecting..." flash without a community
The start-up status is `NoActiveCommunity` when there's no live membership, instead of `Connecting` until the seed corrects it.

## Tests
- New core test `a_request_on_the_desk_makes_the_vetter_side_due_a_refresh`, which also checks the flag is never serialized.
- **Not covered by a test:**
  - the retry and enrol-on-publish paths, which need a signed manifest reply matched to a pending query for a vetter;
  - the connect lock, which needs a mediator.

  The changes are small, and each is commented at its site.
- CHANGELOG entries under `[0.5.0]`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo doc -D warnings`: all pass.

title: vta-service-v0.54.0
body:
### Added

- **keys**: Serve keys/sign-sshsig — git commit signing without key export ([#1957](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1957))

did-git-sign exported its persona's key with keys/export-secret on every
  commit, because keys/sign cannot produce an SSHSIG signature: it frames
  caller bytes under the opaque-signing domain tag (VTI-VTA-003/007), which
  is the point of that hardening.

  keys/sign-sshsig/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #732, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.6) takes a
  digest, a namespace and a hash algorithm. The VTA builds the
  PROTOCOL.sshsig signed data itself and signs it as ProtocolDefined, so the
  signature verifies as an SSHSIG statement in that namespace and as nothing
  else. It is gated on a new constrained capability under VTI-VTA-007,
  `sign-sshsig` (registered upstream as signSshsig), derived wherever `sign`
  is; `sign` is accepted in its place, and an entry narrowed to sign-sshsig
  alone cannot reach the generic oracle. Scope, the context signing policy
  and its daily quota apply through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, and
  the success is audited once as keys.sign-sshsig with the namespace and
  digest. The spec's declared codes are rendered: keys:invalidArgument for a
  digest of the wrong length or an algorithm the key cannot perform,
  keys/sign-sshsig:failedPrecondition for an inactive key.

title: vti-common-v0.38.0
body:
### Added

- **keys**: Serve keys/sign-sshsig — git commit signing without key export ([#1957](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1957))

did-git-sign exported its persona's key with keys/export-secret on every
  commit, because keys/sign cannot produce an SSHSIG signature: it frames
  caller bytes under the opaque-signing domain tag (VTI-VTA-003/007), which
  is the point of that hardening.

  keys/sign-sshsig/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #732, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.6) takes a
  digest, a namespace and a hash algorithm. The VTA builds the
  PROTOCOL.sshsig signed data itself and signs it as ProtocolDefined, so the
  signature verifies as an SSHSIG statement in that namespace and as nothing
  else. It is gated on a new constrained capability under VTI-VTA-007,
  `sign-sshsig` (registered upstream as signSshsig), derived wherever `sign`
  is; `sign` is accepted in its place, and an entry narrowed to sign-sshsig
  alone cannot reach the generic oracle. Scope, the context signing policy
  and its daily quota apply through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, and
  the success is audited once as keys.sign-sshsig with the namespace and
  digest. The spec's declared codes are rendered: keys:invalidArgument for a
  digest of the wrong length or an algorithm the key cannot perform,
  keys/sign-sshsig:failedPrecondition for an inactive key.

- **vtc**: Hidden vetting (PCS) is turned off, read back and run with events from the console ([#1956](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1956))

* feat(vtc): hidden vetting (PCS) is turned off, read back and run with events from the console

  Completes the console's hidden-vetting surface on top of #1955, with the
  three tasks trust-tasks-tf #729 specified (trust-tasks-rs 0.27.5):

  - `vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw/0.1` turns hidden vetting off for a criterion.
    Named vetting is untouched; enrolment rows and the spent-token ledger stay,
    so a later publish works with the same keys. Withdrawing a criterion with
    none is `withdrawn: false`, not an error.
  - `vtc/vetting/hidden/show/0.1` answers an administrator with the stored
    configuration — each event's `approvedBy` and `graceDays`, which the
    manifest leaves out — plus how many members are enrolled under each live
    vetter label and each event's demand against its floor. Counts only, never
    which members.
  - `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1` now holds the approval rules its draft
    states: a new or changed `approvedBy` must be the publishing signer
    (`approverNotSigner`) — it was an unchecked string, so an administrator
    could approve in anyone's name — and an approver who has asked to vet at the
    event is refused (`approverInEvent`). An approval already stored may be
    re-sent by anyone, so a re-publish keeps it.
  - Every publish and withdrawal is audited as `HiddenVettingChanged` (new
    `vti-common` audit variant; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`).



### Fixed

- **vtc**: Working in the admin console counts toward the idle timeout ([#1953](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1953))

The console signed out operators who were using it. The idle timeout
  (`auth.admin_idle_timeout`, 900s) is measured from `Session::last_seen`, and
  only a cookie-authenticated request through the `AuthClaims` extractor
  advanced it. Most of what the console sends is now a signed Trust Task
  document to `/v1/trust-tasks`, which authenticates by its proof and reads no
  session, so a busy operator stopped producing activity. Fifteen minutes after
  the last cookie-borne call the renewal was refused and the session-deadline
  watcher showed Login.

  Counting every signed document would be wrong the other way: the action
  badge, counts and banners post signed reads on timers, and an unattended tab
  would never time out. Only the console can tell input from a poll, so:

  - The console notes real input (pointerdown, keydown, wheel, touchstart) and
    sends `X-VTC-User-Activity` on a document posted within 60s of some
    (`admin-ui/src/lib/user-activity.ts`). Timers in an idle tab send none.
  - The route records activity only for a document that ran successfully, was
    verified as a known signer, and whose principal (the signer, or the
    administrator its console key acts for) owns the session the cookie names
    (`vti_common::auth::touch_cookie_session_for`, which authenticates the
    cookie exactly as the extractors do). A document signed by one identity
    cannot keep another's session alive, and a refused one counts for nothing.

  Renewals and timer-driven reads still never count, so the daemon still
  decides when an operator who walked away is signed out.

title: vta-sdk-v0.63.2
body:
### Added

- **keys**: Serve keys/sign-sshsig — git commit signing without key export ([#1957](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1957))

did-git-sign exported its persona's key with keys/export-secret on every
  commit, because keys/sign cannot produce an SSHSIG signature: it frames
  caller bytes under the opaque-signing domain tag (VTI-VTA-003/007), which
  is the point of that hardening.

  keys/sign-sshsig/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #732, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.6) takes a
  digest, a namespace and a hash algorithm. The VTA builds the
  PROTOCOL.sshsig signed data itself and signs it as ProtocolDefined, so the
  signature verifies as an SSHSIG statement in that namespace and as nothing
  else. It is gated on a new constrained capability under VTI-VTA-007,
  `sign-sshsig` (registered upstream as signSshsig), derived wherever `sign`
  is; `sign` is accepted in its place, and an entry narrowed to sign-sshsig
  alone cannot reach the generic oracle. Scope, the context signing policy
  and its daily quota apply through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, and
  the success is audited once as keys.sign-sshsig with the namespace and
  digest. The spec's declared codes are rendered: keys:invalidArgument for a
  digest of the wrong length or an algorithm the key cannot perform,
  keys/sign-sshsig:failedPrecondition for an inactive key.



### Fixed

- **vti-common**: The secret-Debug census knows hidden-vetting token labels are public ([#1958](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1958))

#1956 added `HiddenVettingChangedData.token_labels` (the hidden-vetting audit
  row), and the workspace census in `vta-sdk/tests/secret_debug_census.rs`
  flags any `Debug`-deriving field whose name contains "token". The field holds
  label names (`token/2026-10`, `token/event/<id>`) that every applicant and
  vetter reads from the join manifest, not tokens, so it joins NOT_SECRET with
  what it holds. This turned main's `Test (workspace)` job red.

- **vtc**: Say why a PCS challenge was refused ([#1954](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1954))

A hidden-vetting proof is bound to a single-use challenge the community
  issues over vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1, and the community spends it
  when the proof arrives. Every way that spend could fail - the challenge
  expired, was already used, was never issued, or is not the one the proof
  was built over - reached the applicant as one `malformedRequest` with the
  cause in a sentence. A client could not tell "you took too long" from
  "your proof was built over the wrong challenge", which is the difference
  between "try again" and "your client has a bug".

  Each failure is now a typed `ChallengeRefusal` that travels from
  `pcs_challenge::consume` through `pcs::decide`, the vetting facts and the
  criterion evaluation to the join spine, and goes out on the Trust Task
  path under a code of its own:

  - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeNotIssued` (details.reason `not_found`)
  - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeAlreadyUsed` (details.reason `gone`)
  - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeExpired` (details.reason `gone`,
    plus `details.expiredAt`)
  - `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeMismatch` (details.reason `conflict`)

  and the same four local parts under `vtc/join-requests/supplement:` when
  a supplement carries the proof. Neither specification declares a
  challenge code yet, so they are consumer-minted under the task's own slug
  (SPEC 8.5), as `requestAlreadyOpen` is; the constants live in
  `vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests` for clients to match on, and the
  error-code census lists them as consumer-minted so it fails the day the
  specification adopts them. Surfaces that carry no code keep the same 400
  `Validation`, now with a sentence that says which failure it was. The
  message never contains the challenge value.

  Single-use is unchanged: a submission still spends the challenge whether
  or not it is accepted, including on a mismatch. The row is now taken
  atomically (`take_raw`) rather than read then removed, and a spent marker
  holding no challenge - only the expiry - is left in its place so a second
  attempt is told "already used" rather than "never issued". An expired
  challenge is put back as it was so repeated attempts keep saying
  "expired". Both go at the retention sweep after `expires_at`, as the
  challenge always did; both writes are `insert_if_absent`, so a challenge
  asked for in the meantime is never overwritten. Each refusal is logged
  with its kind and the applicant, never the challenge.
