title: fix(join): read the current requirements on every join; mark named vetting as a disclosure
body:
## 1. The join page used a stale manifest
After joining against first-vtc, then turning on PCS ZKP there, the join page still said **Vetters: named**. The live manifest does carry `vetting.ext["org.openvtc.hidden-vetting"]`, and I checked that OpenVTC's full path parses it as hidden: `read_mode`, then `read_manifest` (0.3) → `learn_manifest_in` → `hidden_vetting()`. The cause was in `enter_community`:
- Once the book knew the community, `Knowledge::Vetting` / `NoVetting`, the page was built from the stored copy and **never asked again**.
- So a community that turned on hidden vetting, changed its requirements, or started vetting at all still showed what it said before.

**Fix:** a known community is re-read with `learn_over_http` on every join. That's the bounded REST read that needs nothing of us. It also adopts the new manifest into any application under way and records the signing keys. If it fails, the stored copy stands in and the activity log says "Could not read X's current requirements (…); showing what it said last time."

## 2. Named vetting is shown as a disclosure, PCS ZKP as protected
New `badges::vetters_named()` (orange **⚠ VETTERS NAMED**) and a green **✓ PCS ZKP** badge (it was purple). Each comes with `caution()` / `protected()` sentence styles and shared wording:

| | Named | PCS ZKP |
|---|---|---|
| Applicant | "the community will see which vetters vouched for you — each statement carries its vetter's DID" | "…learns that enough vetters vouched for you, not who they were" |
| Vetter | "your statement goes to the community with your DID on it — it will know you vouched for this person" | "your attestation is counted in a zero-knowledge proof — the community never learns it was you" |

**Shown on:**
- the join page ("How it protects you")
- Review and send
- the application's Vetters line
- the desk's "You are" line
- both journey titles (now always badged one way or the other)
- the **attest form, right above "I attest"**, where the vetter signs

## Tests
- Updated `the_page_says_whether_vetters_are_hidden_and_how_it_signs` (the named badge and wording).
- New `the_attest_form_says_whether_the_vetter_is_named`.
- CHANGELOG entries under `[0.5.0]`, which isn't published yet.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo doc -D warnings`: all pass.

title: fix(vtc): a departing member who was never published leaves no failed registry job
body:
When a member leaves with `purge`, the VTC queued a `DeleteMember` registry job unconditionally (`registry/syncer.rs` resolved it straight to `SyncAction::Delete`). For a member who never consented to publication, the registry has no record. It refused the delete with `taskFailed` (its answer for an unknown key), the VTC classified that as permanent, and the job failed on its first attempt. It then stayed in the console's Failed jobs until someone discarded it.

## Change
- **`DeleteMember` checks the mirror first**, as `MarkDeparted` already does.
  - With a mirror record, it deletes as before.
  - Without one, the new `SyncAction::DeleteIfPresent` reads the registry and deletes only if the record exists.
  - A transient read failure is retried.
  - A read the registry can't answer falls back to the delete. A purge is an erasure, so a mirror that lost a record must not leave the membership published.
- **`delete_member` treats the declared `registry/record/delete:notFound` as success**, the same tolerance `delete_trust_record` already has.
- **Console copy:** the Failed jobs text pointed at `vtc sync-jobs retry` on a stopped daemon. It now points at the Retry and Discard buttons beside it, and says when discarding is right.
- **Stale doc comment** on `sweep_failed_sync_jobs` corrected: a permanent refusal fails a job immediately.

## Tests
New `registry::syncer` tests:
- `deleting_a_member_who_was_never_published_completes_without_a_delete`: one read, no delete, queue empty.
- `a_purge_deletes_a_record_the_mirror_lost`.
- `a_refused_read_falls_back_to_the_delete`.

Run locally:
- `registry::`: 113/113.
- admin-ui: vitest 807/807, `tsc -b` clean.
- clippy `-D warnings` (vtc-service): clean.
- The full vtc-service suite is running locally.

## Not here
The trust registry answers an unknown key with the generic `taskFailed` instead of its declared `registry/record/delete:notFound` (`affinidi-trust-registry-rs`, `map_repo_err`). That fix belongs in that repo.

title: feat(did-git-sign): the VTA signs commits; the key never leaves it
body:
did-git-sign exported the persona's Ed25519 seed with keys/export-secret
on every commit and signed locally. It now sends the VTA the commit's
SHA-512 over keys/sign-sshsig/0.1: the VTA builds the SSHSIG signed data
itself, signs it, and returns the raw signature, which is checked against
the key's public half (keys/show) and armoured here. A credential can
then be narrowed to the sign-sshsig capability, so a stolen one signs
commits until revoked and never takes the key.

did-git-sign.signer (or DID_GIT_SIGN_SIGNER) chooses: auto (default) —
the VTA signs, and a VTA without the task falls back to the export with a
warning; vta — never export; export — the old behaviour. init, verify and
health read the public key instead of exporting the key; verify makes its
test signature through the configured signer, and health shows it.

vgi-core gains sshsig_message_hash, sshsig_signed_data and
assemble_ssh_signature; create_ssh_signature is built from them and
unchanged in output (a remote signature assembles byte-equal to a local
one). README and runbook describe the modes and the narrowing.

Depends on nothing unreleased: it calls `keys/sign-sshsig` through the published vta-sdk's `dispatch_trust_task_document`, and a VTA that answers `methodNotFound` gets the export fallback (under `auto`). The task is specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#732 (merged); the VTA side is in a VTI PR that follows.

Tests: `cargo test -p did-git-sign -p vgi-core`, `cargo clippy -p did-git-sign --all-targets -D warnings`. New: remote signature assembles byte-equal to local; a signature in another namespace / over the bare digest / by another key is refused before armouring; signer-mode parsing.

title: feat(vtc): hidden vetting (PCS) is turned off, read back and run with events from the console
body:
Follow-up to #1955. It implements the tasks specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#729 (`trust-tasks-rs` 0.27.5), so every admin-side part of PCS onboarding can be configured from the console.

## Server (`vetting-pcs`)

- **`vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw/0.1`:** removes a criterion's stored parameters and republishes it without them.
  - Named vetting is untouched.
  - Enrolments and the spent-token ledger stay, so turning it back on works with the same keys.
  - Withdrawing a criterion that has none answers `withdrawn: false`, not an error.
- **`vtc/vetting/hidden/show/0.1`:** answers administrators (`VettingManage`) with:
  - the stored configuration, including the `approvedBy` and `graceDays` the manifest omits;
  - `enrolledVetters` per live vetter label;
  - `eventStatus` for each event: `groupSize`, `groupFloor`, `approved`, `live`.

  Counts only. A test asserts no vetter DID appears in the answer.
- **`hidden/publish/0.1` approval rules:**
  - a new or changed `approvedBy` must equal the signer, otherwise `approverNotSigner`. It was an unchecked free string before;
  - an approver who has asked to vet at the event is refused with `approverInEvent`;
  - an unchanged stored approval may be re-sent by any admin, so a re-publish keeps it.
- **Audit:** a new `AuditEvent::HiddenVettingChanged` (vti-common; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is additive). One row per publish and per withdrawal, recording what changed, never a reason.
- **Responses:** both new tasks are built as JSON and read through the generated `Response` types, so a non-conforming answer fails instead of shipping.
- **Helpers:**
  - `pcs_event::has_asked` reports whether a member asked to vet at an event;
  - `pcs_issue::enrolled_counts` counts enrolments per label.

## Console

The PCS section on a criterion's card gains:
- **Turn off hidden vetting**, shown when the build serves `withdraw`.
- **Enrolment counts** beside each vetter label.
- **An events table:** vetters asked against the floor, the approver ("you" when it is the viewer), and the state (Needs approval / Waiting for vetters / Approver is vetting at it / Open / Closed).
- **Event controls:**
  - **Approve**, in the viewer's own DID;
  - **Remove**, which also drops the event's token label;
  - **Add an event** (name, dates, grace days, floor ≥ 2, a tier and its rate), which makes `token/event/<id>` live.

Every edit is a `republish` from `show`'s stored configuration, so a drip-rate change or a label roll keeps every event and approval. A build without `show` keeps #1955's read-only handling of criteria with events.

Turning PCS on for a second criterion shows a warning: vetters enrol and draw under the first one (`pcs_tasks::config_for`).

`docs/03-vtc/vetting.md` gains a "Hidden vetting (PCS)" section.

## Tests

- `hidden_vetting_tasks` (`--features vetting-pcs`), 11/11 locally:
  - `an_event_approval_names_its_approver_and_never_one_of_its_vetters` covers approving in another admin's name, an admin vetter approving their own event, and another admin re-publishing a stored approval.
  - `hidden_vetting_turns_off_and_shows_what_it_stores` covers the declared codes, show before and after publish (stored approvals, counts, no vetter DID), withdraw twice, and that exactly 2 audit rows are written.
- The error-code census has witnesses for the four new codes.
- `trust_task_manifest`: `withdraw` and `show` join `FEATURE_GATED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`.
- `HiddenVettingCard.test.tsx`, 12/12: counts, Approve payload (stored events kept, `approvedBy` = viewer), drip change keeps another admin's approval, add event with its label, remove event, turn off, and the earlier no-`show` paths.
- Clippy `-D warnings` is clean in both builds (default workspace, and `vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`). Fmt clean.
- The full suites (vtc-service with and without `vetting-pcs`, vti-common, admin-ui) are still running locally; results will follow in a comment.

## Lockfile

`cargo update -p trust-tasks-rs --precise 0.27.5` also moved three existing edges within ranges those crates already allow:
- `data-encoding-macro-internal` → `syn 3`;
- `pgp` and `serde-saphyr` → `base64 0.22`.

No new packages.

title: vtc/join-requests submit & supplement: error codes for a refused PCS challenge
body:
## Summary
A hidden-vetting (PCS zero-knowledge) join submission carries a proof bound to a single-use challenge, which the community issues over `vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1`. Neither `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.2, 0.3) nor `vtc/join-requests/supplement` defines an error code for the ways that challenge can be refused. Implementations therefore fall back to `malformedRequest` or a generic validation error. The applicant can't tell an expired challenge from an already-spent one, or either from a client bug.

This proposes four task-specific codes for each of the two tasks, under the task's own name as SPEC §8.5 permits.

## Proposed `errorCodes` additions
For `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.3, and 0.2 if it is still maintained):

```yaml
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeNotIssued
    meaning: The submission's hidden-vetting proof is bound to a challenge, but the community holds no challenge for the applicant's DID — none was requested, or it expired and has since been discarded. The applicant requests a new challenge over vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge, builds the proof over it, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeAlreadyUsed
    meaning: The challenge the proof is bound to was spent by an earlier submission. Challenges are single-use. The applicant requests a new one, rebuilds the proof, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeExpired
    meaning: The challenge the proof is bound to is past its validity window. The details MAY carry `expiredAt`. The applicant requests a new one, rebuilds the proof, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeMismatch
    meaning: The proof is bound to a challenge other than the one the community issued to this applicant, typically one it replaced when the applicant asked again. The current challenge is spent by this attempt. The applicant requests a new one, rebuilds the proof, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
```

`vtc/join-requests/supplement` gets the same four codes, as `vtc/join-requests/supplement:challenge…`, for a supplement carrying the proof.

`retryable: false` is intended: retrying the *same* document can't succeed. Recovery is a new challenge and a new proof, which is a new submission.

## Why each one matters to an applicant
All four have the same remedy, but they say different things:
- **`challengeExpired` / `challengeNotIssued`:** usually time. The person was slow, or the client asked too early.
- **`challengeAlreadyUsed`:** a resubmit or a race.
- **`challengeMismatch`:** usually a client defect, such as reusing an old challenge after asking again. A client should report it as such, not as something the person did.

## Related notes for the spec text (non-normative suggestions)
- **"Discard on use":** an implementation may keep a value-free spent marker until the challenge's expiry, so a repeat attempt reports `challengeAlreadyUsed` rather than `challengeNotIssued`. The spec could say whether that's permitted. The challenge value itself must still be discarded.
- **Multiple hidden-vetting criteria:** when a community publishes more than one and the submission names none, the first criterion checked spends the challenge. Clients should name the criterion (`criterion`, 0.3) on hidden-vetting submissions.

## Reference implementation
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1954 implements these codes in `vtc-service`. That includes the `details` shapes (`reason` marker, plus `expiredAt` for expiry) and an error-code census test that will fail once the spec defines the codes, prompting a switch to the generated constants.

title: fix(vtc): say why a PCS challenge was refused
body:
## What

A hidden-vetting (PCS) proof is bound to a single-use challenge issued over `vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1`, and the community spends it when the proof arrives. Before this change every way that spend could fail went out as one `malformedRequest` (`"validation error: hidden vetting: ..."`). A client could not tell "you took too long" from "your proof was built over the wrong challenge".

Now each failure is a typed `ChallengeRefusal` (`vtc-service/src/vetting/challenge_refusal.rs`). It travels `pcs_challenge::consume` → `pcs::decide` (`DecideError`) → `vetting_facts` (`FactsError`) → `CriterionRefusal` → `SubmitRefusal` / `SupplementRefusal`, and the Trust Task handlers answer it under its own code.

## What the client sees

A `trust-task-error` document with `payload.code`, `payload.message` (an English sentence naming the remedy, never the challenge value) and `payload.details.reason` (the generic marker a code-unaware client reads back into a typed `VtaError`):

| code | meaning | `details` |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeNotIssued` | the community holds no challenge for this applicant: none was requested, or it expired and was swept | `{"reason":"not_found"}` |
| `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeAlreadyUsed` | an earlier submission already spent it | `{"reason":"gone"}` |
| `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeExpired` | its window had closed | `{"reason":"gone","expiredAt":"<RFC 3339>"}` |
| `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeMismatch` | the proof is bound to a different challenge, usually an older one replaced by a newer request (this attempt spends the current one) | `{"reason":"conflict"}` |

The same four local parts apply under `vtc/join-requests/supplement:` when a supplement carries the proof. Constants: `vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests::JOIN_REQUEST_{SUBMIT,SUPPLEMENT}_ERR_CHALLENGE_{NOT_ISSUED,ALREADY_USED,EXPIRED,MISMATCH}`. The remedy is the same for all four: request a new challenge, build the proof over it, and submit again. Surfaces that carry no code (REST, legacy problem-report) still get the same 400 `Validation`, and its message now names the failure.

## Spec

Neither `vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3` nor `supplement/0.1` declares a challenge code, so these are **consumer-minted under the task's own slug** (SPEC §8.5), the same way `submit:requestAlreadyOpen` is. They are listed in the error-code census's `CONSUMER_MINTED`, which fails the day the spec declares them. **Upstream follow-up:** propose these codes in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (`submit` and `supplement` `errorCodes`), then switch to the generated constants.

## Single-use semantics

Unchanged: a submission still spends the challenge whether or not it is accepted, including on a mismatch. What changed in storage:

- The row is now taken atomically (`take_raw`) instead of read and then removed. This closes a small window in which two concurrent submissions could both spend it.
- A **spent marker** replaces the row. It holds only the expiry and `spentAt`, not the challenge, so a replay is told `challengeAlreadyUsed` instead of `challengeNotIssued`. An expired challenge is put back as it was, so repeat attempts keep saying `challengeExpired`. Both are removed by the existing retention sweep after `expires_at`, as the challenge always was. Both writes are `insert_if_absent`, so a challenge requested in the meantime is never overwritten.
- Each refusal is logged (`info`, `refusal = not_issued|already_used|expired|mismatch`, applicant DID). The challenge value is never logged.

## Tests

- Unit (`challenge_refusal.rs`): each refusal → its code under each task, its marker, `expiredAt` only on expired, distinct kinds, and every message names the remedy.
- Unit (`pcs_challenge.rs`): not issued, single-use → already used (and stays so), mismatch spends the real one, a replaced challenge → mismatch, a new challenge clears the marker, expired stays expired until swept → not issued, and the marker holds no challenge and is swept.
- Integration (`tests/it/hidden_vetting_tasks.rs::a_refused_challenge_says_which_way`, `vetting-pcs`): a signed `submit/0.3` over `/v1/trust-tasks` reaches each of the four submit codes with its marker and `expiredAt`, and the message does not echo the challenge.
- Supplement codes are covered by unit mapping only. There is no integration test that drives a hidden-vetting supplement.

Ran locally: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`; `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -D warnings`; `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p vta-sdk` (4003 passed); `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs` (2848 passed); doc tests for vtc-service (vetting-pcs) and vta-sdk.

## Open questions

- With **no cited criterion** and **several hidden-vetting criteria**, `govern` evaluates each one in turn. The first spends the challenge, so the second reports `challengeAlreadyUsed`. A challenge refusal on any criterion also aborts the whole submission, even if a later non-hidden criterion would be met. Both behaviours predate this change and are unchanged here. Clients should cite the criterion.
- The marker means a spent challenge row lingers (holding no challenge value) until the sweep after its expiry, instead of being deleted on the spot. This matches the pcs-challenge spec's "discard when counted" for the value, but not literally for the row.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — local store only
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — new error codes only; `details.expiredAt` is camelCase; openvtc to map the codes
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — a crash between take and marker write leaves no row, so the next attempt is refused (`challengeNotIssued`)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — R6.4: each refusal is a distinct code; store failures stay `internalError`
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — see R5 line
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

A hidden-vetting proof is bound to a single-use challenge the community
issues over vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1, and the community spends it
when the proof arrives. Every way that spend could fail - the challenge
expired, was already used, was never issued, or is not the one the proof
was built over - reached the applicant as one `malformedRequest` with the
cause in a sentence. A client could not tell "you took too long" from
"your proof was built over the wrong challenge", which is the difference
between "try again" and "your client has a bug".

Each failure is now a typed `ChallengeRefusal` that travels from
`pcs_challenge::consume` through `pcs::decide`, the vetting facts and the
criterion evaluation to the join spine, and goes out on the Trust Task
path under a code of its own:

- `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeNotIssued` (details.reason `not_found`)
- `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeAlreadyUsed` (details.reason `gone`)
- `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeExpired` (details.reason `gone`,
  plus `details.expiredAt`)
- `vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeMismatch` (details.reason `conflict`)

and the same four local parts under `vtc/join-requests/supplement:` when
a supplement carries the proof. Neither specification declares a
challenge code yet, so they are consumer-minted under the task's own slug
(SPEC 8.5), as `requestAlreadyOpen` is; the constants live in
`vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests` for clients to match on, and the
error-code census lists them as consumer-minted so it fails the day the
specification adopts them. Surfaces that carry no code keep the same 400
`Validation`, now with a sentence that says which failure it was. The
message never contains the challenge value.

Single-use is unchanged: a submission still spends the challenge whether
or not it is accepted, including on a mismatch. The row is now taken
atomically (`take_raw`) rather than read then removed, and a spent marker
holding no challenge - only the expiry - is left in its place so a second
attempt is told "already used" rather than "never issued". An expired
challenge is put back as it was so repeated attempts keep saying
"expired". Both go at the retention sweep after `expires_at`, as the
challenge always did; both writes are `insert_if_absent`, so a challenge

title: feat(vtc): hidden vetting can be read and withdrawn, and an event approver names themselves (#729)
body:
feat(vtc): hidden vetting can be read and withdrawn, and an event approver names themselves (#729)

Hidden-vetter admission had an on switch (vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1)
and no way to turn it off or to see what was in force.

- vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw/0.1: an administrator removes one criterion's
  hidden-vetting parameters and republishes its manifest entry without them.
  The criterion's named vetting is untouched. Idempotent: a criterion with
  none answers withdrawn: false, not an error. Enrolment rows and the
  spent-token ledger are not deleted, and republishing later derives the
  same keys.
- vtc/vetting/hidden/show/0.1: an administrator reads the stored
  configuration (events' approvedBy and graceDays included, which the
  manifest omits), the published configuration, the current digest, and
  counts only: enrolled vetters per live class label, and per event its
  groupSize against groupFloor with derived approved/live. The community
  MUST NOT disclose which members enrolled or asked. This is the companion
  read publish/0.1 anticipated: because publish replaces events wholesale,
  re-publishing from the manifest un-approves live events.
- vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1 (draft, edited in place): an approvedBy
  that is new or changed must name the publishing signer's principal
  (approverNotSigner); an unchanged stored value may be re-sent by any
  administrator so a re-publish keeps approvals; an approver who asked to
  vet at the event is refused (approverInEvent). Publish and withdraw
  SHOULD be audited with who, which criterion and the deltas, never a
  reason.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

title: fix(join): a vetting statement counts only for the persona it vetted, and the ways in are listed
body:
## What was wrong

1. **The wrong persona's statements went out.** `satisfied_application_persona` used the chooser's persona's ready application, and if it had none, fell back to *any* persona's ready application. So choosing "a new persona" or a persona with nothing ready still went to the invitation step as the vetted persona and presented its statements. After the create-persona step, the resumed route took the same fallback.
2. **The selection was hard to follow.** The ←/→ "Apply as" value showed one persona at a time, so you couldn't see the other choices or how they differed.
3. **"Signing: not checked"** showed whenever the manifest arrived over DIDComm or was already known, because only `learn_over_http` resolved the DID document.

## What changed

- **One complete choice per row** (`KnownVetting` in `join.rs`). Every `RouteOption` now carries `applicant: Option<Applicant>`, which is `Persona(id)` or `NewPersona`. `build_routes` emits one vetting row per persona, ordered ready, then under way, then no application, then "a new persona". After those come "Use an invitation" and "Send an open request". `rows()` adds group headings ("With vetting" / "Other ways in") that can't be selected, and `step()` moves through the rows in drawn order, skipping headings. `ApplyAs` is gone as a row, along with `persona_index`, `selector()`, `shows()` and the `JoinVettingCycle` action.
- **A ready application counts only for its own persona.** `KnownVetting::ready_as(applicant)` returns a persona only when it's the row's own persona and its application is satisfied. There is no fallback. `take_route` handles the cases this way:
  - A ready row goes to the invitation step for that persona.
  - Any other persona row carries on or starts *that* persona's application (`apply_for_vetting` now takes the persona explicitly).
  - The new-persona row creates the persona. Once it exists, the route resumes on **that persona's own row**, which starts a new application for it.
  - Invitation and open request go to the identity step. The submit then attaches only the chosen persona's own statements, matched on its DID as `run_join_sequence` and `join_review` already do.
  - `take_join_route` and `satisfied_application_persona` are removed. `j` (Asking/Unknown phases only) goes to `continue_join`.
- **An application made for an earlier DID of the persona is not called ready.** It must match the DID `run_join_sequence` joins with.
- **Opening row:** the persona just minted, then a ready vetting row, then a held invitation, then an application under way, then the first available row.
- **Join-page wording for the next step.** `join_page_next_step` names the row, e.g. `next: join — Enter on "Present your vetting statements as alice"`. `vetting_actions::next_step_words`, used by the Vetting panel where `j` works, is unchanged.
- **PQC:** a new `learn_signing` resolves the community's DID document with `RESOLVE_TIMEOUT` (R1.2). It runs on entry when the book already knows the community vets, and on resume after a DIDComm manifest, and only when signing is still unknown. It records the result via `publishes_post_quantum_key` and `note_post_quantum_key`. Failure is logged and the page says "not checked — its DID document could not be resolved".
- The "First: …" step line, dim blocked rows, the `[a] read it before you send it` line (for the highlighted row's persona) and "How it protects you" are all kept. The highlighted persona row also shows the DID it joins as. An invitation the community requires is now noted once, beside the vetting heading.

## Tests

- New: `rows_are_grouped_and_the_cursor_skips_the_headings`, `a_ready_application_counts_only_for_its_own_persona`, `the_page_opens_on_the_persona_whose_statements_are_ready`, `each_persona_has_its_own_row_and_a_new_one_starts_from_scratch`, `the_join_page_names_the_row_for_the_next_step`, `signing_is_recorded_from_a_resolved_document`, `every_choice_is_a_row_under_its_group`, `the_next_step_names_the_row_rather_than_a_key_from_another_page`.
- Replaced or updated the old ApplyAs and cursor tests, and the `build_routes` tests for the new signature.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` all pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)

- R1.2: the new outbound resolve is bounded by `RESOLVE_TIMEOUT` (10 s).
- R1.4: no new polling loops.
- R6.4: a failed resolve leaves signing unknown, and the page says the document could not be resolved rather than guessing.
- R3.6: no new service endpoints. DID resolution goes through the existing TDK resolver.

title: feat(vtc): hidden vetting (PCS) is visible and run from the admin console
body:
## Problem

An administrator working only in the VTC console:
- could not tell whether their VTC supports hidden vetting (PCS). The `vetting-pcs` build feature shows nowhere.
- could not turn it on: the only way was a hand-built signed `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1`. There is no console control, no `cnm` command, and the REST route is gone. (`scripts/pcs-demo.sh hide` still POSTs to that removed route.)
- had it silently undone by any later edit to the criterion in the console. `accepts/register/0.2` has no member for the parameters, so the replacement it builds always arrived without them, and `register_accepts_inner` stored it that way.

## Change

**Server**
- `register_accepts_inner` carries a criterion's `hidden_vetting` over to its replacement, as `store_accepts` already does for `position`. It drops it only when the replacement asks for no vetting, which `hidden/publish:noVetting` refuses anyway.
- A stale doc comment on `HiddenVettingConfig` now says the config does reach the manifest.

**Console**
- **Dashboard tile "Hidden vetting (PCS)":** reads `trust-task-discovery/0.3` (patterns `vtc/vetting/hidden/*`). It shows "Supported" when the build routes `hidden/publish`, otherwise "Not in this build", and links to the criteria.
- **Hidden-vetting section on each criterion card** (`HiddenVettingCard.tsx`), rendered only on a build that serves it. It reads the join manifest's `vetting.ext["org.openvtc.hidden-vetting"]`, i.e. what applicants and vetters receive, and shows status, vetter and token labels, drip rate, suite, keys and events.
- **Controls on that section:** turn on, save drip rate, and roll labels to this month. Rolling matters because labels never advance on their own; the card warns when they are behind.
- **A criterion with events is read-only.** Publish replaces `events` wholesale, and the manifest omits `approvedBy`, so a re-publish from it would un-approve every event.
- **The criterion editor** says where hidden vetting is turned on, and that saving keeps it.

**Census**
- `trust_task_manifest` gains `FEATURE_GATED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`: `hidden/publish` must be dispatched exactly when `vetting-pcs` is compiled in.
- Discovery joins `SPINE_DOCUMENT_TYPES`.

## Not in this PR (spec first)

Three things have no task today, so they wait on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#729 and a `trust-tasks-rs` release:
- **Turning hidden vetting off:** `vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw/0.1`.
- **Reading the stored configuration:** `vtc/vetting/hidden/show/0.1`, including events' approvals, enrolment counts per label, and per-event demand against its floor.
- **Managing events from the console.**

The same spec PR tightens `publish/0.1`:
- an event's `approvedBy` must be the signer (today it is an unchecked string);
- an approver in the event is refused;
- publishes are audited.

A follow-up PR implements the server side of all of it, plus the console's event editor and Turn-off.

## Tests

- `hidden_vetting_tasks::saving_a_criterion_keeps_its_hidden_vetting_until_it_stops_asking_for_vetting` (`--features vetting-pcs`), through the real router: register, then publish, then an edit keeps the manifest's `ext`; a replacement with no vetting drops it.
- Console:
  - `HiddenVettingCard.test.tsx`: absent without support, enable payload, drip-rate payload keeps the labels, roll when behind, a criterion with events is read-only, `labelsBehind`.
  - `DashboardTiles.test.tsx`: the tile, both ways, plus the discovery payload.

Run locally:
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service`: 2811/2813 passed on the first run. The 2 failures were the census catching the console naming `withdraw`/`show`; they were removed from this PR. After that, `trust_task_manifest` passes with and without `vetting-pcs`.
- `hidden_vetting_tasks` (`--features vetting-pcs`): 9/9.
- clippy `-D warnings`, both feature sets: clean. fmt: clean.
- admin-ui: vitest 801/801, `tsc -b` clean.

Overlaps #1954 in `vetting/pcs.rs` (one doc comment) and `tests/it/hidden_vetting_tasks.rs` (an appended test). Either rebases trivially.

body:
## Problem
- **Finished requests cluttered the desk.** A signed or declined request stayed under **Requests** among the open ones, still showing the applicant's card (e.g. `name.legal  Alice`).
- **The card was never forgotten.** The design keeps a card only for `cardRetention` after the request closes (§9.3), and `VettingBook::prune` implements that. But **nothing ever called `prune`**, so card values, legal names included, stayed on disk indefinitely. Expired sessions were never closed by it either.

## Fix
- **Card values are forgotten when the request closes.**
  - `VetterPolicy::card_retention_days` now defaults to **0** (it was 7).
  - The card's digest is still kept; the signed statement commits to it.
  - The design doc (§9.3 and the policy example) is updated.
- **`prune` actually runs:** after every vetting outcome (`VettingOutcome::apply`), and on the hourly main-loop tick, which also fires at start-up.
- **Closed requests leave the desk.** After `CLOSED_GRACE` (10 min), long enough for a failed send to roll the request back, `prune` moves a closed request with its card forgotten into a new `VettingBook::vetted: Vec<VettedRecord>`. A record holds only the **community, date and outcome** (`Signed { statement_id }` or `Declined`). It has no card, no claims and no DID. A signed statement's applicant DID stays in `issued`, which withdrawing needs.
- **TUI:**
  - **Requests** lists only open requests, and the tab counts follow.
  - **Issued** becomes **History**: what you signed (as before, with withdraw), plus *Declined* as `date · community` lines. It ends with "Kept: who you signed for, so you can withdraw. Not kept: anyone's card or document."
  - The vetter journey finds its request by id, so a request that just closed doesn't show the next row's card.
- **CHANGELOG:** entry under `[0.5.0]` → Fixed, since 0.5.0 isn't published yet.

## Tests
- **Core (`a_finished_request_forgets_the_person_and_leaves_the_desk`):**
  - a real card arrives and is declined;
  - the legal name is in the serialized book until the first prune and gone after it;
  - the request stays through the grace, then becomes a `Declined` record with no applicant DID anywhere in `vetted`.
- **UI (`history_keeps_signed_and_declined_without_cards`):** checks the History view.
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`: all pass.

While a hidden-vetting (PCS ZKP) join waited up to 15 seconds for the community's challenge (#442), the progress page locked every key except F10. Nothing has been sent at that point, so leaving should cost nothing.

title: feat(join): a hidden-vetting join asks the community for its challenge itself
body:
## What

A community that hides its vetters (PCS ZKP) accepts a join's proof only over a challenge it issued itself (`vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1`). Until now the join failed when no challenge was stored, telling the person to press `m` on the application and join again. Now the join asks for the challenge itself, waits a bounded time for it, and carries on.

## How

- **Asking.** `launch_join_sequence` gets a new gate after the answers and trust-registry gates: `challenge_step(application, hears_replies, fresh)` decides `Ask` or `Proceed`. On `Ask`, `ask_challenge` sends the request with a bounded send (`ASK_TIMEOUT`, R1.2) and records it as a `QueryKind::PcsChallenge` query. The launch then parks in `state.join.challenge_wait`.
- **Waiting.** This reuses the pattern for waiting on requirements. The join flow returns `JoinExit::AwaitChallenge(AwaitingChallenge)`, and the runtime loop (the only loop with an inbound arm) holds it. Resumption happens in one of two ways:
  - When the answer arrives, `challenge_resume_for` picks it out and the loop re-enters with `JoinEntry::Challenge { awaiting, outcome }`. That entry does **not** reset `state.join`, so the persona, invitation, approved answers and registry choice the person made are all kept. The launch is taken up again where it parked.
  - When `CHALLENGE_WAIT` (15s, the same as `REQUIREMENTS_WAIT`) passes with no answer, the loop re-enters with an `Unanswered` outcome.
  - `JoinCancel` while parked forgets the query.
- **Matching.** A new `CommunityAnswer::Challenge { query, community }` is emitted by `inbound::challenge_issued` alongside its existing notice. Matching is on the request's **document id**, so a challenge asked for from the Vetting page (`m`) does not resume the join.
- **Errors (R6.4).** Each failure ends in a "Nothing was sent — join again" sentence that names which of these happened:
  - the request could not be sent (our mediator; the send timeout is worded separately)
  - the community refused (with its code and note)
  - the answer could not be read (contract mismatch, "not a refusal")
  - no answer came within 15s (the service may be offline or unreachable)
- **Loops that can't hear replies (State A).** The join does not ask. If no challenge is stored, the refusal now says that this screen cannot hear the community's answer, and that starting the join again once messaging is running will ask for the challenge itself. The old "press m" advice was wrong there. In practice State A has no persona, and so no application.
- **Existing refusals kept.** The no-attestation and proof-build-error sentences are unchanged. No-attestation is now checked first, so a join with nothing to prove says so without asking for a challenge.

## Single-use semantics (from vtc-service `vetting/pcs_challenge.rs` + `pcs.rs::decide`)

The community keeps **one open challenge per applicant DID** and replaces it whenever it is asked again. A challenge expires after **15 minutes**. It is **consumed on any submission carrying a proof**: the row is removed before the expiry and match checks, so a refused proof spends it too.

So:

- **Every hidden launch that can hear the answer asks for a fresh challenge**, even when one is stored. A stored one may have been replaced, may have expired, or may already be spent, and this client cannot tell. One round trip at join time costs less than sending a proof the community will certainly refuse. The stored challenge is dropped once the new request is sent, because the community has replaced it by then.
- **After a submit that carried a proof**, `Application::hidden_submission_sent()` clears `hidden_challenge` and `hidden_submission`. This is saved together with the pending membership. A submit that failed at our mediator keeps the challenge, since nothing reached the community.

## Tests

- `join_flow::vetting_tests`:
  - `a_hidden_launch_asks_for_its_challenge_rather_than_failing`: no challenge → ask; a stored challenge → still ask; a fresh one → proceed; can't hear replies → proceed.
  - `only_a_hidden_launch_with_an_attestation_asks`
  - `only_the_awaited_challenge_resumes_the_launch`: matching by document id and community; refused and unreadable outcomes are worded distinctly.
  - `a_hidden_join_with_no_attestation_says_so_before_the_challenge`
  - `a_challenge_that_did_not_come_stops_the_join_and_says_why`
  - `a_hidden_join_without_its_proof_stops_and_says_why`: adjusted to the new State-A wording.
- `openvtc-core` `vetting::tests::a_challenge_is_answered_to_its_question_and_spent_by_the_submit_it_binds`: an issued challenge is stored and answered under its query id; a proof-carrying submit spends it, and one with no proof does not.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides` and `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` all pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the send is under `ASK_TIMEOUT` and the wait under `CHALLENGE_WAIT`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the stored challenge is cleared only after the request is sent, and only after a proof-carrying submit returned Ok
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no automatic retry; the person joins again
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a, no new loop
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire change; `CommunityAnswer` is in-process only
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no proof means no submit, as before
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a crash while parked leaves the old challenge cleared (or kept, if the send had not completed) and nothing submitted; the next join asks again
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

A community that hides its vetters accepts a join's zero-knowledge proof
only over a challenge it issued (vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1). Until
now the join failed when none was stored and told the person to press m
on the application and join again.

The launch now asks for a fresh challenge itself, after every question
the person answers, and parks: like a join waiting on a community's
requirements, it hands the wait to the runtime loop (the only loop that
hears inbound answers) and is resumed through JoinEntry::Challenge
without resetting what the person chose. The answer is matched on the
request's own document id (a new CommunityAnswer::Challenge), so a
challenge asked for from the Vetting page does not resume it.

The wait is bounded (15s, the same as for requirements; the send itself
is bounded too) and each failure is worded for what it was: the request
could not be sent (our mediator), the community refused it (with its
code), answered in a form this client cannot read (contract mismatch),
or never answered.

A fresh challenge is asked for on every hidden launch that can hear the
answer, even when one is stored: vtc-service keeps one per applicant,
replaces it on each ask, lets it lapse after 15 minutes and consumes it
on any submission that carries a proof, counted or refused. For the same
reason the stored challenge is cleared once a proof bound to it has been
sent. A loop that cannot hear replies does not ask, and its refusal now
says so instead of pointing at a key it cannot reach. With no attestation

title: feat(vetting): a vetter can give an optional reason and note when declining
body:
## What
`vetting/decline/0.1` carries an optional reason `code` and an optional `message` (1–500 characters). `VettingBook::decline` already passed them through, but the TUI always sent `None, None` and the confirm page had no way to give either.

**Vetter: "Decline this request?"**
- **Reason** (←/→): starts at *no reason given*, then cycles through:
  - could not establish who you are (`couldNotVerify`)
  - your document did not match your card or you (`documentMismatch`)
  - the match code could not be confirmed with you (`livenessFailed`)
  - the vetter prefers not to vouch for you (`notComfortable`)
  - another reason (`other`)
- **Note:** optional free text. More than 500 characters is refused with the count; an empty note sends none.
- **What the page says:** a reason is never required, and whatever you choose goes to the applicant only. The community isn't told you declined, or why.
- **Keys:** `y`/Enter declines and `n`/Esc keeps the request while the cursor is on Reason. On Note, `y` and `n` are typed as text, and Enter declines.

**Applicant:** the request row shows what they were given, e.g. `declined — your document did not match your card or you · they wrote: "…"`. With neither, it still reads `declined`.

The vetter journey's footer now reads `x: decline (a reason is optional)`.

## Tests
- **Core:** new `a_declines_reason_and_note_reach_the_applicant` sends a code and a note through the real exchange and checks both arrive in the applicant's `RequestState::Declined`.
- **Keys:** `y`/`n` and ←/→ act on Reason, while on Note `n` is typed rather than taken as "keep it".
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(vtc): working in the admin console counts toward the idle timeout
body:
## Problem

The admin console signed operators out while they were using it.

The idle timeout (`auth.admin_idle_timeout`, default 900s) is measured from `Session::last_seen`, and only a cookie-authenticated request through the `AuthClaims` extractor advanced it. Most of what the console sends is now a signed Trust Task document to `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, which authenticates by its proof and reads no session. So a busy operator produced no activity. Fifteen minutes after the last cookie-borne call, the renewal was refused for inactivity and the session-deadline watcher (#1905) showed Login.

Counting every signed document would be wrong the other way. The action badge, community counts and banners post signed reads on timers, so an unattended tab would never time out. Only the console can tell input from a poll.

## Change

- **Console** (`admin-ui/src/lib/user-activity.ts`): notes real input (`pointerdown`, `keydown`, `wheel`, `touchstart`; not mouse movement) and sends `X-VTC-User-Activity: 1` on a signed document posted within 60s of input. Timers in an idle tab send nothing. Tracking starts in `watchSession`.
- **Route** (`routes/trust_tasks.rs`): records activity only when all of these hold:
  - the header is present;
  - the document ran successfully;
  - it was verified as a known signer;
  - its principal owns the session named by the cookie. The principal is the signer, or the administrator its console key acts for: `Admission::verified_principal`, the same mapping the per-signer rate limit uses.
- **`vti_common::auth::touch_cookie_session_for`** (new, additive): authenticates the session cookie exactly as the extractors do (signature, session state, `jti` pin), requires the session's DID to equal the principal, then calls `touch_last_seen`. Best-effort, like the extractor's touch.

Invariants preserved:
- Renewals never count.
- Bearer callers never touch.
- A document signed by one identity can't keep another identity's session alive.
- A refused document counts for nothing.

Anyone able to send the header already holds the session and could just click. The header only lets the console report activity the server could not otherwise see.

The VTI spec has no idle-timeout requirement, so there is nothing to cite or record as a divergence.

## Tests

- `vti-common`: own-DID touch; another identity's session is untouched; no cookie or a forged cookie does nothing.
- `vtc-service` unit: `verified_principal` is known only after verification and maps a console key to its admin.
- `vtc-service` it (`session_idle_timeout`), through the real router:
  - a console-key document with the header advances the admin's `last_seen`;
  - one without the header does not;
  - a document signed by another admin does not;
  - a refused document does not.
- Console (vitest): the header is sent within the window, and is absent before any input or after the window.

Run locally:
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -p vtc-service`: 3482/3488 passed. The 6 failures were the admin-UI embed tests, which fail under `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`; re-run with the UI built, all 11 pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- admin-ui `vitest run`: 793 passed. `tsc -b --noEmit`: clean.

title: feat(join): review what the community will receive, and word the invitation page for vetting in hand
body:
## What
The Join step of the applicant journey: before a request goes out, the person sees exactly what the community will receive. The invitation page also stops misdescribing what happens when you hold vetting.

### Review and send
The last page before sending (#439's trust-registry page, retitled " Review and send ") now opens with a review. The publication question follows it.

```
What first-vtc will receive
  Your identity    did:webvh:…:march-issue
  Invitation       none
  Vetting          PCS ZKP  a zero-knowledge proof built from 2 vetter attestations
                   it learns that enough vetters vouched for you — not who they were
  Your face sends  name.legal  Alice Example
  How it decides   meeting its vetting requirements admits you automatically
```

**What each line shows:**
- **Your identity:** the persona's DID, or "a new persona — its DID is made when you send".
- **Invitation:** the issuer, plus a note when the invitation was issued to another of your personas and a proof will link the two.
- **Vetting:**
  - **Named:** "N named statement(s) — it sees who vouched for you", with one line per statement: vetter, method, the claims they checked, and validity.
  - **Hidden:** the PCS ZKP badge, the attestation count, and what the community does and doesn't learn.
  - **None:** "none".
- **Your face sends:** the approved answers.
- **How it decides:**
  - Read from the admission rule of the criterion the application names.
  - With neither an invitation nor vetting, it says the request goes to moderators.

Everything comes from the same records `run_join_sequence` builds the request from (`join_review`).

### Invitation page
When the persona joining holds vetting for this community, it goes with the request whether or not an invitation is chosen. The page used to say joining without one meant "The community reviews and approves the request manually", which wasn't true. Now:
- **Title:** "Also present an invitation?"
- **New line under the prompt:** "Your 2 vetting statements go with this request either way. An invitation is optional on top of them." For PCS ZKP, it names the proof instead.
- **The without row:** "Join without one — with your 2 vetting statements only", followed by the community's actual admission rule.
- **Without vetting held,** the page is unchanged.

`VettingInHand` is filled in `open_invitation_choice` from the same application lookup the join uses. The "how it decides" wording is shared between the two pages (`vetting_decision`).

## Tests
- `the_review_says_what_the_community_receives_and_who_it_learns_vouched`, covering named and hidden. The review comes before the publication question.
- `a_bare_join_reviews_as_a_new_persona_with_nothing_to_present`
- `with_vetting_in_hand_the_invitation_is_optional_on_top`, a rendered page test that also checks the plain open-request wording is unchanged.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p openvtc`: all pass.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: feat: an applicant can consent to trust-registry publication when joining
body:
## Why

A VTC publishes a member in its trust registry only if that member consented. Consent is `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.2 and 0.3). It defaults to `false`, and the VTC copies it onto the member record (`publish_consent`). Approving the request does not consent for the applicant, and the registry sync skips any member without consent.

openvtc hard-coded `registry_consent: false` in `build_join_submit_document`, so nobody who joined through openvtc could ever be published.

## What

**Core (`openvtc-core/src/join.rs`)**
- `JoinPresentation` gains `registry_consent: bool`, and the submit sends it as given.
- `From<Value>` sets it to `false`, so any caller that does not ask keeps today's behaviour.
- Breaking for struct literals; noted in the CHANGELOG.

**TUI join flow**
- New `JoinPage::RegistryConsent` page, shown on every join as the last step before the request goes out (after any requested-attribute answers).
- It is gated in `launch_join_sequence`, which every launch path goes through: identity, invitation, context, vetting and answers.
- The page says what publishing means: a public record that the identity you join with is a member. It also says that leaving the box unticked is a complete answer, that the community may still decline to publish, and that openvtc can't change the answer after joining.
- The box starts unticked. Only Space toggles it, and no letter key answers yes. Enter answers either way, and Esc cancels.
- The answer belongs to the community it was given for (`RegistryChoice::consent_for`) and is `take()`n by the one submit that sends it. A retry, or a second join from the same open flow, asks again.
- The success page shows a `Registry:` row with the answer that was sent.
- The CLI has no separate join entry point. `--invitation` only pre-loads an invitation for the TUI flow, so it goes through the same page.

**Tests**
- `the_applicants_registry_consent_reaches_the_wire_as_given` covers `true` and `false` on submit 0.2 and 0.3. It asserts three things:
  - the raw JSON member `payload.registryConsent` carries the value;
  - no snake_case `registry_consent` member is present;
  - the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::vtc::join_requests::submit::{v0_2,v0_3}::Payload` reads back `Some(value)`.
- `an_unasked_presentation_does_not_consent` covers the `From<Value>` default.
- `join_lifecycle_e2e.rs` sends `true` in the approval scenario and `false` in the rejection scenario. It asserts both the wire member and the VTC's parsed value.
- Unit tests for the page cover its wording, unticked on open, and the keys. Tests for the state handler cover the page opening and parking the launch, a previous yes not pre-ticking the next question, and `consent_for` / `answered_for` semantics.

**Docs**
- `docs/design/multi-community-support.md` gains R-B-6a, and the §3 note now gives the wire name.
- CHANGELOG: Breaking and Added entries.

## Out of scope: changing consent after joining

A member has no way to change consent afterwards. `vtc/members/update` is administrator-only, and no member-signed Trust Task exists for it. A new task has to be specified in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first. Until then, leaving and rejoining with the other answer is the only route: self-remove tombstones the member row by default, which clears `publish_consent`, and re-admission writes a fresh row with the new request's answer.

## Checks run locally (as CI runs them)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
- `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`
- `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --features arbitrary --lib`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- `cargo bench --workspace --no-run`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --test join_lifecycle_e2e -- --include-ignored` (3/3)

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the answer is in-memory UI state, taken by the submit; nothing new is persisted
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): untouched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): untouched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no new type; an existing camelCase member now carries the user's value, checked against the generated spec payloads
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an absent answer sends `false`
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the success row says "consented" / "not consented", not "published"
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): dying before the submit sends nothing, and the next join asks again
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(join): an applicant can consent to trust-registry publication (#439)
body:
feat(join): an applicant can consent to trust-registry publication (#439)

A community publishes a member in its trust registry only if the member
consented, through registryConsent on vtc/join-requests/submit. The VTC
copies it onto the member record; approval does not consent for them, and
the registry sync skips anyone without it. openvtc hard-coded false in
build_join_submit_document, so nobody who joined through it could ever be
published.

Core: JoinPresentation carries registry_consent and the submit sends it as
given. From<Value> sets it false, so every caller that does not ask keeps
today's behaviour.

TUI: every join now stops on a Trust registry page as the last step before
the request goes out, after any requested-attribute answers. It says what
publishing means (a public record that this identity is a member), the box
starts unticked, only Space ticks it, and Enter answers either way. The
answer is held for the community it was given for and consumed by one
submit, so a retry or a second join asks again. The success page shows the
answer that was sent.

Tests check the camelCase wire member for both values on both submit
versions against the generated trust_tasks_rs::specs payloads, the e2e
lifecycle test covers both values, and the page and its state are unit
tested. Docs: multi-community-support.md gains R-B-6a; CHANGELOG updated.

title: feat(vetting): applicant and vetter journeys — the whole process, where you are, and why
body:
## What
Applying for vetting and vetting someone are each now a **journey page**. The page shows the whole process, marks where you are, explains each step as you reach it, and offers only the action the current step needs. It takes the full width of the screen (the menu steps aside), so the process no longer jumps between full-screen and menu-panel layouts.

```
Applying to first-vtc as alice                          PCS ZKP
✓ Requirements ─ ✓ Face ─ ● Vetters ─ ○ Sessions ─ ○ Statements ─ ○ Join
                 Work                               0 of 2
What's happening — Vetters
  A vetter is a member the community has named to vouch for people. …
Your part now
  r  ask a vetter with the ticket link they gave you
  v  find a vetter in the community's directory
Esc: back to your applications (nothing is lost)   x: abandon this application
✓ done   ● yours now   … waiting on someone else   ○ to come
```

**Steps:**
- **Applicant:** Requirements → Face → Vetters → Sessions → Statements → Join
- **Vetter:** Request → Session → Match code → Card → Check → Sign

## How it works
- **`openvtc_core::vetting::journey`:** the pure model. `applicant_journey(&Application)` and `vetter_journey(&DeskEntry)` mark each step done, current, waiting on someone else, or still to come, with progress such as "1 of 2" or the match code.
  - It's built on `Application::next_step`, so the journey and the existing "next:" hints agree.
  - At most one step is current.
  - Every step has `explain(hidden)` text that teaches what the step is for. Where it matters, named and PCS ZKP communities get different text, e.g. who the community learns vouched for you.
- **`ui::journey`:** the step strip, the "What's happening" box and the legend, shared by both sides so they look alike.
- **`components::vetting_journey`:** the page itself. It wraps the Vetting page's existing views (face picker, ask-a-vetter, card page, attest form, confirms) rather than replacing them: an open form is drawn under the strip. With nothing open, it shows "Your part now", plus the applicant's vetters and match codes or the vetter's view of the card.
- **Keys:** with a journey open, only steps already reached take their keys, plus `m`, `x`/decline and Esc. Esc returns to the list with nothing lost. A key for a step not yet reached does nothing.
- **Opening a journey:**
  - Enter on an application, or on a desk request. `c` and `a` still go straight to the card or attest form.
  - Starting an application from the join page (`focus_application`).
  - Opening a vetting Inbox entry (`focus_vetting_target`).
- **Keeping it current:** `sync_journey` rebuilds the open journey on every sync, so a session opening or a statement arriving moves it on by itself. A journey whose application or request has gone closes.

## Not in this PR (next)
- The Join step still hands off to the existing join flow. A "what the community will receive" review screen, including whether the vetting is a named statement or a PCS ZKP proof, comes next.
- Rewording the invitation (VIC) page for an applicant who holds vetting statements.

## Tests
- **Core:** a new application starts at Requirements; then Face, then Vetters, with details; every step explains itself, and hidden mode says vetters stay hidden.
- **Integration (`vetting/tests.rs`):** both journeys follow a real request→session exchange. The vetter is on the match code and waiting for the card.
- **UI:** the strip marks and progress; the applicant page (process, explainer, step key, way out); the vetter page (the match code with what to do); journey keys gated by the steps reached.
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc -p openvtc-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(vetting): attest on the session's method, and allow resending an unrecorded withdrawal
body:
## Problems (vetter side)
1. **The attest form ignored the session's method.** `StartAttest` opened `AttestForm::default()`, so Method was always "in person". After a video-call session, the vetter was one Enter away from signing a statement that misstates how the person was checked.
2. **A refused or unrecorded withdrawal got stuck.** `ArmWithdraw` refused any statement with a withdrawal attached ("That statement is already withdrawn"), including one the community refused (`WithdrawalRefused`, which is only logged) or never recorded. The row read "withdrawal sent — not yet recorded" indefinitely, with no way forward. Yet `VettingBook::withdrawal` explicitly allows sending again until the withdrawal is recorded ("withdrawal converges").

## Fix
1. `StartAttest` reads the desk entry's `DeskState::CardReceived { session }` and opens the form on `session.method`.
2. `IssuedRow` gains `withdrawal_recorded`. `w` is refused only once the community has recorded the withdrawal. While one is pending, the hint reads "w: send the withdrawal again".

## Tests
- New: `an_unrecorded_withdrawal_can_be_sent_again`, covering the hint for none, pending and recorded.
- The method default is a direct lookup in the dispatch path, which needs a live `ActionCtx`. It isn't unit-tested.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

title: fix(inbox): a vetting task opens where its step is taken
body:
## Problem
The inbox tasks raised for vetting were mapped to `TaskKind::Informational("Unknown")` with an empty DID:
- **Vetter side:** "Vetting Request (Inbound)" and "Vetting Card Received".
- **Applicant side:** "Vetting Session (Send Card)".

Opening one showed only its type and task id, with "d: dismiss  Esc: back". So the one notification telling someone it's their turn led nowhere. They had to go to Vetting, switch to the right tab (the desk isn't the default), and find the row themselves.

## Fix
- A new `TaskKind::Vetting(VettingTarget)`, with two targets:
  - `Card { application_id, session_id }`
  - `Desk { request_id }`

  Both are read from the fields the tasks already carry.
- **Enter on one** (`OpenDetail`) calls the new `vetting_actions::focus_vetting_target` instead of building a detail view:
  - **Card:** opens Vetting → Applications on that application, straight into the card page for that session.
  - **Desk:** opens Vetting → desk → Requests with the request selected, or says "That request is no longer on your desk."
- The row is labelled `✓ VET`, with the applicant's or vetter's DID underneath.

## Tests
- New: `a_vetting_task_opens_where_its_step_is_taken`, covering the card target, the desk target and the "gone" message.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

Part of the applicant/vetter flow work. The planned journey pages will become the target these open.

title: fix(join): carry on as the persona just made, and stop naming keys that are gone
body:
## Problem
1. **Wrong persona after making one.** On the vetting join page, choosing "a new persona" opens the create-persona overlay. When it closes, `show_vetting` rebuilds the page and `take_route` resumes. But `vetting_view` picks which persona the page opens on by its own rules: one with a satisfied application, else the first application's persona, else the first by name. With other personas present, the resumed route could start or continue an application as **a different persona** from the one just made.
2. **Stale keys.** The "Applying needs a persona" refusal told the holder to "Press n to create one here, or join anyway (j)". Neither key is bound on that page any more.

## Fix
1. `JoinState::minted_persona` is set when `mint_persona_inline` persists a persona. `vetting_view` takes a new `prefer: Option<PersonaId>`, which `show_vetting` fills from it, so the page reopens on the persona just made. Making it was the decision about who applies.
2. The refusal now reads "Set Apply as to "a new persona" with ←/→, then press Enter to make one."

## Tests
- New: `the_page_reopens_on_the_persona_just_made`. It uses two personas, and the preferred one wins over the page's default pick.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

title: fix(join): a hidden-vetting join with no proof stops instead of submitting nothing
body:
## Problem
When a community hides its vetters (PCS ZKP), the join sends a zero-knowledge proof in `extensions.hiddenVetting` in place of the named vetting statements. In `run_join_sequence`:
- **If `prepare_hidden_submission` failed,** the error was logged as an *info* line and the join was **submitted anyway**, with neither the proof nor any statements. The community decided on no vetting, while the holder believed they had presented theirs.
- **`Ok(false)` (hidden parameters, but no attestation has arrived)** submitted the same empty join, with no message at all.
- **With no community challenge yet,** the join showed "Waiting…" and returned without `fail()`. The progress page never completed, nothing resumed it, and the listener and any persona minted for this join were left behind.

## Fix
A new function, `hidden_proof_refusal`, returns `None` when the proof is built, or `Some(sentence)` otherwise. The caller fails the join with that sentence and runs the same cleanup as every other failed step: remove the listener and roll back a just-minted persona. The three sentences:
- **No challenge:** "…none has arrived yet. Nothing was sent. In Vetting, press m on this application to ask for it, then join again." (`m` is what calls `ask_for_challenge`.)
- **No attestation:** "…no vetter's attestation has reached this application yet, so there is nothing to prove. Nothing was sent."
- **The proof fails:** "The zero-knowledge proof of your vetting could not be built (…). Nothing was sent — joining without it would present no vetting at all."

I also corrected `prepare_hidden_submission`'s doc comment, which said hidden vetting applies to no application today.

## Tests
- New: `a_hidden_join_without_its_proof_stops_and_says_why`, covering the no-challenge and no-attestation refusals. The proof-error path needs real PCS keys to trigger and is covered by the same branch.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The join could ask for the challenge itself rather than sending the holder to press `m`. That fits better into the planned applicant journey, where "get the community's challenge" becomes a visible step.

Under a community that hides its vetters, the join sends a PCS zero-knowledge
proof in place of the named statements. When that proof could not be built,

carrying no vetting at all: the community decided on nothing while the holder
believed they had presented their vetting. With no attestation yet the same
happened silently, and with no community challenge the join stopped without

title: feat: show PQC signing and PCS ZKP vetting, and say what each credential is
body:
## What
Two cryptographic properties are now visible wherever they matter. Each is drawn as a filled badge, and its meaning is explained once per page:

| Badge | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `PQC-SIGNED` | Signed with a post-quantum key (ML-DSA) as well as a classical one | **Credential:** its proof set has an `mldsa*`/`slhdsa*` proof. **Community:** a credential it issued you has one, or, before joining, its DID document lists an ML-DSA-44 key under `assertionMethod` |
| `PCS ZKP` | The community proves vetting with a PCS zero-knowledge proof. It learns that enough vetters vouched, not who they were | The community's stored vetting requirements (`org.openvtc.hidden-vetting`), read with the same `hidden::read_mode` an application adopts |

**Where they appear:**
- **My Credentials:** a badge on each PQC-signed row, plus a "Signature" line in the detail view that also says "classical only" when it isn't.
- **Communities:** both badges on the community's header line, with a legend.
- **Vetting → Applications:** a badge on the row, and a "Vetters" line: hidden, named, or not known until the requirements arrive.
- **Vetting desk:** a badge on the row, and a "You are" line: hidden (counted in a zero-knowledge proof) or named (your signed statement, with your DID, goes to the community).
- **Join page:** a new "How it protects you" block. It always states both properties, including when they're absent ("named — the community sees which vetters vouched for you", "classical keys only").

**Credentials list:** each row now shows what the credential is (Membership, Role: vetter, a statement), which of your personas it was issued to, and a readable validity. Before, every row showed the issuer and two raw timestamps, so four first-vtc rows looked identical.

## How
- **`openvtc_core::proof_check`:** new `signed_post_quantum(&Value)` and `publishes_post_quantum_key(&Document)`. The second handles relative `#key` references, which webvh documents use.
- **`VettingBook`:**
  - `KnownCriterion::hidden_vetting()` / `VettingBook::hidden_vetting(community)`.
  - A new `KnownCommunity::post_quantum_key: Option<bool>`, `serde(default)` so older configs load, recorded from the DID document the join flow already resolves in `learn_over_http`. No extra network call.
- **UI:** a new `ui::badges` module with one definition per badge. Credential rows get `post_quantum` and `subject_label`, filled in one pass (`finish_credential_rows`) so no list misses them.

## Not covered
- A community reached only over DIDComm, never resolved here, shows "Signing: not checked" on the join page until its DID document is read.
- PQC is shown from the proofs as held. Credentials are verified with `proof_check::verify_signed` on receipt, which fails a set if any proof fails.

## Tests
- **Core:** a PQ proof in a set is recognised, a classical-only one isn't, and a document's ML-DSA signing key counts while an auth-only one doesn't. A stored criterion knows whether its vetters are hidden.
- **UI:**
  - A credential row shows its kind, persona, validity and badge, with the legend once.
  - The join page states both properties when present and when absent.
- `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(vetting): a card with no face says so, and f chooses one from the card
body:
## Problem
An applicant tried to send their card to a vetter and got:

> Could not preview the card: VTA Error: persona disclosure preview failed: not found: … persona did:webvh:… has no profile bound, so there is nothing to disclose

A vetting application's persona wears no face until the holder presses `f` on the application and picks one. Nothing enforces that before the card step. On the card page:
- The raw VTA refusal named a DID and no action to take.
- `f` didn't work on that page.
- The face picker only opened when the page was in list mode. So `f` from the holder-grant retry page produced only a status line, and with no faces at all the picker (and its "Make a face" row) never opened.

## Fix
- **`preview_refusal`:** "has no profile bound" now reads "This application has no face yet, so there is no card to show. Press f to choose the face vetters see — you come back here once it is worn."
- **`f` on the card page** sends `ChooseFace` for the card's own application, not the list's selected row. The card is remembered in a new field, `VettingState::card_after_face`.
- **The `Faces` outcome opens the picker** from the list, the card page or the holder-grant retry. It also opens with an empty face list, whose only row makes a face.
- **Returning to the card:** wearing a face (`FaceWorn`), making one (create, which also wears it), or pressing Esc in the picker returns to the card it was opened from. From the list, everything behaves as before.
- **Card page hint:** now reads "Enter: preview  f: choose the face  Esc: not now".

## Tests
- New: `a_card_with_no_face_worn_says_to_choose_one`, `vetting_card_chooses_the_face_on_f`, `a_face_chosen_from_the_card_returns_to_the_card`, `backing_out_of_the_picker_returns_where_it_came_from`.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 816 passed. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

Part of the wider applicant/vetter flow work. This is the smallest piece that removes the dead end.

title: vta-sdk: keep a trust-task rejection's code and details instead of flattening to Protocol(String)
body:
## Problem
`vta-sdk` turns most trust-task rejections into `VtaError::Protocol(format!("trust task failed [{code}]: {message}"))` (`vta-sdk/src/client/mod.rs`, the rejection mapping before `seal_vault_secret`). The payload's `details` is read only for `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion`. For every other code it is dropped, and the code itself survives only inside a sentence.

As a result, callers:
- can't act on data the VTA already sends, and
- have to string-match the code out of the message to tell rejections apart. That's the drift a typed error is meant to prevent.

## Concrete case
`persona/profile/delete` refuses a bound face with `persona/profile/delete:bound` and `details.personaDids` (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/persona.rs`, `handle_profile_delete`).

OpenVTC needs those DIDs. A face can be worn by a persona the client can't see from its own memberships, for example another client sharing the VTA or a `pnm` binding. OpenVTC's prompt should say *who* wears the face before it offers to take the face off them.

Because the SDK drops `details`, OpenVTC (OpenVTC/openvtc#430) currently:
- matches `delete:bound]` in the error string, and
- parses the count from "N persona(s) are bound to this profile".

So it can only say "worn by N personas", not which ones. The same applies to the `versionConflict` rejections, whose `details.currentVersion` is also lost.

## Proposal
Add a variant that keeps the rejection as data, for example:

```rust
VtaError::Rejected { code: String, message: String, details: Option<serde_json::Value> }
```

Keep `Display` producing today's `trust task failed [{code}]: {message}` text, so log and error output doesn't change. The existing special cases (`permissionDenied`, `transportUnavailable`, `unavailable`, `unsupportedType`/`unsupportedVersion`) stay as they are.

Possibly add helpers such as `VtaError::rejection_code()` / `rejection_details()`, so callers can match on `code.rsplit_once(':')` for the local part without parsing strings.

## Acceptance
- A `persona/profile/delete:bound` rejection exposes `details.personaDids` to the caller.
- A `…:versionConflict` rejection exposes `details.currentVersion`.
- The `Display` output of existing errors is unchanged.

Once this ships, OpenVTC's `openvtc_core::persona::profile::worn_by` string-match can be replaced with a typed read, and the prompt can name the DIDs.
