title: vti-common-v0.37.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc/git-ns**: Single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties ([#1936](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1936))

* feat(vtc/git-ns): single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties

  A community in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022, #1925) has one
  administrator. Fixed rule 7 of git-ns/right/grant/0.3 still refused every
  elevated self-grant, so `cnm git adopt <repo> --owner <own DID>` failed with
  git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. Break-glass left records nobody could ever ratify.

  Single-administrator mode now reaches rule 7. It uses the same discipline as
  the consent waiver (`git_ns::single_admin`):

  - Only where nobody else is eligible. `others_eligible` reuses
    `admin_consent::approvers_for` over the namespace's `git.ns.admin`. That
    covers the break-glass deciders and any approve scope reaching them. It also
    counts any other member whose git rights could make this grant (rules 1 and
    2). One eligible party, or the mode off, and the refusal stands.
  - Every path the rule covers: right/grant, repo/create (implied repo.create
    naming self as owner), repo/adopt naming self, namespace/reseat to self, and
    drift/resolve adopt for one's own account. The rules accept a `Waivable`
    token only for that exact actor, right and resource. Rules 1, 2 and 5, the
    granter-covers floor, the consent-class gate and policy all still apply.
  - Requires the requester's operation-bound step-up. This is the break-glass
    mechanism (`bound_step_up`), bound to the document actually signed (for an
    adoption, the drift/resolve document).
  - Writes a Critical `SingleAdminMode { event: selfGrantWaived }` audit row
    before the write. It names the rule, task, digest, git-ns action, right and
    resource. If the audit write fails, the operation is refused and nothing is
    recorded.
  - Marks the result. The record carries `singleAdmin { at, task }`, which is
    never published. The answer carries `ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`.
    git-ns/view 0.4/0.5 lists waived records under the same ext member. The ACL
    resource grant shows `selfGrantWaived: true`. A `gitNs.right.selfGrantWaived`
    activity item is written.
  - Counts for invariants. Waived records count toward the last-owner and
    last-admin invariants, unlike unratified break-glass.

- **vtc**: Custom roles, capability approver sets, admin-key rollover and capability-driven console (VTI-CLT-025 – 032, VTI-APV-018) ([#1927](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1927))

Phase C2 of role-based administration (docs/05-design-notes/vtc-admin-roles.md).

  Single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022, #1925): ChangeRoles and RestoreBackup
  go through gesture_then_consent_for, so with the mode on and nobody else
  eligible they run on the requester's bound gesture, the waiver audited
  Critical; both are tested. A restore replaces the audit log, so its waiver row
  is written again into the restored log after the commit.

  Custom roles (§6.2). vtc/roles/{define,list,show,delete}/0.1 are served on the
  signed-document spine with the generated types. A role is a record in the acl
  keyspace (role:<name>, carried by a backup), resolved onto every entry read
  from its stored definition; an entry naming an undefined role confers nothing,
  sign-in included (VTI-ACL-011). define/delete take vtc.roles.assign +
  vtc.approvals.admin, the requester's bound gesture and the N-of-M consent of the
  other holders (new Act::ChangeRoles). A ceiling is bounded by what the requester
  and every approver hold and may approve (exceedsDefinerAuthority, VTI-ACL-042,
  -071); git.commit.sign is additive and never in a ceiling. delete is refused
  while any entry (expired ones too) or pending grant holds the role (inUse),
  counted and removed under the admin-set lock a custom-role grant commits under.

  Approver sets (§7). may_approve reads approve authority alone (VTI-ACL-040), so
  the least-privilege approver counts for every act (VTI-ACL-041); a test covers
  every Act.

  Departed-granter review (§6.3). A removed, narrowed or expired granter's
  grants become one acl.grants.review action for the holders who may approve
  vtc.roles.assign (the subjects excluded): approve re-affirms each grant the
  approver covers, decline withdraws at once, a lapse is withdrawn by the
  delegation sweeper (kept as the backstop; it now also notices expired
  granters).

  Key rollover. acl/swap-key/0.1 rolls the signer's own entry to a new key with
  exactly its authority (VTI-CLT-025 – 032, VTI-ACL-052): no console key, a
  required short-lived VP-JWT link proof from the new key addressed to the VTC,
  AclKeyRotated audited before one atomic move_if_unchanged, the member row and
  delegatedBy pointers following the key, old sessions revoked. A member's own
  rotation now re-points delegations too. cnm community continue rotates the
  granted key this way; cnm community rotate rotates a configured one
  (vtc-client: VtcClient::acl_swap_key). Note: VTI-ACL-054 – 058 (hand-off
  markers) are a different mechanism and are not implemented here.

  Backup restore. backup/finalize-import with confirm: true is previewed, then
  parked (Act::RestoreBackup) for the holders of vtc.backup.restore; approvers see
  the payload without its password, and the staged bundle is kept alive for the
  action's lifetime.

  Console. auth/whoami returns the caller's live capabilities (the published
  member) and ext["org.openvtc"].{adminRole, approves}; navigation and action
  buttons render per capability; a Roles page lists, defines and deletes roles
  through the action list; the new action kinds have pinned summary templates.

- **vtc**: Single-administrator mode, set at install, for communities with one administrator (VTI-APV-022) ([#1925](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1925))

A community run by one person has nobody to give second-party consent
  (VTI-APV-014, -018 - 020). Without this, its administrator could add a
  colleague or change an authority rule only through the offline break-glass.
  VTI-APV-022 lets a node run in single-administrator mode instead. This
  implements it at the VTC.

  - Config: `[acl] single_admin_mode` (default false). Host configuration
    only (item 1). It is read at start, kept out of the runtime registry,
    and refused by name by `config/patch` and `vtc/config/import`, with the
    host-side fix in the refusal. It is written to config.toml only when on.
  - Setup: `vtc setup --single-admin` (interactive and `--from`),
    `single_admin_mode = true` in the setup TOML, and an interactive
    "Run as a single-administrator community?" (default No). Setup warns when
    it is chosen beside `co_admin_did`, because the mode has no effect while
    that administrator is eligible.
  - Gate: where the approver set is empty and the mode is on, the consent
    gate neither refuses nor parks. The requester's operation-bound step-up
    (VTI-APV-015) stands in for the consent. Spending it writes a Critical
    `SingleAdminMode{consentWaived}` audit row naming the requirement, task,
    kind and digest. The row is written before the write, and a failure to
    audit refuses the operation. Once the write lands, the operation enters
    the action history marked `ext.org.openvtc.consentWaived`. A non-empty
    approver set parks exactly as before (item 2).
  - Reductions (VTI-APV-019) are unchanged and keep their cooling-off.
    Removing the subject at once would let one credential first remove the
    only other eligible party and then act on the waiver
    (vtc-action-list.md section 8.5).
  - Boot (item 4): Critical `inEffect` at every start with the mode on, and
    `enabled`/`disabled` when the value differs from the last start (stored in
    the install keyspace). A start that cannot audit does not proceed.
  - Visibility (item 3): `vtc/admin/actions/list` carries
    `ext.org.openvtc.singleAdminMode`. The console shows a permanent,
    non-dismissable banner on every page and a dashboard tile, and marks
    waived operations in Actions. `cnm actions list` prints a notice and marks
    waived operations.
  - Docs: admin-access section 2.1a, bootstrap runbook, non-interactive setup
    and example TOML, vtc-action-list section 8.5, vtc-admin-roles section 7,
    the infographic, and CLAUDE.md.

  Adds the `AuditEvent::SingleAdminMode` variant to vti-common. The enum is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is additive.

- **vtc**: Administration is role-based — capabilities, built-in roles and explicit act scope (VTI-ACL-030 – 037, VTI-APV-018) ([#1924](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1924))

  reads "admin with an empty context list" as unrestricted: it carries explicit
  administrative authority beside its community role.

  Model (vtc-service/src/acl/capability.rs, entry.rs)
  - VtcAclEntry gains adminRole (seven built-ins: community-admin, moderator,
    vetting-lead, repo-manager, credential-officer, auditor, approver; custom
    roles are a C2 placeholder), act all|none, capabilities ceiling|none|listed
    with resource qualifiers (git-ns, git-repo, policy, criterion) and additive
    grants, approve and approveCapabilities. Absent means none.
  - A typed registry of 20 capabilities with authority-conferring flags. The
    effective set is ceiling ∩ listed (plus additive), and every gate asks one
    question: entry.can(capability, resource). No authority list is tested
    with is_empty().

  Gates (§4)
  - Every require_super_admin / is_super_admin / "any admin" gate is replaced
    by the specific capability. Reads need any administrative role; writes need
    their capability. Console sign-in admits every administrative role. git-ns
    community-admin standing is git.ns.admin unqualified.
  - vtc/members/update refuses a move to or from a community role that implies
    an administrative role (moderator, issuer, admin) with adminRoleForbidden;
    acl/change-role carries the bound gesture for it.

  Consent (VTI-APV-018, -019, -009)
  - APV-014 generalises to any authority-conferring capability: approvers are
    holders of the same capability at a covering qualifier who may approve it;
    the requester (and, for a reduction, the subject) is excluded. A2's
    after_reduction, agreements, cooling-off, record_effect and notices are
    kept; actions record the capabilities at stake. An expiry put on or brought
    forward is a reduction of everything the entry holds. The last holder of
    vtc.roles.assign is never removed.

  Granting bounds (§6.3; VTI-ACL-031, -033, -042, -050, -053, -071)
  - A granter must hold each capability and vtc.roles.assign at a qualifier at
    least as wide, may confer approve only within its own, never past its own
    expiry, never to itself. delegatedBy is recorded. A departed or narrowed
    granter's grants go under review and are withdrawn after the action
    lifetime unless re-affirmed (review listing + sweeper, not an action-list

  Wire
  - acl/{grant,update,show,list,revoke,change-role}/0.2 are served with the
    generated trust_tasks_rs types beside 0.1, mapped per acl/_shared/0.2
    CONVENTIONS §8; an entry 0.1 cannot express is refused at 0.1. Six 0.2
    summary templates are pinned (Rust and console).

  Migration (§9)
  - At boot, before anything is authorized, every ACL row in the pre-role shape
    is rewritten in place with the same mapping a backup import uses. All rows
    are mapped before any is written, and each is one put, so a refusal or a
    crash leaves no half-migrated row. A second boot is a no-op. The run is
    audited once (new AuditEvent::AclMigrated, Critical: counts plus the
    context-scoped admins left with no administrative role), and those losses
    are raised as an acknowledge item for the remaining community-admins
    (VTI-VTC-023; new pinned template, urn:openvtc:vtc:operator:acl-migration).
    A row that cannot be mapped refuses the boot, naming the DID and the
    offline fix (vtc acl remove, which now removes an undecodable row, then
    vtc acl add). It is never dropped.
  - Backup import maps legacy rows: unrestricted admin -> community-admin,
    context-scoped admin -> no administrative role (listed for re-grant in the
    import report), moderator / issuer -> the matching role, custom -> none.
  - Install bootstrap and the co-admin are community-admins; offline
    `vtc acl add --role admin` writes a community-admin, and gains
    --admin-role and --capability cap[@resource]; --contexts is refused.

  Clients
  - vtc-client gains the 0.2 calls; cnm access list/show/grant/update use 0.2
    with --admin-role / --capability / --approve.
  - The console's Access control shows each entry's administrative role and
    capabilities, adds and edits with role and capability narrowing, and no
    longer calls a least-privilege entry "all" ([#746](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/746)).

- **vtc**: Operator writes need acknowledging, reductions notify and cool off, and execution survives a crash (VTI-VTC-023, VTI-APV-019) ([#1920](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1920))

Phase A2 of the administrator action list (docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md).

- **vtc**: An approver device can be an administrator's step-up factor (VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-016) ([#1919](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1919))

An administrator who signs in with a VTA wallet holds no passkey at the
  community, so every operation behind the operation-bound step-up was refused
  for them. A step-up approver — an Ed25519 did:key bound to one subject as
  their step-up factor, such as the browser plugin's approver identity — can
  now answer it.

  - Gate: the inline request is auth/step-up/approve-request/0.4, accepting
    `approverSigned` (naming the subject's approvers) and/or `webauthn`.
    auth/step-up/approve-response/0.6 carries the approver's attest/0.1
    statement, verified as received against this service's own pending
    record; the answer itself must be signed by the subject's own DID, never
    a console key. Once a subject holds a dedicated factor (approver or
    step-up passkey) their session passkeys stop counting. Audited as
    OperationStepUpApproved with the evidence kind and approver DID.
  - Store: new backed-up keyspace `step_up_approvers`; one approver DID per
    subject, once (revoked DIDs are burned), at most five per subject,
    distinct from the subject's DID, DID-document keys and every console key,
    checked at enrolment and at every use (VTI-APV-015 as amended).
  - Enrolment on the signed-document spine, every binding resting on an anchor
    independent of the subject's signing key and audited with `enrolledVia`
    (VTI-APV-016): auth/step-up/approver/{invite,redeem/start,redeem/finish}
    (R2), enroll (R3, behind a factor already held, bound to the terms
    digest), list and revoke; vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.3 (R1,
    claim under the token's DID verified against its live document, binding
    written at bootstrap); `vtc admin enrol-approver` (R4, offline invite,
    audited at boot as a break-glass).
  - Console: approverSigned via a feature-detected window.vtaWallet
    approveStepUp, falling back to WebAuthn; Approver devices card; member
    invite; redemption page.

- **vtc**: Consent-gated operations wait in an action list and complete on the N-th approval (VTI-APV-017) ([#1918](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1918))

A VTC operation that needs other administrators' approval -- an unrestricted
  grant (VTI-APV-014), a reduction of another unrestricted admin (VTI-APV-019),
  a lowered consent threshold (VTI-APV-020), an authority-policy change
  (VTI-VTC-022) -- is no longer refused with `auth:consent_required` and re-sent.
  Phase A1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md.

  Once every other check passes and the requester's operation-bound step-up is
  spent (VTI-APV-015), the operation is parked as an action in the new
  `admin_actions` keyspace (excluded from backup: it binds the ACL as it stood on
  this host). The record keeps the requester's signed document verbatim, the
  payload, requester, step-up evidence, approver set, threshold, one challenge
  per approver, a state pin and its lifetime. The requester is answered
  `trust-task-next-step/0.1` (202, continuation `proceed`, expecting
  `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.1` with the action id) and never sends it again.

  Approvers decide with `task-consent/decision/0.1` or `/0.2`, signed by their
  own DID (a delegated console key is refused). The approval that reaches the
  threshold moves the action out of `open` under a lock -- so concurrent final
  approvals execute it once -- and dispatches the stored document through the
  handler it was submitted to, re-running every check against the community as
  it is then; the consent gate re-checks approver eligibility, threshold and
  state pin. It closes `completed`, or `failed` with nothing written. One deny
  closes it for everyone; the requester can cancel; it expires; it is
  invalidated when the requester loses authority, the pinned state moves, or the
  eligible approvers can no longer reach the threshold (VTI-APV-004/-005/-006/
  -007/-008/-009/-017). Freshness and replay are held once, at submission
  (VTI-OPS-024..027).

  decision/0.2 `webauthn` evidence is verified against the approver's passkeys
  with user verification required, as an additional factor. `approverSigned`
  evidence is refused (evidenceInvalid, approverSignedUnsupported) until the
  approver store lands.

  New config keys, runtime-patchable: acl.action_lifetime (72 h, 15 min-14 d),
  acl.action_max_open_per_requester (5, 1-20), acl.action_max_open (50,
  10-500), acl.action_decline_cooldown (1 h, 0-24 h). More than three actions by
  one requester in ten minutes writes a Critical `AdminActionBurst` audit row
  and flags approvers' cards; an approver may decide at most ten a minute
  (VTI-APV-021, section 7a.1).

  Summaries are templates as data (title/effect prose, JSON Pointer fields, a
  closed format set) keyed by (kind, typeUri), each pinned by digest in the
  build, with shared vectors run by the service and the console (VTI-APV-011,
  -013).

  Served on the signed-document spine: vtc/admin/actions/{list,show,cancel,
  acknowledge}/0.1 (acknowledge answers notAcknowledgeable until A2 raises
  acknowledge items), with conformance witnesses and declared-code witnesses.



### Fixed

- **vtc**: Removing an administrator, lowering the consent threshold and changing authority policy take a second party (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-020, VTI-VTC-022) ([#1917](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1917))

* fix(vtc)!: removing an administrator, lowering the consent threshold and changing authority policy take a second party (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-020, VTI-VTC-022)

  One unrestricted administrator could undo VTI-APV-014 alone: remove every
  other administrator one at a time, lower the consent threshold back to 1, and
  rewrite the policy that decides authority (vtc-action-list.md §8.1, holes 1-3).
  These are the stop-gaps of §7b, built on the consent machinery that already
  exists. Each is replaced by its action-list rule once that lands.

  1. Removals and demotions of an administrator take the requester's
     operation-bound step-up (VTI-APV-019). acl/revoke (removal and scope
     reduction), a downward acl/change-role, an acl/update or acl/grant rewrite
     that takes authority from a live admin (narrowed scopes, an expiry brought
     forward), and vtc/members/admin-remove of an admin all go through
     bound_step_up::redeem_or_request. When the subject is another live
     unrestricted admin they also take consent through admin_consent, from the
     unrestricted admins other than BOTH the requester and the subject (approver
     set `unrestricted-admins-except-subject`; the subject's decision is refused
     as notAnApprover). Where that set is empty (two unrestricted admins), the
     step-up suffices, and once the write lands it is audited as the new
     `AuthorityReducedUnopposed` event at AuditSeverity::Critical; a removal also
     sends the subject the signed removal notice. The attrition guards
     (check_attrition, lock_admin_set, last-admin) are unchanged and still run;
     attrition is also asked before the gesture so a stranded removal never asks
     for one. Removing an expired or non-admin entry is unchanged.
     vtc/members/update can no longer demote an admin (it has no operation to
     bind a gesture to) and names acl/change-role instead.

  2. Lowering acl.unrestricted_admin_consent_threshold, by config/patch or an
     applied vtc/config/import, takes the requester's step-up and consent at the
     threshold as it stands (VTI-APV-020), pinned to that value. Raising it, or
     leaving it unchanged, stays immediate; the meetable check is unchanged.

  3. policy/upsert/0.2 and policy/activate/0.1 require an unrestricted admin
     (require_super_admin), not any admin. For the purposes that decide authority
     (roleChange, removal, join, crossCommunityRoles, gitNamespace —
     PolicyPurpose::decides_authority) they also take the step-up and consent of
     another unrestricted admin (VTI-VTC-022). The upload and activation checks
     run before the gate, so a module that would be refused asks nobody.

  4. vtc/members/admin-remove applies acl/revoke's scope-cover check
     (caller_covers_target, VTI-ACL-050): an entry the actor cannot see answers
     as not found, one it does not fully cover is refused.

  admin_consent is generalised over an `Act` (GrantUnrestricted,
  ReduceUnrestricted, LowerThreshold, ChangeAuthorityPolicy) that decides the
  approvers, the refusal wording, what the approvers are shown and the state the
  consent is pinned to. require and gesture_then_consent keep their signatures
  and are Act::GrantUnrestricted, so APV-014 is unchanged. TaskError gains a
  StepUp variant so a gate deep in an operation refuses with the ceremony inline.

This adopts it. - trust-tasks-rs and its sibling crates move to 0.27.1, in lockstep with the TDK release built on it: affinidi-tdk 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33, affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.18 (mediator 0.37), and affinidi-messaging-mediator-{admin,tui} 0.8. The graph holds one trust-tasks-rs (and one trust-tasks-proof), so the mediator `MediatorAcl` is one type and no bridge is needed. 0.27.0's typed git-ns `ActivityItem.source` needed no change: the VTC builds that response from JSON, and its wire is unchanged. - `vtc/admin/actions/{list,show,cancel,acknowledge}/0.2` are served beside 0.1. At 0.2 a cooling-off (VTI-APV-019) is category `coolingOff` with `landsAt` and `cancellableBy: requester`, no threshold, expiry or approvers remaining, closes `landedAfterCoolingOff`, and its subject sees it as `callerRole: subject` in `all` and `history`, never `waitingForMe`. 0.1 keeps answering as before (`ext["org.openvtc"].coolingOff`, `thresholdMet`). A parked operation's next step expects show/0.2. vtc-client, cnm and the console use 0.2; cnm and the console count down to `landsAt`. - A reduction parked for its cooling-off sends the subject `vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice/0.1` (durable push). The landing still sends the authority-reduced notice (`unopposed`); a cancelled one reduces and sends nothing more. Landing never waits on delivery. - An operator's offline write (VTI-VTC-023), the emergency bootstrap included, is raised with `typeUri` the record type `vtc/operator/offline-write/0.1` and the record `{command, dids, host, at}` as payload, replacing the URN placeholder and four per-command templates with one pinned template. The emergency marker now records the recovery DID and the administrators it wiped. A document of the record type answers `unsupportedType`; the manifest census lists it as embedded-only. - The console approves with the admin's approver device through the plugin's `approveDecision` (vta-browser-plugin #293): the device signs a decision-purpose statement over the per-approver salted wire digest, and the wallet signs `task-consent/decision/0.2` carrying it as `approverSigned` evidence. Precedence: approver device, passkey, wallet signature alone, then the `cnm consent approve` guidance. - A crash between a `policy/upsert` revision write and its effect marker was reconciled `failed` although the revision existed, because the upsert moves no state pin (CLAUDE.md R2.1). An executing action's revision is now stored under an id derived from the action and execution (`admin_actions::policy_revision_id`), so the row is its own evidence. - **vtc**: Administration is role-based — capabilities, built-in roles and explicit act scope (VTI-ACL-030 – 037, VTI-APV-018) ([#1924](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1924)) Phase C1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-admin-roles.md. A VTC ACL entry no longer reads "admin with an empty context list" as unrestricted: it carries explicit administrative authority beside its community role. Model (vtc-service/src/acl/capability.rs, entry.rs) - VtcAclEntry gains adminRole (seven built-ins: community-admin, moderator, vetting-lead, repo-manager, credential-officer, auditor, approver; custom roles are a C2 placeholder), act all|none, capabilities ceiling|none|listed with resource qualifiers (git-ns, git-repo, policy, criterion) and additive grants, approve and approveCapabilities. Absent means none. - A typed registry of 20 capabilities with authority-conferring flags. The effective set is ceiling ∩ listed (plus additive), and every gate asks one question: entry.can(capability, resource). No authority list is tested with is_empty(). Gates (§4) - Every require_super_admin / is_super_admin / "any admin" gate is replaced by the specific capability. Reads need any administrative role; writes need their capability. Console sign-in admits every administrative role. git-ns community-admin standing is git.ns.admin unqualified. - vtc/members/update refuses a move to or from a community role that implies an administrative role (moderator, issuer, admin) with adminRoleForbidden; acl/change-role carries the bound gesture for it. Consent (VTI-APV-018, -019, -009) - APV-014 generalises to any authority-conferring capability: approvers are holders of the same capability at a covering qualifier who may approve it; the requester (and, for a reduction, the subject) is excluded. A2's after_reduction, agreements, cooling-off, record_effect and notices are kept; actions record the capabilities at stake. An expiry put on or brought forward is a reduction of everything the entry holds. The last holder of vtc.roles.assign is never removed. Granting bounds (§6.3; VTI-ACL-031, -033, -042, -050, -053, -071) - A granter must hold each capability and vtc.roles.assign at a qualifier at least as wide, may confer approve only within its own, never past its own expiry, never to itself. delegatedBy is recorded. A departed or narrowed granter's grants go under review and are withdrawn after the action lifetime unless re-affirmed (review listing + sweeper, not an action-list item). Wire - acl/{grant,update,show,list,revoke,change-role}/0.2 are served with the generated trust_tasks_rs types beside 0.1, mapped per acl/_shared/0.2 CONVENTIONS §8; an entry 0.1 cannot express is refused at 0.1. Six 0.2 summary templates are pinned (Rust and console). Migration (§9) - At boot, before anything is authorized, every ACL row in the pre-role shape is rewritten in place with the same mapping a backup import uses. All rows are mapped before any is written, and each is one put, so a refusal or a crash leaves no half-migrated row. A second boot is a no-op. The run is audited once (new AuditEvent::AclMigrated, Critical: counts plus the context-scoped admins left with no administrative role), and those losses are raised as an acknowledge item for the remaining community-admins (VTI-VTC-023; new pinned template, urn:openvtc:vtc:operator:acl-migration). A row that cannot be mapped refuses the boot, naming the DID and the offline fix (vtc acl remove, which now removes an undecodable row, then vtc acl add). It is never dropped. - Backup import maps legacy rows: unrestricted admin -> community-admin, context-scoped admin -> no administrative role (listed for re-grant in the import report), moderator / issuer -> the matching role, custom -> none. - Install bootstrap and the co-admin are community-admins; offline `vtc acl add --role admin` writes a community-admin, and gains --admin-role and --capability cap[@resource]; --contexts is refused. Clients - vtc-client gains the 0.2 calls; cnm access list/show/grant/update use 0.2 with --admin-role / --capability / --approve. - The console's Access control shows each entry's administrative role and capabilities, adds and edits with role and capability narrowing, and no longer calls a least-privilege entry "all" ([#746](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/746)). - **cnm**: Setup onboards the personal VTA the way pnm does — self-minted key, grant, rotate ([#1923](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1923)) `cnm setup` used to require a sealed bundle from an administrator before cnm could touch the personal VTA. It now follows pnm's admin cold start: mint an ephemeral did:key, park it, print the grant routes (`vta import-did`, `admin_did` in setup.toml, `pnm acl create`), and on `cnm setup continue [] [--vta-did ] [--vta-url ]` authenticate, which rotates to a fresh did:key over `acl/swap-key` and removes the temp DID's entry. A continue before the grant prints the routes and stays resumable. Non-interactive mode mirrors pnm ([#1753](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1753)): `cnm setup --name [--overwrite]` and `continue --vta-did` each print one `{slug, admin_did, state}` line. Alternatives in the wizard: - "Bootstrap from your existing pnm session" when a pnm profile on this machine ($PNM_HOME honoured) is bound to the same VTA DID. pnm's config and session store are read only; pnm's key authenticates in memory once, over REST (so no mediator socket is taken from a running pnm), to grant cnm's own freshly minted key, which then rotates as above. The grant is an unrestricted admin: cnm creates a top-level context per community on the personal VTA, which the VTA gates on super-admin. - "I have a sealed bundle from an admin" — unchanged, digest pinned. Communities now get an admin identity each, so one operator's communities share no key. `cnm community add [--vtc-did] [--vta-did] [--slug] [--overwrite]` mints a did:key for that community, parks it in `pending_communities` (not selectable by --community or as default until confirmed), and prints the VTC grant routes: `co_admin_did` in vtc setup, `vtc acl add` offline, or an existing admin's `cnm access grant` / console, noting the second-administrator approval an online unrestricted grant waits for. `cnm community continue [--vtc-did] [--vta-did]` confirms with a DI-signed authenticate to the VTC (VTC audience) before promoting the profile. The VTC has no key-rotation task (no acl/swap-key; a successor admin entry is itself an unrestricted grant needing a second admin's consent, VTI-APV-014), so the minted key is kept rather than a rotation invented. Reusing another community's key takes `--reuse-identity ` (or an explicit, warned choice in the wizard). `cnm community list` shows each community's identity and the pending ones; `delete` drops a pending one. Holding a community identity as a persona on the personal VTA is a follow-up. - **vtc**: Consent-gated operations wait in an action list and complete on the N-th approval (VTI-APV-017) ([#1918](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1918)) A VTC operation that needs other administrators' approval -- an unrestricted grant (VTI-APV-014), a reduction of another unrestricted admin (VTI-APV-019), a lowered consent threshold (VTI-APV-020), an authority-policy change (VTI-VTC-022) -- is no longer refused with `auth:consent_required` and re-sent. Phase A1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md. Once every other check passes and the requester's operation-bound step-up is spent (VTI-APV-015), the operation is parked as an action in the new `admin_actions` keyspace (excluded from backup: it binds the ACL as it stood on this host). The record keeps the requester's signed document verbatim, the payload, requester, step-up evidence, approver set, threshold, one challenge per approver, a state pin and its lifetime. The requester is answered `trust-task-next-step/0.1` (202, continuation `proceed`, expecting `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.1` with the action id) and never sends it again. Approvers decide with `task-consent/decision/0.1` or `/0.2`, signed by their own DID (a delegated console

title: Single-administrator mode is one person, under as many identifiers as they hold (VTI-APV-022, VTI-ACL-052)
body:
VTI-APV-022 waived consent only where no eligible party but the requester
existed (item 2). It counted entries, and entries are not people: one person
holding an administrator entry per device was asked to approve their own
requests from another of their own devices, which is the multi-step ceremony
the mode exists to remove, with no second mind behind any step of it.

The node cannot tell one person's identifiers from two people's, so the mode
no longer tries. In single-administrator mode consent is waived whether or
not other administrators' entries exist; the mode SHOULD be enabled only
where every administrator is the same person (new item 2), and stays what it
was otherwise: host-only, a gesture bound to each operation, reported to
every administrator in every session — so a second person who does exist
sees it — and audited at the highest severity.

VTI-ACL-052's single-administrator exception follows: any holder of
unrestricted act scope may edit its own entry in the mode, not only the sole
holder, still refused where the edit would leave no unrestricted entry.
VTI-APV-019's removal conditions (re-authentication, notice, highest
severity) already apply wherever the mode waives a consent.

title: A subject may relabel its own entry, and a sole administrator in single-administrator mode may edit its own (VTI-ACL-052)
body:
VTI-ACL-052 forbade every self-edit but rotation, which also forbade two
edits it was never aimed at:

- The label. It is on no axis of authority (VTI-ACL-001), so a subject that
  relabels itself gains nothing a bound could have withheld. The remaining
  risk is a misleading self-description; the change is audited and SHOULD be
  shown to others as self-set.
- A community run by one person. Its sole holder of unrestricted act scope
  already holds every axis, so an edit to its own entry cannot widen
  anything, and there is nobody else to make the edit for it. In
  single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022) that subject may edit its own
  entry under the mode's conditions: a re-authentication bound to the
  operation (VTI-APV-015), the highest audit severity, and never an edit
  that leaves the node without an unrestricted entry.

The rationale for VTI-ACL-052 / VTI-ACL-053 says why neither exception
reopens the bypass the pair closes.

title: fix(did-git-sign): init finds persona DIDs across the context and its sub-contexts
body:
## Problem

`did-git-sign init --profile bob --vta-did <VTA> --context openvtc-bob` showed:

```
openvtc-bob — OpenVTC BOB (no DID)
openvtc-bob/qme5theer1qr — did:webvh:Qme5…:first-vtc (no DID)
```

Then it listed DIDs in the exact chosen context, found none, and offered to create a new did:webvh. That DID has no git rights in any community.

## Where openvtc puts persona DIDs

Read from openvtc `origin/main`:

- **Every persona has a sub-context of its own** under the account's top context: `<top>/<slug>` (`openvtc-core/src/config/context_path.rs` `build_sub_context_id`/`child_path`).
  - A **standalone persona** (`create_persona.rs`, `auto_context`) takes its slug from the persona label.
  - A **persona minted while joining a community** (`join_flow.rs`) takes its slug from the community's display name. When the community has no name, the slug comes from the VTC DID's SCID instead (`fallback_token`, e.g. `openvtc-bob/qme5theer1qr`).
- The persona's keys and DID are created in that sub-context (`community_context::ensure_context`, then `create_persona_keys` / `create_did_via_server(context_id)`).
- `create_did_webvh` is called with `set_primary: false`, so **no context ever has a primary DID**.
- The top context (`config.account.top_context_id`, e.g. `openvtc-bob`) holds no persona DID itself.

## What the VTA does (VTI `origin/main`)

- `vta/webvh/dids/list` (`operations/did_webvh/lifecycle.rs`) filters `contextId` by **exact** match.
- With **no** filter, it returns every DID whose context passes `auth.has_context_access`. That check is segment-aware: an admin of a parent context covers the whole subtree (`vti-common` `ActScope::covers`).
- `keys/list` (`operations/keys.rs`) also filters `contextId` exactly, with the same subtree-aware visibility check.

So did-git-sign makes one unfiltered `dids/list` call and selects the subtree itself. That costs one round trip in total, not one per context.

## Changes

- **Finding the DID.** `init` matches the chosen context and everything under it, segment by segment: `ctx` and `ctx/…` match, `ctx-other` does not.
  - Context labels show how many DIDs are in each subtree (`2 DIDs`, `no DIDs`). The primary DID is still shown, after the count, when one is pinned.
  - The DID picker shows each DID's name, through `names::inline`, and the context it lives in.
  - When there is exactly one DID, `init` uses it and says which one.
- **Creating a DID (changes the default 0.12.1 introduced).** `init` offers to create a DID only when the whole subtree has none. The prompt is: "No DID found in <ctx> or its sub-contexts. A new DID has no git rights in any community until granted. Create one?", and the default answer is **No**. Under `--yes` it never creates one. It stops instead, and says to point `--context` at the context holding the persona, or to run `pnm did-mgmt dids create --context …`.
- **Key picker.**
  - Keys are listed from the chosen DID's own context, not the selected context.
  - Only the DID's own `assertionMethod` Ed25519 keys are offered. Which keys count is decided by `vgi_core::ed25519_signing_keys_from_doc`, the same rule the verifier uses.
  - Each key is shown with the `DID#key-N` it signs as.
  - The old `resolve_did_key_fragment` fell back to `#key-0` when it could not match a key. That fallback is gone: a DID with no matching key now fails with a clear error.
- **Grant command.** `pnm contexts create` fails for a context that already exists, so `init` now prints both commands:
  - If `<ctx>` does not exist yet: `pnm contexts create … --admin-did <setup> --admin-expires 1h --admin-handoff`
  - If it already exists: `pnm acl create --did <setup> --role admin --contexts <ctx> --expires 1h --handoff`

  Both sets of flags were checked against the local `pnm … --help`.
- README Setup and RUNBOOK §3 are updated to match.

No version bump; the release commit does that.

## Tests

New unit tests in `main.rs`:

- subtree matching (`ctx`, `ctx/x`, `ctx/a/b`, `ctx-other`, `ctxby/x`, child vs parent)
- collecting and ordering DIDs across a subtree
- context and DID labels
- `--yes` refuses to create without prompting, the prompt defaults to No, and declining refuses
- the key filter: assertion keys only, relative and embedded methods, bare and multicodec `publicKey`, X25519 excluded
- the grant command text for both paths

Checks run: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p did-git-sign --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p did-git-sign` (93 + 7 + 2 + 2 passing).

title: fix(did-git-sign): init finds persona DIDs across the context and its sub-contexts (#135)
body:
fix(did-git-sign): init finds persona DIDs across the context and its sub-contexts (#135)

openvtc keeps every persona in a sub-context of the account context
(`<account>/<slug>`) and pins no primary DID, so `init --context openvtc-bob`
showed every context as "no DID", listed DIDs of the exact context only,
found none, and offered to create a new DID with no git rights anywhere.

- One unfiltered `webvh/dids/list` (the VTA filters `contextId` exactly, and
  with no filter returns every DID the caller's subtree-aware ACL covers);
  the chosen context's subtree is selected client-side, segment-aware.
- Context labels count the DIDs in each subtree; the primary DID is extra
  information only when pinned. The DID picker shows each DID's name and
  context; a single DID is used and named.
- Creation is offered only for an empty subtree, defaults to No, and is
  never done under --yes (which bails with guidance). This changes the
  default 0.12.1 introduced.
- The key picker lists only the chosen DID's own assertionMethod Ed25519
  keys, from the DID's context, using vgi-core's signing-key rule; the
  silent `#key-0` fallback is gone.
- The printed grant covers an existing context too: `pnm acl create
  --role admin --contexts <ctx> --expires 1h --handoff` beside
  `pnm contexts create … --admin-handoff`.

title: chore: release 0.4.0
body:
Releases 0.4.0 for the 5 Oct demo. There have been no releases since 0.3.1 (15 Aug). It's a minor bump rather than a patch because the project is pre-1.0 and this range includes breaking changes (#397, #255, #362).

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: the workspace `version` goes from `0.3.1` to `0.4.0`, and the `openvtc-core` requirement from `0.3` to `0.4`.
- `openvtc-core/Cargo.toml`: `openvtc-vetting-pcs` goes from `0.3.1` to `0.4.0`.
- `Cargo.lock`: only the three workspace crates move (`cargo update --workspace`).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased]` becomes `[0.4.0] - 2026-10-04`, headed by a **Major changes** summary (vetted admission, guided join, DTG Credentials v1, personas and faces, communities, security, transport and setup, TUI) and a **Breaking** section. The detailed entries are unchanged below it, and an empty `[Unreleased]` stays at the top.

## Notes

- **Merge order with #423.** If #423 (the held-statements tab) merges first, I'll rebase so its entry lands in 0.4.0. If this merges first, #423's entry needs moving into a fresh Unreleased section.
- **Tagging and publishing** are manual (#422) and not part of this PR.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- `git grep 0.3.1` finds no stray references outside the changelog and lockfile.

title: feat(vetting): held statements get a tab of their own
body:
The Vetting page counts held statements on its checklist, but none could be opened, so an applicant had no way to see what a vetter actually signed. This adds a **Vetting** tab to My Credentials, beside Membership. It's useful for the 5 Oct demo: after a session, the applicant can open the statement they just received.

The change is client-only, with no protocol, VTA or VTC change.

## Behaviour

- **List.** One row per held statement, across every application (`VettingBook::applications[*].statements`). Each row names the vetter (contact alias, then verified agent name, then DID, as on the other tabs), then the method and community, e.g. `in person · Kernel Developers`, then the validity window.
- **Detail.** The usual headline (`Vetting statement · valid`), issued by, about and valid lines, followed by what the vetter signed:
  - `For`: the community, labelled the way the Membership tab labels it;
  - `Method`;
  - `Declared`: the relationship they declared;
  - `Relied on`: the documents they relied on, when any;
  - `Verified`: the claims they verified;
  - `Received`.

  Then the ID and the raw credential. `c` copies the JSON.
- **No removal.** A statement belongs to its application, so `d` does nothing on this tab, as on Membership. The detail footer now leaves out `d: remove` on both tabs rather than advertising a key that does nothing.
- **Status is the window only.** Whether a vetter has withdrawn a statement is the community's to record (design §9.6). The tab claims nothing about revocation (R6.3).
- **Persistence.** Applications keep their statements after the join, so members see theirs too.

## Code

- `CredentialsState::active_list()` replaces the per-tab `match` that was repeated in five places across the panel and key handler. `CredentialTab::allows_local_removal()` replaces the `!= Membership` check.
- `VrcSummary` gains two display fields: `note` (shown after the name in the list) and `facts` (labelled lines in the detail view). Existing constructors set them empty, so the other tabs render exactly as before.
- `collect_vetting_statements` in `state_handler/main_page/mod.rs` builds the rows. Every peer-supplied string goes through `sanitize_display`.
- The design doc's §12.3 as-built note and the CHANGELOG are updated.

## Testing

- `a_held_statement_is_listed_with_what_the_vetter_signed`: the row's issuer, subject, status, note and each fact.
- `an_application_without_statements_lists_none`.
- `credential_detail_d_does_nothing_on_the_vetting_tab`.
- `switch_tab_cycles_and_resets_index` now covers Membership → Vetting → Received.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass. `cargo test -p openvtc` passes (786).

**Not checked in a running TUI.** The rendering path is shared with the existing tabs, but nobody has looked at the new tab on screen yet.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no network code
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): no network code
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): read-only view
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): none touched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): none touched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire types changed
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): status is the validity window and says nothing about revocation
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: ci(release): at most two semver checks at once in the Release PR job
body:
#1938 measured 91 GB free on / at the start of the run that then died the
same way (runner lost 13 minutes into "Checking API compatibility", "The
operation was canceled" with no newer push), so the disk was never the
cause: memory is. release-plz semver-checks every changed crate in a pool of
`available_parallelism` workers with no setting for it, and the release
pending since #1918 touches eleven crates, so four cold dependency builds
the size of vta-service's run at once.

release-plz runs `cargo-semver-checks` from PATH, so put a gate ahead of
the real binary that admits two checks at a time (two flock slots), and log
what it admits next to a 30 s memory sample. Reverts #1938's SDK deletion
and halved build jobs, which addressed neither.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: ci(mobile): the cross-compile builds dependencies unoptimised again
body:
#1931 set `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2` so tests spend less
time running dependencies. Mobile build runs nothing — it checks that
vta-mobile-core cross-compiles for five targets and that its bindings
generate — and paid the optimisation once per target, about 14 minutes
each. A job that took 39-57 minutes before has run past its 60-minute
limit since (#1939 twice; main's runs for #1932-#1938 cancelled at 60).

A profile in a cargo config file takes precedence over the manifest's, so
the job writes the default back for itself; every other job keeps #1931.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): PR-open gate — close pull requests from openers the policy does not allow
body:
Builds on `git-ns/bridge/event/0.4` and `git-ns/bridge/job/0.5` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#723), published in trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3. The workspace floor is raised to `trust-tasks-rs = { version = "0.27.3", … }`. The sibling `trust-tasks-*` crates stay at `"0.27"`, and `Cargo.lock` moves only trust-tasks-rs, from 0.27.1 to 0.27.3.

## What

The VTC side of the pull-request gate. A community can now restrict who may open a pull request on the repositories it governs. The bridge reports each pull request opened or reopened (`git-ns/bridge/event/0.4` `pullRequestOpened`). The VTC checks the author against the community's pull-request policy. When the author is not allowed, the VTC queues a `closePullRequest` job (`git-ns/bridge/job/0.5`), and the bridge posts the community's message on the pull request and closes it (result steps `comment`, then `close`).

**This is hygiene, not the merge gate.** The required commit-trust check is still what keeps untrusted commits out. The gate fails open: if the VTC or bridge is down, if the bridge lacks job 0.5, or if a setting can't be read, the pull request stays open.

## Behaviour (event 0.4, request step 6)

- The VTC serves `git-ns/bridge/event/0.4` beside 0.1–0.3, so 0.4 is listed in `trust-task-discovery`. Older payloads are read as 0.4, and every 0.3 event kind works unchanged.
- A pull request is ignored unless its repository is recorded `active` in a bridge-mode namespace. It is also ignored when the level in force is `anyone`.
- The author's account is matched by forge + id, never by login, through account links to a member. These are **always allowed**:
  - an owner or maintainer of the repository, explicit or implied (a namespace admin included);
  - the bridge's own app account (`<slug>[bot]`);
  - a login in `pr_exempt`.
- Per level, the linked holder must be:
  - `members`: a current member;
  - `committers`: a holder of `git.commit.sign`, explicit or implied (namespace-wide grants included);
  - `maintainers`: `maintain` or higher;
  - `{"roles": [...]}`: a member whose ACL role is listed.
- An account linked to nobody is allowed only under `anyone`.
- **Reopen:** a reopen by an owner, a maintainer or the bridge is an override and is never closed again. A reopen by anyone else re-checks the author exactly as an opening does.
- The message is rendered from the template using only `{author}` (login), `{repo}` (owner/name), `{community}` and `{join_hint}`. No DID, membership state, role or reason goes into it. A value that doesn't look like a login is not rendered. The message is capped at 16384 characters.

## Settings (`gitNamespace` policy `settings`)

| key | default |
|---|---|
| `pr_open` | `"anyone"` (no behaviour change) |
| `pr_open_overrides` | `{}`: `{"github.com/acme[/repo]": level}`; the repository's entry wins over the namespace's, which wins over `pr_open` |
| `pr_exempt` | `["dependabot[bot]"]` |
| `pr_close_message` | built-in Markdown template |
| `pr_join_hint` | derived from the community profile (public URL if set) |

An unreadable value is logged and falls back to that key's default (for `pr_open`, `anyone`). The shipped `git_ns.rego` sets the defaults and documents the keys.

## Job 0.4 vs 0.5

- Discovery now records `takesV0_5` beside `takesV0_4`.
- A bridge that lists 0.5 is sent **every** job as 0.5: 0.5 is a superset with the same meaning, and accepting 0.4 is only a SHOULD for such a bridge.
- A bridge that lists only 0.4 keeps getting 0.4 and never gets a `closePullRequest`.
- When the bridge is known to lack 0.5, the event handler queues nothing; it reads only the cached discovery answer, because it holds the store lock while the bridge waits for its acknowledgement. When the answer is unknown, the dispatcher asks the bridge and cancels the job.
- In both cases, the namespace's administrators get one `gitNs.pullRequest.gateUnenforced` activity row plus a log warning. They are told again only after the bridge has taken 0.5 and then lost it.

## Records

- Only closes are recorded:
  - the `closePullRequest` job, which shows in `activity/list` as `gitNs.job.closePullRequest`;
  - on a `succeeded` result with `close` applied, the audit row `gitNs.pullRequest.closed`, with detail `{number, author (login), level}`.
- A pull request that was allowed leaves no record.
- `closePullRequest` jobs are left out of `git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1`, because that spec's `JobKind` enum doesn't include the new kind (a spec gap in #723 — the list should be bumped with job 0.5).

## Not done

The configured level isn't shown on the namespace card or in `cnm git view --admin`: the namespace rows in `namespace/list/0.1` are `additionalProperties: false`. The docs say so.

## Tests

- Unit tests (`git_ns::pr_gate`): the decision table (each level, exempt, unlinked, owner/maintainer/bridge always allowed, reopen override vs re-check), settings parsing/validation/defaults/overrides, and message rendering (placeholders, one-pass substitution, login sanitising, length cap).
- Policy tests: the default gate is `anyone`, and settings are read from Rego.
- Integration tests (`git_ns::tests::pr_gate`): from the signed 0.4 event through dispatch to the 0.5 job, the result, and the audit row; the per-repo override; inactive repository and default policy (nothing happens); a bridge without 0.5 (no close and one notice, other jobs still sent as 0.4); every job sent as 0.5 to a 0.5 bridge; 0.3 event kinds under 0.4.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): PR-open gate — close pull requests from openers the policy does not allow (#1937)
body:
feat(vtc/git-ns): PR-open gate — close pull requests from openers the policy does not allow (#1937)

* feat(vtc/git-ns): PR-open gate — close pull requests from openers the policy does not allow

The VTC side of git-ns/bridge/event 0.4 (pullRequestOpened) and
git-ns/bridge/job 0.5 (closePullRequest), trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#723,
published in trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3 (now the workspace floor).

- bridge/event 0.4 is served (and so listed in trust-task-discovery) beside
  0.1-0.3, which are read as 0.4; every earlier event kind is unchanged.
- On pullRequestOpened for a repository recorded active in a bridge-mode
  namespace, the author (matched by forge + id through account links) is
  checked against the gitNamespace policy's new settings: pr_open
  ("anyone" default | members | committers | maintainers | {"roles": [...]}),
  pr_open_overrides (per namespace / repository), pr_exempt (default
  ["dependabot[bot]"]), pr_close_message and pr_join_hint. Owners and
  maintainers (explicit or implied), the bridge's app account and exempt
  logins are always allowed; unlinked accounts only under "anyone". A reopen
  by an owner, maintainer or the bridge is an override; anyone else's
  re-checks the author.
- A disallowed pull request gets a queued closePullRequest job whose message
  renders only {author} (login), {repo}, {community} and {join_hint}.
- Jobs go as 0.5 to a bridge that lists 0.5 and as 0.4 to a 0.4-only bridge;
  closePullRequest never goes to a bridge without 0.5, whose namespace's
  administrators are told once (gitNs.pullRequest.gateUnenforced).
- Only closes are recorded: the job (activity gitNs.job.closePullRequest) and,
  on a succeeded close, the audit row gitNs.pullRequest.closed
  {number, author login, level}. bridge/job/list 0.1 omits closePullRequest
  jobs, whose kind its JobKind enum does not yet name.

Hygiene, not the merge gate: the required commit-trust check is unchanged and
the gate fails open.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(claude): git-ns jobs go as 0.5 to bridges that list it (send_versioned)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): dispatch a Trust Task through a boxed router, not one 1.1 MiB poll frame

dispatch_typed was an async fn holding the whole routing match, so its
unoptimised poll frame carried every arm's handler future and temporaries —
measured at ~1.13 MiB (aarch64 debug) — under whichever handler ran. A
git-ns test thread needed ~2.08 MiB in all, and on Linux with vetting-pcs
git_ns::tests::reproject_is_an_owners_for_their_repository_only_and_refused_without_a_bridge
overflowed the 2 MiB test stack (the second time: #1907 grew the join path
and boxing three arms put it off).

dispatch_typed is now a plain fn returning the chosen arm's future, boxed
where it is chosen, so its frame is popped before any handler is polled.
The same test now passes with a 1.15 MiB stack (was 2.08 MiB). Routing is
unchanged: the same 70 arms, in the same order.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc/git-ns): serve git-ns/bridge/job/list 0.2 — closePullRequest jobs with their pull request number

trust-tasks-rs 0.27.4 (trust-tasks-tf #727) publishes bridge/job/list 0.2,
whose JobKind names job 0.5's closePullRequest and whose rows carry the
pull request number. The VTC now serves 0.2 beside 0.1: 0.2 lists every
job, a closePullRequest row with its number; 0.1 still leaves those jobs
out before paging, as 0.2 requires of a VTC answering 0.1.

The console asks 0.2 (list-limits, OpenAPI snapshot and wire.ts follow),
and labels the kind ("close pull request #N").

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: ci(release): the Release PR job fits eleven parallel semver checks
body:
release-plz runs the semver check for every changed crate in a pool of
`available_parallelism` workers (4 on ubuntu-latest), and each check builds
the crate's dependency tree twice, the crates.io baseline into a target dir
of its own. The pending release touches eleven crates, so four cold builds
run at once at cargo's default -j4. Since 2026-10-03 the job has died 11-20
minutes into "Checking API compatibility" on every push (exit 143, once
"The runner has received a shutdown signal"), with the 12 GiB swap in place,
and the Release PR has stayed stale since #1918.

Halve the build jobs per check, delete the ~20 GB of preinstalled Android,
.NET and GHC SDKs the job never uses (as ci.yml does), and sample memory and
disk every 30 s into a log printed after the run, so a recurrence names the
exhausted resource.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties
body:
A community in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022, #1925) has one
administrator. Fixed rule 7 of git-ns/right/grant/0.3 still refused every
elevated self-grant, so `cnm git adopt <repo> --owner <own DID>` failed with
git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. Break-glass left records nobody could ever ratify.

Single-administrator mode now reaches rule 7. It uses the same discipline as
the consent waiver (`git_ns::single_admin`):

- Only where nobody else is eligible. `others_eligible` reuses
  `admin_consent::approvers_for` over the namespace's `git.ns.admin`. That
  covers the break-glass deciders and any approve scope reaching them. It also
  counts any other member whose git rights could make this grant (rules 1 and
  2). One eligible party, or the mode off, and the refusal stands.
- Every path the rule covers: right/grant, repo/create (implied repo.create
  naming self as owner), repo/adopt naming self, namespace/reseat to self, and
  drift/resolve adopt for one's own account. The rules accept a `Waivable`
  token only for that exact actor, right and resource. Rules 1, 2 and 5, the
  granter-covers floor, the consent-class gate and policy all still apply.
- Requires the requester's operation-bound step-up. This is the break-glass
  mechanism (`bound_step_up`), bound to the document actually signed (for an
  adoption, the drift/resolve document).
- Writes a Critical `SingleAdminMode { event: selfGrantWaived }` audit row
  before the write. It names the rule, task, digest, git-ns action, right and
  resource. If the audit write fails, the operation is refused and nothing is
  recorded.
- Marks the result. The record carries `singleAdmin { at, task }`, which is
  never published. The answer carries `ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`.
  git-ns/view 0.4/0.5 lists waived records under the same ext member. The ACL
  resource grant shows `selfGrantWaived: true`. A `gitNs.right.selfGrantWaived`
  activity item is written.
- Counts for invariants. Waived records count toward the last-owner and
  last-admin invariants, unlike unratified break-glass.

cnm: `git grant|create|adopt|reseat|drift resolve` now sign and go through
the step-up flow `git break-glass` uses. They print a note before the gesture
and a "Single-administrator waiver applied" note after.

vti-common: `SingleAdminModeData` gains optional `right` and `resource`
fields and derives Default. The struct has not been released yet (it was added
in #1925, after vti-common 0.36.0), so this is not breaking against crates.io.
vtc-client adds additive type-URI constants and `self_grant_waived`.

Spec: rule 7 is a MUST naming break-glass as the only way. This is host
configuration, not policy, but it diverges from the rule's text until the git-ns
spec admits VTI-APV-022. The divergence is documented. The upstream change and
the Appendix F entry are not in this PR.

Docs: git-namespaces (separation of duties), admin-access §2.1a and §3.3,
vtc-action-list §8.5, bootstrap runbook, CLAUDE.md.

## Security reasoning

- The waiver never widens past VTI-APV-022 item 2. The eligibility test is the consent gate's own (`approvers_for`), plus anyone whose git rights could make the grant. That makes it stricter than #1925's set. As soon as a second administrator, or an owner who could grant, exists, rule 7 applies again.
- Rules 1, 2 and 5 still run, so nothing is granted that the actor could not grant to someone else. The `Waivable` token covers exactly one (actor, right, resource) and only `single_admin::waivable` can build one.
- The step-up is the break-glass gesture, bound by digest to the signed document and spent before the write. A console key alone cannot satisfy it.
- No waived write can land without its Critical audit row, because the row is written first and an audit failure refuses the operation. The mode itself stays host configuration only.

## Tests

- `git_ns::tests::single_admin` (10): sole admin adopt waived with step-up + Critical row ordered before the grant + record/answer/view/ACL markers + activity item; second admin present refused; repo owner who could grant present refused; mode off refused; audit failure refuses (gesture spent, nothing recorded); waived record counts for last-owner (`git-ns:lastOwner` on self-revoke); grant, repo/create (implied), reseat (also last-admin) and drift adopt each waived.
- `rules` unit tests: the waiver lifts rule 7 only for its exact grant, and rules 2 and 5 still bind; waived vs unratified break-glass invariant counting.
- vti-common round trip for `selfGrantWaived`; cnm note tests, including terminal-escape safety.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, and the `vetting-pcs` clippy all pass.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2739/2740 passed. The one failure, `action_list_a2::vti_apv_019_the_first_of_two_administrators_to_act_wins` (a reduction race test this PR doesn't touch), passes when re-run alone.
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -p cnm-cli`: 740/740 passed. Doctests pass. Admin UI `npm run lint` and vitest (752) pass. `check-authz-context-types.sh` OK.

## Not in this PR

- Upstream dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf change to rule 7, and the VTI spec Appendix F divergence entry.
- The console still pre-blocks self-grants client-side (`isSelfGrant`). Only the activity label and audit description were added there.

A community in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022, #1925) has one
administrator. Fixed rule 7 of git-ns/right/grant/0.3 still refused every
elevated self-grant, so `cnm git adopt <repo> --owner <own DID>` failed with
git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. Break-glass left records nobody could ever ratify.

Single-administrator mode now reaches rule 7. It uses the same discipline as
the consent waiver (`git_ns::single_admin`):

- Only where nobody else is eligible. `others_eligible` reuses
  `admin_consent::approvers_for` over the namespace's `git.ns.admin`. That
  covers the break-glass deciders and any approve scope reaching them. It also
  counts any other member whose git rights could make this grant (rules 1 and
  2). One eligible party, or the mode off, and the refusal stands.
- Every path the rule covers: right/grant, repo/create (implied repo.create
  naming self as owner), repo/adopt naming self, namespace/reseat to self, and
  drift/resolve adopt for one's own account. The rules accept a `Waivable`
  token only for that exact actor, right and resource. Rules 1, 2 and 5, the
  granter-covers floor, the consent-class gate and policy all still apply.
- Requires the requester's operation-bound step-up. This is the break-glass
  mechanism (`bound_step_up`), bound to the document actually signed (for an
  adoption, the drift/resolve document).
- Writes a Critical `SingleAdminMode { event: selfGrantWaived }` audit row
  before the write. It names the rule, task, digest, git-ns action, right and
  resource. If the audit write fails, the operation is refused and nothing is
  recorded.
- Marks the result. The record carries `singleAdmin { at, task }`, which is
  never published. The answer carries `ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`.
  git-ns/view 0.4/0.5 lists waived records under the same ext member. The ACL
  resource grant shows `selfGrantWaived: true`. A `gitNs.right.selfGrantWaived`
  activity item is written.
- Counts for invariants. Waived records count toward the last-owner and
  last-admin invariants, unlike unratified break-glass.

cnm: `git grant|create|adopt|reseat|drift resolve` now sign and go through
the step-up flow `git break-glass` uses. They print a note before the gesture
and a "Single-administrator waiver applied" note after.

vti-common: `SingleAdminModeData` gains optional `right` and `resource`
fields and derives Default. The struct has not been released yet (it was added
in #1925, after vti-common 0.36.0), so this is not breaking against crates.io.
vtc-client adds additive type-URI constants and `self_grant_waived`.

Spec: rule 7 is a MUST naming break-glass as the only way. This is host
configuration, not policy, but it diverges from the rule's text until the git-ns
spec admits VTI-APV-022. The divergence is documented. The upstream change and
the Appendix F entry are not in this PR.

Docs: git-namespaces (separation of duties), admin-access §2.1a and §3.3,
vtc-action-list §8.5, bootstrap runbook, CLAUDE.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-console): single-administrator mode lets the console send git self-grants for the VTC to waive

The console blocked every elevated git self-grant client-side (`isSelfGrant`),
so a lone administrator on a node in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022)
could not use the waiver the VTC now applies (`git_ns::single_admin`).

With the mode on (read from `ext.org.openvtc.singleAdminMode` on the shell's
action-list read, `useSingleAdminMode`), the grant, reseat, adopt, create and
drift-adopt forms no longer block a self-grant. They show "Single-administrator
mode: this self-grant will be waived, recorded as a critical audit event, and
needs your passkey", build the task, and let the VTC decide. The sign dialog
repeats the notice and uses the same bound step-up flow as break-glass (refused
until the passkey gesture, then the identical document is resent). A
`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` refusal under the mode explains that somebody else
could make the grant. An accepted answer that carries
`ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived` says so in the toast. `adoptStanding` offers a
self-adopt under the mode and keeps every other check.

Records made under the waiver are listed by `git-ns/view` under
`ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`. The drift read already makes that view call,
so its answer now carries them. The repository's people tables and the member
page's git rights flag each one "self-granted (single-admin)".

With the mode off nothing changes: the client-side block and the break-glass
offer stay as they were.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.5.4` → `0.5.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): live admin console — a hint-only event stream over HTTPS (binding 0.3 streamed responses)
body:
UX2: the admin console is told *when* to re-read, over one live channel per session, instead of polling every read on a timer. It implements `vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.1` and `vtc/admin/events/event/0.1` (trust-tasks-rs 0.27.2 generated types), carried as an **HTTPS binding 0.3 §2.1 streamed response** on the existing `POST /v1/trust-tasks` door. No new route.

### Wire
- The signed subscribe goes with `Accept: text/event-stream, application/json;q=0.5`. The door runs the whole spine first, so any refusal is the ordinary JSON `trust-task-error` and **opens no stream**. Only a success answers `200 text/event-stream` (`Cache-Control: no-store`), and the signed `#response` is its first event.
- Each event carries one complete document on one `data:` line, with no `event:` field. The SSE `id` is the resume token, and heartbeats are `: heartbeat` comments.
- After the `#response` the stream carries only hints and heartbeats, never a `trust-task-error`. It ends without a reason.
- Resumption is in-band only, through `since`. `Last-Event-ID` is a cross-check: if it disagrees with `since`, the subscribe is refused `malformedRequest`. An unknown, foreign or expired `since` opens with `resumed: false`, never an error.

### The hints-only rule
A hint carries `topic`, `at`, `resumeToken`, and `count` on actions, acknowledgements and joinRequests. It never carries a record, an id or a DID. The integration tests assert the shape of every hint the VTC sends. The console reacts only by invalidating the react-query keys of that topic's own signed read.

### VTC (`src/admin_events`, `trust_tasks/event_tasks.rs`)
- **Bus:** a broadcast fed from the storage seams: action save/delete, join-request store/delete, member store/delete, ACL store/delete, config overrides and the community profile.
- **Effective topics:** requested ∩ readable. A topic is readable exactly when the community would answer its read: one gate table (`admin_events::read_capability`) that the `members/list`, `join-requests/list` and `config/export` handlers gate on too. Today `config` needs `vtc.config.admin` (as `config/export` does) and every other topic goes to any administrator. Standing is re-checked on every ACL change, before every hint and once per heartbeat. If the readable topics shrink, the stream ends.
- **Hint suppression:** a per-recipient digest means a change the caller's read would not show sends no hint. Hints are limited to one per topic per second.
- **Stream end:** the stream also ends when the client goes, at shutdown, when the signer's ACL entry, the console-key delegation or the document's `expiresAt` lapses, after an hour, or when a write stalls for 2× the heartbeat.
- **Caps:** 5 concurrent streams per administrator and 256 in all, then `tooManyStreams` (retryable). The defaults are 25 s heartbeat and 10 min / 4096 changes of resume history. All are documented.
- **Freshness and replay:** the subscribe has a 5-minute `issuedAt` window. Its response is never recorded for redelivery, so a replayed subscribe gets `204` and opens nothing.
- **Signing:** hints are signed with the VTC key. No lock is held across an await (R1.3).

### Console
- One subscription per session, read with streaming `fetch`. It reconnects with a freshly signed subscribe carrying `since`, with exponential backoff and jitter, using `retry:` as the floor. It stops for the session on `streamUnavailable`, `notAdministrator`, `permissionDenied` or `unsupportedType`.
- Hints invalidate:
  - the Actions badge and page;
  - the acknowledgement and single-admin banners;
  - the Join requests badge, page and tile;
  - the Members page and tile;
  - the config screens.
- A **Live / Polling** indicator shows Live only while bytes keep arriving, and goes offline after 2× heartbeat of silence (R6.2). Going offline triggers an immediate re-read.
- Badge and tile polls run every 5 minutes while live and every 60 s otherwise.

### cnm
`cnm actions watch [--topic …] [--json]` prints the hints on a terminal. It works over HTTPS only.

### Censuses
- subscribe is in `DISPATCHED_URIS` and has a conformance witness.
- notAdministrator, streamUnavailable and tooManyStreams have error-code witnesses.
- The console manifest lists subscribe as sent and event as received.
- The OpenAPI document and `wire.ts` are regenerated.
- The trust-tasks-rs floor is raised to 0.27.2.

### Open points
- **Consumer rule 1's bearer cross-check (SHOULD).** The `/v1/trust-tasks` door authenticates by the document's proof alone and reads no bearer token, so the caller is always the proven issuer. That meets the SHOULD's intent: the stream is never opened on a session the proof did not establish.
- **`singleAdminMode` never changes while the process runs.** It is boot configuration, and a restart ends every stream and resumes with `resumed: false`.
- **Rebased onto #1931.** The `joinRequests` hint's count is `vtc/join-requests/list`'s own `totalEstimate` (pending filter, `limit: 1`) — the same read the console's badge and tile make. A request referred for review also raises its join-review queue item, which moves the `actions` topic through the action list's save seam. The console's badge and tile polls (now `limit: 1` reads) keep the live/offline intervals, and hints invalidate their keys.

### What CI must prove
- `Test (workspace)`, `Test (VTC)`. This includes the new `tests/it/admin_events.rs`, which covers: the response first then a hint on an action change, capability filtering, shrink ending the stream, refusals as JSON, replay → 204, unknown and foreign `since`, resume, the heartbeat, credential expiry and the stream cap. It also includes the census, conformance and manifest tests, and `openapi_snapshot`.
- The `Test (VTC admin UI)` job: lint and `wire:check`, plus vitest, including `live-events.test.ts` with a mocked stream.
- `clippy -D warnings`, workspace and `vetting-pcs`, plus fmt.

Run locally:
- After the rebase onto #1931: targeted integration filter (admin_events, action_list, trust_task_manifest, openapi, join_requests, community_verbs, members_crud, admin_config) 236/236. Before it, the full `--test it` run was 986/988; the 2 failures are `routing_modes` tests that fail only because `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` was set.
- vtc-service lib tests filtered to `admin_events`, `admin_actions`, `trust_tasks`, census, conformance and join: 351 passed. The full lib suite was not run locally.
- `cnm-cli`: 120/120 passed.
- vitest: 761/761 passed.
- `npm run lint`, both clippy configurations and fmt: clean.

   - **Event 0.4 `pullRequestOpened`.** Sent for GitHub `pull_request` `opened`/`reopened` on managed repositories. It carries author, actor, draft and fromFork, and never the title, body, branches or diff. The bridge-posted check on the same delivery is unchanged. It is only sent under `event_version = "0.4"`, which is opt-in: the spec forbids sending 0.4 to a VTC that has not listed it in a discovery answer, and this bridge does not send discovery requests. The default stays 0.3.
   - **Job 0.5 `closePullRequest`.** The bridge takes job 0.4 and 0.5 and lists both in discovery. It posts the comment, then closes the PR, idempotently:
     - already closed or merged: `unchanged`, no comment;
     - reopened after `issuedAt` by anyone but the App: `unchanged`;
     - the App's own comment with `<!-- vgi-bridge job:<jobId> -->` already there: the comment step is `unchanged`.
     Forgejo answers `notCapable`.
   - **GitHub App permission.** `pull_requests: write`, the one permission that covers both commenting and closing. Existing installs keep working. Without write, the comment step is `forbidden` and `missingPermissions` lists `pull_requests:write`.
   - **Docs.** BRIDGE.md §3/§6d/§7, RUNBOOK §8f/§8k/§8m, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC, bridge.example.toml.

vta-sdk 0.63 (the latest) and trql-client 0.22 still declare `trust-tasks-rs ^0.26`.
